Option D (Object Lock Governance) protects object versions for 30 days from their creation, not for 30 days after a delete occurs, and users with the bypass permission can still remove versions, so it adds retention management complexity without guaranteeing the required post-deletion recovery window.

stem: A company has an application that uses Amazon Cognito user pools for authentication. The company wants to allow users to sign in using their corporate Active Directory credentials through SAML 2.0 federation. Which configuration enables this?

options.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center with the corporate Active Directory and use OIDC tokens from Identity Center as the authentication mechanism for the Cognito user pool.
Configure the corporate Active Directory as a SAML 2.0 identity provider in the Cognito user pool and map SAML attributes to Cognito user pool attributes for SSO access.
Configure Amazon Cognito identity pools with the corporate Active Directory as an authenticated provider and use IAM roles for attribute mapping and access control.
Deploy AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD in the VPC and configure a trust relationship with the corporate AD to enable pass-through authentication for Cognito users.

explanation: Cognito user pools natively support SAML 2.0 identity providers. Configuring the corporate AD as a SAML IdP allows users to sign in with corporate credentials, with SAML attribute mapping providing user profile information. Option C (Cognito identity pools) provides temporary AWS credentials, not application authentication through SAML. Option D (AWS Managed AD) requires deploying infrastructure and does not directly integrate with Cognito user pools for SAML federation. Option A (IAM Identity Center) is for AWS account/application SSO, not for federating external identity providers into Cognito user pools.

stem: A company has an application that uses an Amazon SQS queue for processing orders. Occasionally, a malformed message causes the processing Lambda function to fail repeatedly. The company wants to prevent these messages from blocking the queue while retaining them for debugging. Which solution should be implemented?

options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) on the source SQS queue with a maximum receive count of 3, so messages that fail processing three times are automatically moved to the DLQ.
Configure the Lambda function with a longer timeout value and implement retry logic within the function code to attempt processing each message up to 5 times before failing.
Configure the SQS queue with a longer visibility timeout and message retention period to allow more time for the Lambda function to successfully process problematic messages.
Configure a CloudWatch alarm that monitors the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric and triggers an SNS notification when messages are stuck in the queue beyond a threshold.

explanation: A dead-letter queue with maxReceiveCount of 3 automatically moves messages that fail processing after 3 attempts, preventing queue blocking while preserving the messages for debugging. Option B (longer timeout with retry) keeps the message in the queue longer and still blocks processing of subsequent messages. Option D (CloudWatch alarm) only alerts about the problem but does not resolve the blocking issue. Option C (longer visibility timeout) delays retry but does not prevent the malformed message from blocking the queue indefinitely.

stem: A company needs to migrate a 500 GB on-premises MySQL database to Amazon Aurora MySQL with minimal downtime. The database handles 5,000 transactions per second during business hours. Which migration strategy minimizes application downtime?

options.text: Set up MySQL native replication from the on-premises database to an EC2-based MySQL instance, then promote the EC2 instance and migrate to Aurora using snapshot restore.
Use AWS Application Migration Service to replicate the entire database server to an EC2 instance in AWS, then perform an in-place upgrade to convert the EC2 database to Aurora.
Create a mysqldump export of the entire database, upload the dump file to S3, and import it into Aurora MySQL using the S3 import feature before switching the application endpoint.
Use AWS DMS with a full load plus change data capture (CDC) task to replicate data continuously from the source MySQL to Aurora MySQL and cut over during a brief maintenance window.

explanation: DMS with full load plus CDC performs initial data migration while continuously replicating changes. The application experiences downtime only during the brief cutover when the application endpoint switches to Aurora. Option C (mysqldump) requires database downtime during the entire export/import process for a 500 GB database. Option A (native replication to EC2) adds an intermediate step and the EC2 to Aurora migration requires additional downtime. Option B (Application Migration Service) migrates entire servers, not databases, and does not provide in-place Aurora conversion.

stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application serves traffic from 6 AM to midnight with peak usage between 9 AM and 5 PM. Minimum capacity is 4 instances and peak capacity is 20 instances. Which purchasing combination optimizes cost?

options.text: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for the equivalent of 4 instances running 24/7, and use On-Demand Instances for the additional capacity that scales between 4 and 20 instances.
Purchase Reserved Instances for 20 instances to cover peak capacity and use Auto Scaling to adjust the running count, ensuring all instances benefit from reserved pricing.
Use all On-Demand Instances with Auto Scaling configured to scale between 4 and 20 instances based on CPU utilization to maintain full flexibility without long-term commitments.
Use all Spot Instances with a Spot Fleet diversified across multiple instance types and Availability Zones, accepting occasional interruptions for maximum cost savings.

explanation: Savings Plan for the baseline 4 instances provides significant savings on the always-running capacity. On-Demand handles the variable portion (4-20 instances) with full flexibility. This balances commitment savings with elasticity. Option B (20 RIs) wastes money on 16 reserved instances that are only used during peak hours. Option C (all On-Demand) is the most expensive option for baseline capacity. Option D (all Spot) risks interruption for a production web application, causing user-facing outages.

stem: A company is deploying an application that processes credit card payments. PCI DSS compliance requires that cardholder data is tokenized before storage and that the tokenization service is isolated from the rest of the application. Which architecture meets this compliance requirement?

options.text: Deploy the tokenization service in the same VPC as the application but in a dedicated private subnet with a security group that allows inbound traffic only from the application tier.
Deploy the tokenization service as a Lambda function inside the application VPC private subnets, invoked directly by the application tier using standard Lambda function invocation.
Deploy the tokenization service on the same EC2 instances as the application but in a separate Docker container with application-level network isolation using container networking.
Deploy the tokenization service in a separate VPC with VPC peering to the application VPC, using security groups and NACLs to restrict traffic to only the tokenization API endpoint.

explanation: A separate VPC places the tokenization service in its own network boundary, and VPC peering with tightly scoped security groups and NACLs restricts connectivity to only the tokenization API, satisfying the PCI DSS requirement to segment the cardholder data environment from the rest of the application. Option A (same VPC, dedicated subnet) keeps the service inside the application's network boundary, so it is segmented by subnet only and not isolated from the rest of the application as required. Option B (Lambda in application VPC subnets) places the tokenization function in the same network segment as the application, providing no segmentation of the cardholder data environment. Option C (container on shared EC2 instances) relies on container-level separation on shared hosts, which does not provide the network-level isolation PCI DSS segmentation requires.

stem: A company is designing a highly available architecture for a web application. The application must remain available even if an entire Availability Zone fails. Which TWO components should the solutions architect include in the design? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Deploy EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group spanning at least two Availability Zones with a minimum capacity that allows the application to run with one AZ unavailable.
Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of the Application Load Balancer to cache responses at edge locations and serve cached content if the origin becomes unavailable.
Deploy EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone with an Auto Scaling group configured to rapidly replace failed instances and restore capacity within five minutes.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer with cross-zone load balancing enabled and health checks configured to detect unhealthy instances and route traffic to healthy targets.

explanation: An ALB distributes traffic across AZs and health checks ensure traffic only goes to healthy instances. An Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs maintains capacity even when one AZ is lost by launching replacement instances in surviving AZs. Option C (single AZ) does not survive an AZ failure. Option B (CloudFront caching) only helps for cached content and cannot serve dynamic requests if the origin fails.

stem: A company is building a search feature for an e-commerce website. The search must support full-text search, fuzzy matching, autocomplete suggestions, and faceted filtering across millions of product listings. Which AWS service should power the search functionality?

options.text: Use Amazon OpenSearch Service with a multi-node cluster configured for full-text indexing, fuzzy matching, autocomplete suggesters, and faceted aggregation queries.
Use Amazon CloudSearch with a multi-AZ search domain configured for automatic scaling, full-text search, and faceted filtering across the product catalog dataset.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with a Global Secondary Index on the product name field and filter expressions to implement search, fuzzy matching, and faceted filtering queries.
Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the pg_trgm extension for fuzzy matching, full-text search indexes, and materialized views for pre-computed faceted filter counts.

explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service provides enterprise-grade full-text search with built-in support for fuzzy matching, autocomplete suggesters, faceted aggregations, and scales to millions of documents. Option C (DynamoDB) is designed for key-value lookups and does not support full-text search, fuzzy matching, or efficient faceted filtering. Option D (PostgreSQL) can handle basic search but does not scale well for millions of products with complex search features. Option B (CloudSearch) is a legacy service with limited features compared to OpenSearch and is not actively developed.

stem: A company has a data lake in Amazon S3 containing 100 TB of data in CSV format. Data scientists query the data using Amazon Athena but complain about slow queries and high costs. The data is queried frequently on the 'customer_id' and 'transaction_date' columns. Which combination of changes provides the MOST improvement?

options.text: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the data bucket and configure Athena query result reuse to cache previous query results for faster repeated query execution.
Convert CSV files to Apache Parquet format with Snappy compression and partition the data by transaction_date to reduce data scanned per query significantly.
Migrate all data from S3 to Amazon Redshift Serverless and run queries using Redshift SQL instead of Athena to leverage the columnar storage and query optimization.
Increase the number of S3 buckets to distribute the data across multiple locations and enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to speed up data access for Athena queries.

explanation: Converting to Parquet provides columnar storage (Athena reads only needed columns) and Snappy compression reduces file sizes. Partitioning by transaction_date allows Athena to skip irrelevant data. Combined, these can reduce data scanned by 90%+, cutting both cost and time. Option D (more buckets with Transfer Acceleration) does not reduce data scanned and Transfer Acceleration is for uploads. Option C (Redshift migration) adds significant cost and operational overhead. Option A (Intelligent-Tiering with query reuse) does not reduce the amount of data scanned per query.

stem: A company hosts a public-facing web application on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company wants to protect the application from common web exploits including cross-site scripting (XSS), SQL injection, and HTTP flood attacks. Which solution provides comprehensive protection?

options.text: Enable AWS Shield Standard on the ALB for DDoS protection and configure security group rules to limit the number of concurrent connections per source IP address.
Attach AWS WAF to the ALB with AWS Managed Rules for the Core Rule Set (CRS), SQL Database rule group, and a rate-based rule to protect against XSS, SQLi, and HTTP floods.
Configure the ALB with an HTTPS listener using a strict SSL policy and enable access logging to S3 for post-incident analysis of web exploit attempts in the logs.
Deploy Amazon GuardDuty with EKS Runtime Monitoring to detect web exploit attempts and configure automated remediation through Lambda to block offending IP addresses.

explanation: AWS WAF with Managed Rules provides real-time protection against XSS, SQL injection (via specific rule groups), and HTTP floods (via rate-based rules) at the ALB level. Option A (Shield Standard with security groups) protects against DDoS but security groups cannot inspect HTTP content for XSS or SQLi. Option D (GuardDuty) is a threat detection service, not a web application firewall, and does not block web exploits in real-time. Option C (HTTPS with logging) encrypts traffic and enables analysis but does not block exploit attempts.

stem: A company uses AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by Amazon API Gateway. During peak traffic, some Lambda invocations fail with 'TooManyRequestsException' errors due to concurrent execution limits. The company needs to handle these bursts without dropping requests. Which solution addresses this issue?

options.text: Configure API Gateway with request throttling and a usage plan that limits the request rate to match the Lambda concurrency limit, returning HTTP 429 to excess requests.
Configure Lambda reserved concurrency for the function at a value equal to the maximum expected concurrent invocations to guarantee capacity allocation during peak traffic.
Request a Lambda concurrency limit increase through AWS Service Quotas and configure provisioned concurrency for the function to handle the expected peak invocation rate.
Add an Amazon SQS queue between API Gateway and Lambda using Lambda event source mapping to buffer requests and process them within the Lambda concurrency limit.

explanation: Increasing the Lambda concurrency limit allows more simultaneous executions during peak traffic. Provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments warm, reducing cold starts and ensuring consistent performance. Option A (API throttling) drops excess requests rather than handling them. Option D (SQS buffering) makes the API asynchronous, which changes the user experience for synchronous API calls. Option B (reserved concurrency) guarantees capacity for this function but limits the account's available concurrency for other functions without increasing the total limit.

stem: A company needs a message broker that supports MQTT and WebSocket protocols for IoT device communication. Millions of devices send telemetry data that must be routed to different backend services based on message topics. Which AWS service should be used?

options.text: Use AWS IoT Core with message routing rules that filter messages by topic and forward them to different backend services including Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, and Kinesis.
Use Amazon SNS with topic-based filtering and a WebSocket-compatible API Gateway to receive device messages and fan out to multiple SQS queues for backend service consumption.
Use Amazon MQ with an ActiveMQ broker configured for MQTT protocol support and message topic-based routing to distribute messages to different consumer queue destinations.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with custom MQTT bridge deployed on EC2 to translate MQTT messages into Kinesis records partitioned by device topic for backend processing.

explanation: AWS IoT Core natively supports MQTT and WebSocket protocols, scales to millions of devices, and provides a rules engine that routes messages to different AWS services based on topic patterns. Option C (Amazon MQ) supports MQTT but is not designed for millions of concurrent IoT connections and lacks native integration with AWS services. Option D (Kinesis with MQTT bridge) requires managing custom MQTT translation infrastructure. Option B (SNS with API Gateway) does not natively support MQTT protocol and requires custom device firmware changes.

stem: A company runs a containerized application on Amazon ECS with EC2 launch type using 10 m5.xlarge instances running 24/7. The containers use only 40% of the total CPU and memory capacity on average. The company wants to reduce compute costs without changing the application. Which optimization should be implemented?

options.text: Switch from EC2 launch type to Fargate launch type to pay only for the CPU and memory each container task actually requests rather than paying for full EC2 instance capacity.
Enable ECS cluster auto scaling with capacity providers to right-size the number of EC2 instances based on actual container resource reservations across the cluster.
Configure ECS service auto scaling to reduce the number of running tasks during low-usage periods and increase task count during peak periods based on CPU metrics.
Replace the 10 m5.xlarge instances with 5 m5.2xlarge instances to consolidate workloads onto fewer, larger instances with better price-performance ratio and lower overhead.

explanation: ECS cluster auto scaling with capacity providers automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances to match actual container resource reservations, eliminating the 60% unused capacity. This directly reduces the number of running instances. Option A (Fargate) may cost more than right-sized EC2 instances for 24/7 workloads and changes the infrastructure model. Option D (fewer larger instances) still maintains the same total capacity and does not address the 60% underutilization. Option C (service auto scaling) adjusts task count but the fixed 10 instances still run regardless of task count.

stem: A company needs to migrate an on-premises application to AWS. The application accesses a file share using the NFS protocol. The company wants to maintain on-premises access to the files during the migration while gradually moving data to Amazon S3. Which service facilitates this hybrid storage approach?

options.text: Deploy Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with a hybrid deployment configuration to provide NFS access both on-premises and in AWS with automatic data tiering to S3 storage.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway on-premises to provide an NFS mount point backed by Amazon S3, with a local cache for frequently accessed files during migration.
Deploy AWS DataSync agents on-premises to continuously synchronize the NFS file share to Amazon S3, with the application continuing to access files through the local NFS share.
Deploy AWS Transfer Family with an NFS endpoint in the VPC and configure a VPN connection from on-premises to allow the application to mount the Transfer Family NFS share.

explanation: Storage Gateway File Gateway provides an NFS mount point on-premises that transparently stores data in S3. The local cache ensures low-latency access to frequently used files while data gradually moves to S3. Option C (DataSync) synchronizes data but does not provide a transparent NFS interface backed by S3. Option A (FSx for NetApp ONTAP) is a managed file system but does not provide a simple on-premises NFS gateway to S3. Option D (Transfer Family) is for SFTP/FTP/FTPS file transfers, not NFS mount points.

stem: A company deploys a web application using Amazon CloudFormation. The deployment occasionally fails due to dependency issues between resources. The company wants to ensure that if a deployment fails, all resources are rolled back to the previous working state. Which CloudFormation feature provides this protection?

options.text: Enable CloudFormation stack termination protection to prevent accidental deletion and configure drift detection to identify resources that have changed outside of CloudFormation.
Enable CloudFormation stack rollback on failure with the --disable-rollback flag set to false, ensuring automatic rollback to the last known good state when stack operations fail.
Configure CloudFormation stack policy that prevents updates to critical resources and use the DependsOn attribute in templates to define explicit dependency ordering between resources.
Configure CloudFormation change sets to preview all resource changes before execution and manually approve only the changes that will succeed based on the change set preview.

explanation: CloudFormation automatic rollback on failure (enabled by default) reverts all resources to the previous state when a stack create or update fails, ensuring the application returns to a working state. Option D (change sets) allows previewing changes but does not guarantee success or provide automatic rollback. Option A (termination protection and drift detection) prevents deletion and detects drift but does not handle deployment failure rollback. Option C (stack policy with DependsOn) controls which resources can be updated and ordering but does not provide rollback on failure.

stem: A company builds a real-time leaderboard for a mobile game with millions of concurrent players. The leaderboard must update within 100 milliseconds of a score change and support queries for top-N players and a player's rank. Which data store is BEST suited?

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with sorted sets to store player scores, using ZADD for score updates and ZREVRANGE/ZRANK for top-N and rank queries with sub-millisecond latency.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with a Global Secondary Index on the score attribute and query with ScanIndexForward set to false to retrieve top-N players sorted by highest score.
Use Amazon Neptune graph database to model player-score relationships as vertices and edges, using Gremlin traversal queries to find top-scoring players and rank positions.
Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with an index on the score column and use SQL ORDER BY queries with LIMIT to retrieve top-N players and subqueries to calculate individual player ranks.

explanation: Redis sorted sets are purpose-built for leaderboard use cases, providing O(log N) score updates (ZADD), O(log N + M) top-N queries (ZREVRANGE), and O(log N) rank queries (ZRANK) with sub-millisecond latency. Option B (DynamoDB GSI) does not efficiently support rank queries and scanning a GSI for top-N is slow with millions of items. Option D (Aurora MySQL) cannot provide 100ms updates at millions of concurrent players due to write locking and query overhead. Option C (Neptune) is designed for relationship traversal, not sorted-set operations like leaderboards.

stem: A company uses Amazon CloudWatch to monitor its AWS infrastructure. The company has 500 EC2 instances with detailed monitoring enabled, 200 custom metrics, and 50 CloudWatch dashboards. Monthly CloudWatch costs are higher than expected. Which action provides the MOST cost reduction?

options.text: Replace custom CloudWatch metrics with the CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) to publish metrics as structured log events that are automatically extracted as metrics.
Switch from detailed monitoring (1-minute intervals) to basic monitoring (5-minute intervals) on non-critical EC2 instances to reduce the number of metric data points collected.
Consolidate the 50 CloudWatch dashboards into 10 dashboards using multiple widgets per dashboard to reduce the per-dashboard monthly charge while maintaining visibility.
Migrate from CloudWatch to a self-managed Prometheus and Grafana stack on EC2 instances to eliminate CloudWatch charges while maintaining equivalent monitoring capabilities.

explanation: Detailed monitoring generates metrics every 1 minute vs. basic monitoring every 5 minutes, creating 5x more data points. Switching non-critical instances to basic monitoring significantly reduces metric costs for 500 instances. Option C (dashboard consolidation) saves on dashboard charges but dashboards are $3/month each, which is relatively small compared to metrics costs. Option A (EMF) does not reduce metric costs since extracted metrics are billed the same as custom metrics. Option D (self-managed Prometheus) requires managing infrastructure and may cost more when including EC2 and operational overhead.

stem: A company has a microservices application where services communicate over HTTPS within a VPC. The company needs to issue and manage TLS certificates for internal service-to-service communication without using publicly trusted certificates. Which solution provides this capability?

options.text: Deploy an OpenSSL-based certificate authority on an EC2 instance to generate self-signed certificates for internal services and distribute them through Systems Manager Parameter Store.
Use AWS Certificate Manager Private CA to create a private certificate authority and issue private TLS certificates for internal services with automated certificate renewal.
Use AWS Secrets Manager to generate and store TLS certificates for internal services with automatic rotation configured to renew certificates before their expiration date.
Use AWS Certificate Manager to provision public TLS certificates for internal service domain names and attach them to the internal Application Load Balancer listeners.

explanation: ACM Private CA creates a private certificate authority for issuing private TLS certificates for internal service communication. It provides automated renewal and integrates with AWS services. Option D (ACM public certificates) requires public domain validation and is not designed for internal private service names. Option A (OpenSSL on EC2) requires managing the CA infrastructure and manual certificate distribution. Option C (Secrets Manager) stores secrets but does not act as a certificate authority or manage TLS certificate lifecycle.

stem: A company runs a stateful web application where each user session maintains an active WebSocket connection to a specific backend server. The application runs on EC2 instances behind a load balancer. The company needs the load balancer to maintain WebSocket connections to the same backend instance. Which load balancer type should be used?

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions enabled using duration-based cookies to maintain client affinity to the same backend instance for WebSocket connections.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer with a Lambda target group that manages WebSocket connection state in DynamoDB and routes requests to the appropriate backend instance.
Deploy a Network Load Balancer with TCP listeners to maintain long-lived WebSocket connections through TCP-level connection tracking to the same backend instance.
Deploy a Classic Load Balancer with TCP listeners configured for WebSocket protocol support and connection draining enabled to gracefully handle instance deregistration.

explanation: Application Load Balancer natively supports WebSocket connections and sticky sessions ensure that all messages from a client are routed to the same backend instance maintaining the WebSocket state. Option C (NLB with TCP) maintains connections at the TCP level but does not provide application-layer sticky sessions for reconnection scenarios. Option D (Classic Load Balancer) is legacy and does not support WebSocket protocol natively. Option B (ALB with Lambda) adds unnecessary complexity and Lambda cannot maintain persistent WebSocket connections.

stem: A company needs to store and retrieve 500 million user profile objects, each approximately 4 KB in size. The access pattern is simple key-value lookups by user ID with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale. Which database provides the BEST fit?

options.text: Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with the user ID as the primary key index and connection pooling through RDS Proxy to handle high-concurrency key-value lookup queries.
Use Amazon DocumentDB with the user ID as the document key to provide MongoDB-compatible JSON document storage with single-digit millisecond read performance.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity mode and the user ID as the partition key to provide consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale.
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with cluster mode enabled and the user ID as the key to provide sub-millisecond in-memory access for all 500 million user profiles.

explanation: DynamoDB is designed for key-value lookups at any scale with consistent single-digit millisecond performance. On-demand mode handles variable traffic without capacity planning. 500 million 4 KB items (2 TB total) is well within DynamoDB's capabilities. Option A (Aurora) can handle the data but may not provide consistent single-digit millisecond latency under high concurrency for simple key-value lookups. Option D (ElastiCache) would require 2 TB of RAM which is extremely expensive for persistent data storage. Option B (DocumentDB) is designed for document queries, which is overkill for simple key-value lookups.

stem: A company needs to deploy a web application in a VPC that requires both IPv4 and IPv6 support. External users will connect via IPv6 and the application must communicate with backend services using IPv4. Which VPC configuration supports this dual-stack requirement?

options.text: Create an IPv6-only VPC with a NAT64 gateway for IPv4 communication and configure the ALB to accept IPv6 connections from external users and translate to IPv4 for backends.
Create a dual-stack VPC and deploy separate ALBs for IPv4 and IPv6 traffic, using Route 53 to route AAAA records to the IPv6 ALB and A records to the IPv4 ALB.
Create a dual-stack VPC with both IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR blocks, configure subnets with dual-stack addressing, and use an ALB with dual-stack listeners for client connections.
Create an IPv4-only VPC and deploy Amazon CloudFront with IPv6 enabled to accept IPv6 connections at the edge and forward requests to the IPv4 ALB origin in the VPC.

explanation: A dual-stack VPC with both IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR blocks supports both protocols natively. ALBs with dual-stack listeners accept IPv6 from external users and communicate with IPv4 backend targets. Option A (IPv6-only with NAT64) requires additional NAT64 infrastructure and is not the standard dual-stack approach. Option D (CloudFront with IPv6) adds a CDN layer when the requirement is for direct VPC dual-stack support. Option B (separate ALBs) unnecessarily duplicates infrastructure when a single ALB supports dual-stack.

stem: A company is building a workflow that processes insurance claims. Each claim goes through several steps: validation, assessment, approval, and payment. Some steps require human review and may take days to complete. Which service should orchestrate this workflow?

options.text: Use Amazon SQS with separate queues for each processing step and Lambda functions that move claims between queues as each step completes including human review notifications.
Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to trigger each processing step on a schedule and use DynamoDB to track claim state across the validation, assessment, approval, and payment steps.
Use AWS Step Functions with Standard Workflows to orchestrate the multi-step claim processing with wait states for human review tasks and automatic state management.
Use AWS Lambda orchestration with one function calling the next function in sequence, using DynamoDB to store workflow state and SNS to notify human reviewers when needed.

explanation: Step Functions Standard Workflows support long-running processes (up to 1 year), wait states for human review tasks, built-in state management, error handling, and visual workflow monitoring. Option A (SQS queues) requires building custom workflow state management and tracking across multiple queues. Option B (EventBridge Scheduler) is designed for scheduled events, not dynamic multi-step workflows with human interaction. Option D (Lambda orchestration) has timeout limitations and requires building custom state management in DynamoDB.

stem: A company has an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster with 6 cache.r5.xlarge nodes. CloudWatch metrics show that memory utilization is consistently below 30% and CPU utilization is below 20%. The cluster handles 50,000 requests per second. Which optimization reduces costs?

options.text: Switch to ElastiCache Serverless for Redis which automatically scales capacity based on workload demand and eliminates the need to provision and manage specific node types.
Reduce the number of nodes from 6 to 3 by reconfiguring the cluster with fewer shards, maintaining the same instance type for each remaining node in the cluster.
Purchase Reserved Nodes for the 6 cache.r5.xlarge instances with a 1-year All Upfront commitment to receive up to 50% discount on the current cluster configuration.
Right-size the cluster by switching to cache.r5.large nodes, which provide half the memory and compute at a lower hourly cost while still accommodating the observed utilization.

explanation: With under 30% memory and 20% CPU, the nodes are over-provisioned. Switching to cache.r5.large (half the size) reduces per-node cost while still leaving significant headroom for the workload. Option B (fewer nodes) may impact availability and data distribution across fewer shards. Option A (ElastiCache Serverless) may have higher per-request costs than right-sized provisioned nodes for a consistent 50K req/sec workload. Option C (Reserved Nodes) saves money but on the existing oversized infrastructure, wasting capacity.

stem: A company deploys Lambda functions that need to access resources in a VPC (RDS database and ElastiCache cluster). The Lambda functions must also access the internet to call external APIs. Which VPC configuration allows both VPC resource access and internet access for Lambda?

options.text: Configure Lambda in the VPC private subnets and deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet to provide internet access while maintaining private connectivity to RDS and ElastiCache.
Configure Lambda in the VPC private subnets and attach an Internet Gateway route to the private subnet route table to enable both VPC resource access and internet connectivity.
Configure Lambda outside the VPC for internet access and create VPC interface endpoints for RDS and ElastiCache to allow Lambda to connect to the VPC resources privately.
Configure Lambda in the VPC public subnets with auto-assigned public IP addresses to provide direct internet access and use security groups for RDS and ElastiCache connectivity.

explanation: Lambda functions attached to private subnets reach RDS and ElastiCache through their VPC ENIs, and a route to a NAT Gateway in a public subnet gives them outbound internet access for external API calls. Option B (Internet Gateway route in private subnets) does not work: Lambda ENIs never receive public IP addresses, so return traffic through an IGW cannot reach them, and the route would also make the subnets public. Option C (Lambda outside the VPC) does not work: interface endpoints are only reachable from inside a VPC, so a non-VPC Lambda function cannot connect to RDS or ElastiCache instances in private subnets. Option D (Lambda in public subnets) does not work because VPC-configured Lambda ENIs are never assigned public IPs, so even in a public subnet the functions have no internet path.

stem: A company runs an application that requires a relational database with automatic storage scaling, up to 15 read replicas, and the ability to clone the entire database in minutes for testing. Which database service provides all of these capabilities?

options.text: Amazon Aurora MySQL with automatic storage scaling up to 128 TB, up to 15 Aurora read replicas across multiple AZs, and fast database cloning using copy-on-write technology.
Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled, storage auto scaling configured, and read replicas deployed across multiple Availability Zones for read scaling and availability.
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with Provisioned IOPS storage auto scaling, cross-Region read replicas for global read distribution, and automated snapshots for database cloning.
Amazon Redshift Serverless with automatic scaling of compute and storage, data sharing across multiple clusters for read distribution, and snapshot-based cluster cloning.

explanation: Aurora MySQL scales storage automatically up to 128 TB, supports up to 15 Aurora replicas that share the same storage volume, and its fast cloning feature uses copy-on-write to create a full database clone in minutes without duplicating storage. Option B (RDS for MySQL) now supports up to 15 read replicas, but each replica maintains its own storage copy and cloning requires a snapshot restore that takes far longer than minutes for a large database. Option C (RDS for PostgreSQL) likewise supports up to 15 read replicas but has no fast copy-on-write cloning — automated snapshots must be fully restored to new storage. Option D (Redshift Serverless) is a data warehouse for analytics workloads, not a general-purpose relational database for the application.

stem: A company is deploying a machine learning training workload that requires multiple GPU instances to work together with high-bandwidth, low-latency interconnects. The training job processes a 50 TB dataset stored in Amazon S3. Which compute configuration maximizes training performance?

options.text: Launch inf1.24xlarge Inferentia instances in a cluster placement group with high-bandwidth networking and Amazon EFS for shared access to the training dataset.
Launch g4dn.12xlarge instances in an Auto Scaling group with GP3 EBS volumes and configure the training framework to download data from S3 to local instance storage.
Launch p4d.24xlarge instances in a cluster placement group with Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) enabled and use FSx for Lustre linked to S3 for high-throughput data access.
Launch p3.16xlarge instances in a spread placement group with enhanced networking enabled and use S3 direct access with multi-part downloads for training data loading.

explanation: p4d.24xlarge instances provide 8 A100 GPUs with 600 Gbps networking. Cluster placement groups minimize inter-node latency. EFA enables GPU-direct communication for distributed training. FSx for Lustre provides high-throughput parallel access to the S3 dataset. Option D (p3 in spread placement) increases latency between nodes and S3 direct access is slower than FSx for Lustre for large datasets. Option B (g4dn with EBS) uses inference-optimized GPUs and EBS is slower than FSx for Lustre for ML training. Option A (Inferentia instances) are designed for inference workloads, not training.

stem: A company deploys a serverless application using API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB. The application receives 1 million requests per day with an average Lambda execution time of 500ms at 256 MB. The company wants to understand and optimize costs across all three services. Which tool provides the BEST cost visibility?

options.text: Use AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks to identify underutilized Lambda functions and over-provisioned DynamoDB tables with recommendations for right-sizing.
Use the AWS Pricing Calculator to model the expected costs for the current workload configuration and compare against alternative architectures for cost optimization.
Use AWS Budgets with service-level budgets for API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB to set spending alerts and track actual costs against planned budgets for each service.
Use AWS Cost Explorer with resource-level granularity and filtering by service to analyze costs for API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB individually and identify optimization opportunities.

explanation: Cost Explorer provides detailed cost analysis with filtering by service, resource, and time period. Resource-level granularity shows exactly where money is spent across API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB. Option C (Budgets) tracks spending against budgets but does not provide the analytical depth for cost optimization. Option A (Trusted Advisor) has limited serverless-specific checks and does not provide resource-level cost analysis. Option B (Pricing Calculator) estimates costs for new configurations but does not analyze actual usage costs.

stem: A company needs to configure DNS for a new application hosted on AWS. The application uses an Application Load Balancer. The company wants the domain name to point to the ALB with minimal DNS management and automatic failover between ALB IP addresses. Which Route 53 record type should be used?

options.text: Create a Route 53 CNAME record pointing to the ALB DNS name, which redirects DNS queries to the ALB's hostname for resolution by the ALB's own DNS infrastructure.
Create a Route 53 alias A record pointing to the ALB DNS name, which automatically resolves to the ALB's current IP addresses and benefits from Route 53's free alias queries.
Create a Route 53 A record with the ALB's static Elastic IP address, which provides a fixed IP that does not change when the ALB scales or replaces underlying resources.
Create a Route 53 SRV record pointing to the ALB with port and weight parameters specified, which enables service discovery and load distribution at the DNS level.

explanation: Route 53 alias A records natively integrate with AWS resources like ALBs, automatically tracking IP address changes without manual updates. Alias queries to AWS resources are free. Option A (CNAME) cannot be used at the zone apex and incurs standard query charges. Option C (A record with static IP) is not possible because ALBs do not support Elastic IP addresses. Option D (SRV record) is used for service discovery protocols, not standard web application DNS.

stem: A company needs to run a batch of 10,000 independent tasks, each taking 20-40 minutes. The tasks are CPU-intensive and the company wants the FASTEST completion time with minimal infrastructure management. Which compute service should be used?

options.text: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with a launch template and a desired capacity of 100 instances, processing tasks from an SQS queue using a custom worker application.
Use Amazon ECS with EC2 launch type and a cluster with capacity providers configured to scale the number of container instances based on pending task count.
Use AWS Batch with a managed compute environment and Fargate platform to automatically provision containers for each task without managing underlying EC2 infrastructure.
Use AWS Lambda with concurrent invocations for each task, configuring the function with maximum memory allocation and a 15-minute timeout for CPU-intensive processing.

explanation: AWS Batch with a Fargate compute environment automatically provisions a container for each job, handles scheduling, retries, and massive parallel execution of the 10,000 tasks with no servers or clusters to manage. Option A (EC2 Auto Scaling with SQS) requires building and operating a custom worker application, queue-polling logic, and scaling configuration. Option B (ECS on EC2) requires managing container instances, instance types, and capacity providers. Option D (Lambda) cannot run these tasks because the 20-40 minute execution time exceeds Lambda's maximum timeout of 15 minutes.

stem: A company needs to implement a caching strategy for a REST API. The API returns product data that changes approximately every 10 minutes. Some endpoints return user-specific data that should not be cached. Which caching architecture handles both scenarios?

options.text: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the DynamoDB table with a 10-minute item cache TTL to cache product reads and bypass the cache for user-specific queries.
Deploy Amazon API Gateway caching on the REST API stage with a 600-second cache TTL configured globally and per-method cache invalidation for user-specific endpoint methods.
Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of the API with a 10-minute TTL for product data endpoints and the Cache-Control no-store header configured for user-specific endpoints.
Deploy Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the API and the database with 10-minute TTL for product cache keys and no caching for user-specific queries identified by user ID.

explanation: CloudFront with per-behavior TTL settings handles both scenarios: product endpoints get a 10-minute cache at edge locations for global performance, while user-specific endpoints use no-store to bypass caching. Option D (ElastiCache) caches at the application layer but does not reduce latency for globally distributed users like an edge cache. Option B (API Gateway caching) caches at the API level but has limited cache capacity and does not provide edge caching. Option A (DAX) only works with DynamoDB and cannot selectively bypass caching for specific API endpoints.

stem: A company processes log files stored in Amazon S3. The processing application runs on EC2 instances that download files from S3, process them, and upload results back to S3. The instances are in the same Region as the S3 bucket. Data transfer costs are unexpectedly high. What is the MOST likely cause and solution?

options.text: The EC2 instances are in a different Availability Zone than the S3 endpoint, incurring cross-AZ data transfer fees. The solution is to move instances to the same AZ as the S3 endpoint.
The EC2 instances are accessing S3 through a NAT Gateway, incurring data processing charges. The solution is to create an S3 VPC gateway endpoint for free private S3 access.
The S3 bucket has Requester Pays enabled, charging the EC2 instance account for data transfer. The solution is to disable Requester Pays and use standard S3 data transfer pricing.
The S3 bucket has Transfer Acceleration enabled, adding per-GB transfer charges. The solution is to disable Transfer Acceleration since the instances are in the same Region as the bucket.

explanation: NAT Gateway charges $0.045 per GB processed, which adds up significantly for large log file transfers. An S3 VPC gateway endpoint routes S3 traffic for free through the AWS private network, eliminating NAT Gateway data processing charges. Option D (Transfer Acceleration) is unlikely to be enabled for same-Region access and charges are clearly labeled separately. Option A (cross-AZ) does not apply to S3 access since S3 is a Regional service. Option C (Requester Pays) does not cause unexpected charges when both the bucket and instances are in the same account.

stem: A company needs to implement a comprehensive data encryption strategy for an application that uses Amazon RDS, Amazon S3, and Amazon EBS. Which TWO actions ensure encryption at rest for all three services? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Deploy AWS CloudHSM and configure all three services to use CloudHSM-backed custom key stores for maximum control over the hardware security modules managing encryption keys.
Enable encryption on RDS instances using AWS KMS and enable EBS encryption by default in the account settings to encrypt all new EBS volumes with a KMS key automatically.
Configure VPC endpoints for S3, RDS, and EBS to ensure that all data transfers between services occur over encrypted AWS PrivateLink connections within the VPC.
Enable default encryption on S3 buckets using SSE-KMS with a customer managed key and configure the bucket policy to deny uploads without server-side encryption headers.

explanation: S3 bucket default encryption with SSE-KMS ensures all objects are encrypted at rest. RDS encryption with KMS encrypts database storage, and EBS encryption by default ensures all new volumes are automatically encrypted. Together these cover all three services. Option C (VPC endpoints) provides private connectivity but does not encrypt data at rest. Option A (CloudHSM) provides stronger key management but adds significant cost and complexity for standard encryption-at-rest requirements.

stem: A company needs to design a message processing system where each message must be processed by exactly one consumer from a group of consumers. Messages should be load-balanced across the consumer group, and if a consumer fails, its messages should be reprocessed by another consumer. Which architecture meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use Amazon SNS with an SQS queue subscription for each consumer, where each consumer gets its own queue containing a copy of every published message for processing.
Use Amazon MQ with a RabbitMQ broker and a work queue pattern where the broker distributes messages round-robin to consumers and requeues messages from failed consumers.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Enhanced Fan-Out consumers where each consumer in the group receives its own copy of every record for independent processing.
Use Amazon SQS standard queue with multiple consumers polling the queue, leveraging the built-in visibility timeout to ensure each message is processed by only one consumer.

explanation: An SQS standard queue with multiple polling consumers implements the competing-consumers pattern as a fully managed, serverless service: the visibility timeout hides each in-flight message from other consumers, and if a consumer fails without deleting the message it becomes visible again for another consumer to reprocess. Option A (SNS fan-out to per-consumer queues) delivers a copy of every message to every consumer instead of load-balancing each message to exactly one. Option B (Amazon MQ RabbitMQ work queue) meets the functional requirements but requires provisioning, sizing, and maintaining a message broker, adding operational overhead SQS avoids. Option C (Kinesis Enhanced Fan-Out) delivers every record to every registered consumer rather than distributing each record to a single consumer in the group.

stem: A company is building a data pipeline that ingests 100 GB of CSV data daily from an SFTP server into Amazon S3. The data must be transformed into Parquet format and partitioned by date before being available for querying in Amazon Athena. Which solution requires the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy an EC2 instance running an SFTP client on a cron schedule to download files, then use a Python script to convert CSV to Parquet and upload to S3 with date partitioning.
Use AWS DataSync with an agent on-premises near the SFTP server to synchronize files to S3, then use Amazon EMR with Apache Spark to batch-convert CSV files to Parquet.
Use Amazon AppFlow to connect to the SFTP server and ingest data into S3, then use Lambda functions triggered by S3 events to convert each file from CSV to Parquet format.
Use AWS Transfer Family with an SFTP endpoint to receive files directly into S3, then trigger an AWS Glue ETL job to convert CSV to Parquet and partition by date.

explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP endpoint that delivers files directly to S3. AWS Glue is serverless and handles CSV-to-Parquet conversion with date partitioning, requiring no infrastructure management. Option A (EC2 with scripts) requires managing EC2 infrastructure and custom code. Option C (AppFlow) does not support SFTP as a connector source and Lambda has file size and timeout limitations. Option B (DataSync with EMR) requires managing a DataSync agent and EMR cluster, adding operational overhead.

stem: A company runs an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that processes messages from an SQS queue. During the day, the queue receives 10,000 messages per hour, but at night it receives fewer than 100 messages per hour. The Auto Scaling group maintains a minimum of 5 instances 24/7. Which change provides the GREATEST cost reduction?

options.text: Replace the EC2 instances with Lambda functions triggered by SQS events to eliminate idle instance costs and pay only for actual message processing compute time.
Configure the Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy based on the SQS queue depth with multiple thresholds to add instances in steps as the queue grows.
Configure a target tracking scaling policy based on the SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible per instance metric, allowing the group to scale down to 1 instance during low traffic.
Configure a scheduled scaling action to set the minimum capacity to 1 instance at night and 5 instances during the day based on the known traffic pattern schedule.

explanation: Replacing the instances with Lambda functions triggered by the SQS queue eliminates all idle compute cost: at night the near-zero message volume costs almost nothing, and during the day Lambda scales automatically with queue depth, so the company pays only for actual processing time. Option B (step scaling) adds instances reactively as the queue grows but leaves the 5-instance minimum running idle at night. Option C (target tracking) allows scaling down but still keeps at least 1 instance running 24/7. Option D (scheduled scaling) also leaves an idle instance running all night, saving less than eliminating instances entirely.

stem: A company needs to migrate a legacy application that uses a self-managed RabbitMQ message broker to AWS. The application cannot be modified to use a different messaging protocol. The company wants a managed solution with high availability. Which service should be used?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge as a replacement for RabbitMQ with event rules configured to route messages to the appropriate consumers based on the original RabbitMQ exchange routing.
Use Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) as a replacement for RabbitMQ since Kafka supports similar publish-subscribe messaging patterns with higher throughput.
Use Amazon SQS as a replacement for RabbitMQ and update the application connection strings to point to SQS endpoints using the RabbitMQ-compatible SQS Java SDK adapter.
Use Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ with a cluster deployment across multiple Availability Zones for high availability while maintaining full RabbitMQ protocol and API compatibility.

explanation: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ is a managed service that provides full RabbitMQ compatibility, allowing the legacy application to connect without code changes. Multi-AZ deployment provides high availability. Option C (SQS) uses a different API and there is no RabbitMQ-compatible SQS adapter. Option B (MSK/Kafka) uses a completely different protocol and messaging model than RabbitMQ. Option A (EventBridge) has a different API and routing model than RabbitMQ exchanges and queues.

stem: A company has deployed a web application using an Auto Scaling group with a minimum of 2 instances and a maximum of 10 instances across 3 Availability Zones. The company discovers that during an AZ failure, the application loses 33% of capacity temporarily. How should the architecture be modified to maintain full capacity during an AZ failure?

options.text: Enable cross-zone load balancing on the ALB and configure the Auto Scaling group to launch replacement instances in healthy AZs within 60 seconds of detecting an AZ failure.
Increase the minimum capacity to 3 instances (one per AZ) and set the desired capacity to 3 so that losing one AZ still leaves 2 instances to handle the full application load.
Set the minimum capacity to 6 instances (2 per AZ) so that losing any one AZ leaves 4 instances running, providing enough capacity to handle the full application workload.
Increase the minimum capacity to 4 instances distributed across 3 AZs so that losing any one AZ still leaves at least 2 instances with sufficient capacity for the full workload.

explanation: With 6 instances across 3 AZs (2 per AZ), losing one AZ leaves 4 instances which is still double the original minimum of 2. This ensures full capacity during any single AZ failure. Option B (3 instances) leaves only 2 after AZ failure which was the original minimum but may not handle full load if the application was scaled beyond minimum. Option D (4 instances) may leave only 1 instance in an AZ that fails if distribution is uneven. Option A (replacement launching) does not maintain capacity immediately during the failure since launching takes time.

stem: A company stores documents in Amazon S3 and needs to enable full-text search across all documents. Documents are in PDF, Word, and text formats totaling 5 TB. Search results must be returned within 2 seconds. Which approach should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Use Amazon Athena with S3 Select to scan document content stored in S3 and return matching results using SQL LIKE queries against the full text of each document file.
Use Amazon Kendra to create an index connected to the S3 bucket as a data source, leveraging its built-in document parsing and natural language search capabilities.
Use Amazon Textract to extract text from all documents, store the extracted text in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and implement a search API using OpenSearch query DSL.
Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze and index document content with entity extraction, store results in DynamoDB, and search using DynamoDB query operations on extracted entities.

explanation: Amazon Kendra is an enterprise search service that natively connects to S3, parses multiple document formats (PDF, Word, text), builds a search index, and returns results with natural language understanding within seconds. Option C (Textract to OpenSearch) requires building a custom extraction pipeline and managing the OpenSearch cluster. Option A (Athena with S3 Select) cannot parse PDF/Word formats and is not designed for full-text search. Option D (Comprehend to DynamoDB) extracts entities but does not provide full-text search capabilities.

stem: A company uses Amazon DynamoDB with provisioned capacity mode. The table has 1,000 Write Capacity Units (WCUs) and 5,000 Read Capacity Units (RCUs) provisioned. CloudWatch metrics show that actual usage is 200 WCUs and 1,000 RCUs on average with occasional spikes to 500 WCUs and 3,000 RCUs. Which optimization reduces costs?

options.text: Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for 200 WCUs and 1,000 RCUs with a 1-year commitment to receive significant discounts on the baseline provisioned capacity usage.
Reduce the provisioned capacity to 500 WCUs and 3,000 RCUs to match the peak usage and accept occasional throttling when traffic exceeds these peak capacity limits.
Switch to DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode which charges per request and automatically handles the variable traffic pattern without any capacity provisioning or management.
Enable DynamoDB auto scaling with target utilization of 70% for both reads and writes, setting minimum capacity to 200 WCUs/1,000 RCUs and maximum to 1,000 WCUs/5,000 RCUs.

explanation: Auto scaling dynamically adjusts capacity to match actual usage (200-500 WCUs, 1,000-3,000 RCUs), eliminating the waste from over-provisioned static capacity (1,000 WCUs, 5,000 RCUs). Option C (on-demand) may cost more than auto-scaled provisioned capacity for predictable workloads with consistent baseline traffic. Option A (reserved capacity) locks in capacity at the low baseline and does not address the over-provisioning of the remaining capacity. Option B (manual reduction) does not adjust dynamically and will throttle during spikes.

stem: A company is building a serverless application that uses Amazon API Gateway as the entry point. The company wants to protect the API from abuse by limiting the number of requests each API consumer can make. Different consumers should have different rate limits based on their subscription tier. Which feature should be configured?

options.text: Configure API Gateway usage plans with API keys to assign different rate limits and burst limits to each consumer tier, tracking usage against their allocated quotas.
Configure Amazon CloudFront in front of API Gateway with different cache behaviors per consumer tier, using CloudFront Functions to enforce rate limiting per API key.
Configure AWS WAF rate-based rules attached to the API Gateway with different rate thresholds configured per IP address based on the consumer tier identification.
Configure API Gateway stage-level throttling with a single rate limit for all consumers and use Lambda authorizers to return different throttling headers per consumer.

explanation: API Gateway usage plans allow creating different tiers with specific rate limits, burst limits, and quotas. API keys identify consumers and associate them with their tier. This is the native solution for per-consumer rate limiting. Option C (WAF rate-based rules) limits by IP address, not API consumer identity, and cannot differentiate tier levels per consumer. Option D (stage-level throttling) applies the same limit to all consumers and Lambda authorizer headers do not control actual throttling. Option B (CloudFront with Functions) is not designed for per-consumer API rate limiting.

stem: A company needs to deploy a containerized application that requires persistent storage. The storage must survive container restarts and be accessible if the container is rescheduled to a different host. The application runs on Amazon EKS with Fargate. Which storage option should be used?

options.text: Use Amazon EFS with the EFS CSI driver to create Persistent Volumes that can be mounted by pods on any Fargate node, providing shared and persistent storage across restarts.
Use Amazon EBS with the EBS CSI driver to create Persistent Volumes that are attached to the Fargate node and automatically reattached when pods are rescheduled to new nodes.
Use Amazon S3 with the Mountpoint for S3 CSI driver to mount an S3 bucket as a volume in the pod, providing unlimited persistent storage accessible from any Fargate node.
Use the Fargate ephemeral storage with a 200 GB capacity configuration to provide temporary storage that persists across container restarts within the same pod lifecycle.

explanation: Amazon EFS with the EFS CSI driver provides persistent, shared storage that is accessible from any Fargate node. Data survives container restarts and pod rescheduling because EFS is a network file system independent of the compute host. Option B (EBS) is not supported with Fargate pods since EBS volumes are tied to specific EC2 instances. Option D (ephemeral storage) is lost when the pod is terminated or rescheduled. Option C (S3 Mountpoint) provides read-optimized access and does not support the full POSIX write semantics many applications require.

stem: A company has a REST API that returns product catalog data. The same catalog data is requested thousands of times per minute by different clients. The data changes only once per hour. The API is served by Lambda functions behind API Gateway. Which caching strategy provides the BEST performance improvement?

options.text: Enable API Gateway stage-level caching with a 3600-second TTL on the GET methods for catalog endpoints to serve repeated requests from the API Gateway cache layer.
Enable Lambda response streaming and configure the function to return pre-computed responses stored in DynamoDB with read-through caching via DAX with 3600-second TTL.
Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of API Gateway with a cache policy that sets max-age to 3600 seconds for catalog endpoints, caching responses at edge locations globally.
Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster and modify the Lambda function to check the cache before querying the database, with a 3600-second TTL on cached catalog data.

explanation: CloudFront caches responses at 400+ global edge locations, serving thousands of requests per minute from cache without reaching API Gateway or Lambda. The 1-hour TTL matches the data change frequency. This provides the best performance by reducing latency for all global clients. Option A (API Gateway caching) only caches in one Region, not at global edge locations, and has limited cache capacity. Option D (ElastiCache) caches at the application layer but still requires Lambda invocation for each request. Option B (DAX) only works with DynamoDB and still requires Lambda invocation.

stem: A company needs to securely transfer 10 TB of data daily from an on-premises data center to Amazon S3 over an existing AWS Direct Connect connection. The data must be encrypted in transit and at rest. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync with an agent deployed on-premises to transfer data over Direct Connect to S3 with in-transit TLS encryption and S3 server-side encryption at rest.
Use a custom application on EC2 instances that downloads data from the on-premises server over Direct Connect using TLS and uploads to S3 with client-side encryption enabled.
Use AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoint in the VPC accessible over Direct Connect to receive files encrypted with SFTP protocol and store them in S3 with SSE-KMS encryption.
Use the AWS CLI s3 sync command running on an on-premises server to transfer data over Direct Connect with HTTPS encryption and S3 bucket default encryption configured.

explanation: AWS DataSync is purpose-built for large-scale data transfers with built-in TLS encryption in transit, automatic integrity verification, bandwidth throttling, and scheduling. It integrates with S3 server-side encryption for at-rest protection. Option D (AWS CLI s3 sync) lacks the optimization features of DataSync for large transfers (bandwidth management, incremental transfer, verification). Option C (Transfer Family SFTP) adds the overhead of managing an SFTP workflow and is designed for third-party file transfers, not bulk data movement. Option B (custom EC2 application) requires managing custom code and EC2 infrastructure.

stem: A company operates a SaaS application serving 1,000 tenants. Each tenant's data must be isolated from other tenants. The application uses Amazon DynamoDB. Which data isolation strategy provides the BEST balance of security and cost efficiency?

options.text: Create a separate DynamoDB table for each tenant with IAM policies restricting each tenant's access to only their own table, providing complete physical data isolation.
Use a single DynamoDB table with a tenant ID as the partition key prefix and implement fine-grained IAM policies with condition keys to restrict access to tenant-specific items.
Create a separate AWS account for each tenant using AWS Organizations and deploy isolated DynamoDB tables in each account with cross-account access for management.
Use a single DynamoDB table with a tenant ID attribute and implement application-level access control in the Lambda functions to filter results based on the authenticated tenant.

explanation: A single table with tenant ID as the partition key prefix provides logical isolation with IAM condition keys (dynamodb:LeadingKeys) enforcing item-level access control at the AWS level, and one table keeps costs and management low. Option A (separate tables per tenant) creates management complexity with 1,000 tables and makes capacity management and cross-tenant operations difficult. Option C (separate AWS accounts per tenant) is extremely expensive and operationally complex for 1,000 tenants. Option D (application-level filtering) relies on application logic for security, which is error-prone and not enforced by AWS.

stem: A company is migrating from a commercial relational database (Oracle) running on on-premises hardware to AWS. The application uses basic SQL queries with no Oracle-specific features like PL/SQL stored procedures or Oracle RAC. The company wants to minimize ongoing licensing and operational costs. Which target database provides the MOST cost savings?

options.text: Migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool for DDL conversion and DMS for data migration to eliminate all Oracle licensing costs permanently.
Migrate to Amazon RDS for Oracle with License Included pricing to avoid managing Oracle licenses while maintaining complete SQL compatibility with the existing application.
Migrate to Amazon EC2 with Oracle Database installed and purchase Oracle licenses directly from Oracle to maintain full control over the database configuration and licensing.
Migrate to Amazon RDS for Oracle with Bring Your Own License (BYOL) on Dedicated Hosts to reuse existing Oracle licenses and reduce per-hour database instance costs.

explanation: Since the application uses only basic SQL with no Oracle-specific features, migrating to Aurora PostgreSQL eliminates all Oracle licensing costs. Aurora provides high performance at a fraction of Oracle licensing cost. Option B (RDS Oracle License Included) bundles expensive Oracle licensing into the hourly rate. Option D (BYOL on Dedicated Hosts) still requires Oracle licenses and Dedicated Host costs. Option C (EC2 with Oracle) adds infrastructure management overhead and still requires Oracle licensing.

stem: A company wants to use AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure but needs to prevent accidental updates to production database resources. Database instances and their configurations must be protected from any stack updates. Which CloudFormation feature provides this protection?

options.text: Add the DeletionPolicy: Retain attribute to all database resources in the CloudFormation template to preserve databases if the stack is accidentally deleted or updated.
Enable CloudFormation termination protection on the stack to prevent any changes to the stack including updates to database resources and accidental stack deletion.
Create a separate CloudFormation stack for database resources and a different stack for application resources to isolate database changes from application deployment updates.
Configure a CloudFormation stack policy that explicitly denies Update actions on all database resources using the Resource type pattern for RDS and DynamoDB resources.

explanation: A stack policy explicitly controls which resources can be updated during stack update operations. Denying Update actions on database resource types prevents accidental modifications. Option B (termination protection) only prevents stack deletion, not updates to individual resources. Option A (DeletionPolicy: Retain) preserves resources on deletion but does not prevent modifications during updates. Option C (separate stacks) isolates deployments but does not prevent updates to the database stack itself.

stem: A company is deploying a containerized application on Amazon ECS. The application requires blue/green deployments with automatic rollback if the new version fails health checks. Which deployment configuration should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Configure ECS with rolling update deployment type using minimum healthy percent of 100% and maximum percent of 200% to gradually replace tasks while maintaining availability.
Configure ECS with external deployment controller and a Lambda function that manages task creation, health check validation, and traffic shifting through ALB listener rule updates.
Configure two separate ECS services behind the same ALB and use Route 53 weighted routing to gradually shift traffic from the blue service to the green service during deployment.
Configure ECS with AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment type, which creates a new task set behind the ALB and shifts traffic only after the new tasks pass health checks.

explanation: ECS with CodeDeploy blue/green deployment creates a new replacement task set, validates health checks, and shifts traffic using ALB listener rules. Automatic rollback reverts traffic to the original task set if health checks fail. Option A (rolling update) replaces tasks incrementally but does not support instant rollback to the previous version. Option C (two services with Route 53) adds DNS propagation delay and requires manual management of two services. Option B (external controller with Lambda) requires building custom deployment logic.

stem: A company needs to process real-time video streams from 500 security cameras. Each stream produces 2 Mbps of video data. The application must analyze each frame for object detection and store flagged frames in Amazon S3. Which architecture handles this workload?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to ingest all camera feeds, Amazon Rekognition Video for real-time object detection analysis, and S3 for storing flagged frame images.
Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) to ingest video streams, EC2 GPU instances for frame-by-frame object detection, and S3 for storing flagged results.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest video data as binary records, Lambda functions for object detection using a custom ML model, and S3 for storing flagged frames.
Use AWS IoT Greengrass on edge devices to preprocess video feeds locally, Amazon SQS to queue detection requests, and SageMaker endpoints for centralized object detection.

explanation: Kinesis Video Streams is purpose-built for ingesting video streams from cameras. Rekognition Video integrates natively with Kinesis Video Streams for real-time object detection without managing ML infrastructure. Flagged frames are stored in S3. Option B (MSK) is not designed for video stream ingestion and requires managing GPU instances for detection. Option C (Kinesis Data Streams) has a 1 MB record size limit which is insufficient for video frames, and Lambda cannot run GPU-based detection. Option D (Greengrass with SQS) requires deploying edge compute and the SQS-based architecture adds latency and complexity.

stem: A company is deploying a multi-account environment and needs to share Amazon VPC subnets from a central networking account with application accounts. Application accounts should be able to launch resources in the shared subnets but not modify the network configuration. Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Create VPC peering connections between the networking account VPC and each application account VPC, and configure route tables to enable cross-account network connectivity.
Create IAM cross-account roles in the networking account that allow application accounts to assume roles with EC2 and VPC permissions for launching resources in shared subnets.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share VPC subnets from the networking account with application accounts in the same AWS Organization for resource deployment.
Deploy AWS Transit Gateway in the networking account and attach VPCs from application accounts to enable shared network connectivity with centralized routing management.

explanation: AWS RAM enables sharing VPC subnets with other accounts. Application accounts can launch resources (EC2, RDS, etc.) in shared subnets but cannot modify the VPC, subnets, route tables, or other network components. Option A (VPC peering) creates separate VPCs in each account, not shared subnets. Option D (Transit Gateway) provides connectivity between VPCs but does not share subnets for direct resource deployment. Option B (cross-account roles) grants broad permissions that may allow network modifications, not meeting the restriction requirement.

stem: A company runs a production workload on 20 Amazon EC2 m5.xlarge instances 24/7 and has a development environment with 10 m5.large instances used only during business hours. The company plans to keep this setup for at least 3 years. Which purchasing strategy provides the LOWEST total cost?

options.text: Purchase 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the 20 production m5.xlarge instances and use Spot Instances for the 10 development m5.large instances.
Purchase 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for all 30 instances (both production and development) to receive the maximum discount on the entire fleet.
Purchase 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the 20 production m5.xlarge instances and use On-Demand pricing for the 10 development m5.large instances.
Purchase a 3-year Compute Savings Plan covering the 20 production instances and use Instance Scheduler to stop development instances outside business hours with On-Demand pricing.

explanation: 3-year Compute Savings Plan provides the deepest discount for production (similar to 3-year RI). Instance Scheduler stops dev instances ~60% of the time (nights/weekends), and On-Demand for the ~40% running time is cheaper than reserving instances that only run part-time. Option C (RIs for prod, On-Demand for dev) wastes money on full On-Demand pricing during dev business hours. Option A (Spot for dev) can interrupt developer work. Option B (RIs for all 30) wastes money on 10 dev RIs that are unused 60% of the time.

stem: A company uses Amazon Aurora MySQL with a writer instance and two reader instances. The writer instance fails. The company needs to understand how Aurora handles this failure and what the expected recovery time is. What happens when the Aurora writer instance fails?

options.text: Aurora redirects all write traffic to the remaining reader instances which handle both reads and writes until a new dedicated writer instance is provisioned automatically.
Aurora triggers an automated snapshot restore process that creates a new DB cluster from the most recent automated snapshot, requiring manual application endpoint reconfiguration.
Aurora launches a new writer instance from the last automated backup and replays transaction logs, typically completing recovery within 10-15 minutes with potential data loss.
Aurora automatically promotes one of the existing reader instances to become the new writer, typically completing failover within 30 seconds with no data loss due to shared storage.

explanation: Aurora automatically promotes a reader to writer within approximately 30 seconds. Because all instances share the same storage volume, there is no data loss and no need to replay transaction logs. The cluster endpoint automatically points to the new writer. Option C (backup restore) describes RDS behavior, not Aurora's shared storage architecture. Option A (readers handling writes) is not how Aurora works; only the writer instance handles writes. Option B (snapshot restore) requires manual intervention and is not part of Aurora's automatic failover process.

stem: A company needs to restrict EC2 instance launches in specific AWS Regions. Only us-east-1 and eu-west-1 should be allowed for all accounts in the organization. Which approach enforces this restriction?

options.text: Create IAM policies in each account that deny ec2:RunInstances with a condition that the aws:RequestedRegion is not us-east-1 or eu-west-1, and attach to all IAM users.
