Disable all AWS Regions except us-east-1 and eu-west-1 in the AWS Organizations account settings to prevent any service usage in non-approved Regions.
Create an SCP that denies all ec2:RunInstances actions with a condition that the aws:RequestedRegion is not in the allowed list of us-east-1 and eu-west-1 Regions.
Create AWS Config rules in each account to detect EC2 instances launched in non-approved Regions and configure auto-remediation to terminate them within 5 minutes.

explanation: SCPs apply to all accounts in the organization and cannot be overridden by account-level IAM policies. Denying ec2:RunInstances with a Region condition prevents launches in any non-approved Region. Option A (per-account IAM policies) must be maintained in each account and can be removed by account administrators. Option B (disabling Regions) prevents all services, not just EC2, and may break legitimate workloads. Option D (Config with auto-remediation) is reactive, allowing instances to run briefly before termination.

stem: A company runs a data processing application that reads from an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream with 10 shards. The application is deployed on 5 EC2 instances using the Kinesis Client Library (KCL). The company notices that processing is falling behind. Which action improves processing throughput WITHOUT increasing stream costs?

options.text: Enable Kinesis Enhanced Fan-Out for the consumer application to get dedicated 2 MB/second throughput per shard instead of sharing the default read throughput.
Switch from KCL to Lambda as the Kinesis stream consumer with a batch size of 1000 records to leverage Lambda's automatic scaling for higher processing throughput.
Increase the number of shards from 10 to 20 using the UpdateShardCount API and correspondingly scale the EC2 instances to 20 for doubled processing capacity.
Increase the number of EC2 instances to 10 to match the shard count, allowing each KCL worker to process exactly one shard for maximum parallelism and throughput.

explanation: With 10 shards and 5 instances, each KCL worker processes 2 shards; scaling to 10 instances lets KCL rebalance to 1 shard per worker, doubling per-shard processing capacity without changing the stream at all. Option A (Enhanced Fan-Out) incurs additional consumer-shard-hour and data retrieval charges on the stream, and extra read bandwidth does not help when the bottleneck is record processing speed. Option B (Lambda consumer) requires rewriting the KCL application and does not guarantee higher throughput for long-running record processing. Option C (doubling shards to 20) doubles shard-hour charges, directly increasing stream costs, and resharding is unnecessary when the current ingestion bandwidth is sufficient.

stem: A company is building a serverless application that needs to aggregate data from multiple AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, and a third-party REST API) into a single API response. Each data source takes 1-3 seconds to query. The total response time must be under 4 seconds. Which approach meets this requirement?

options.text: Use three separate Lambda functions behind API Gateway, one for each data source, and have the client make three parallel requests and combine the results on the client side.
Use AWS AppSync with a pipeline resolver whose functions query DynamoDB, S3, and the third-party API one after another, combining results into a single GraphQL response.
Use a single Lambda function that queries DynamoDB, S3, and the third-party API sequentially, caching results in ElastiCache for subsequent requests with a 5-minute TTL.
Use AWS Step Functions Express Workflow with a Parallel state that runs Lambda functions for each data source concurrently, combining results in a final aggregation step.

explanation: A Step Functions Express Workflow with a Parallel state fans out to the three data-source Lambda functions concurrently, so total time is roughly that of the slowest source (about 3 seconds) plus milliseconds of orchestration overhead, and the workflow can be invoked synchronously through API Gateway. Option A (client-side aggregation) requires three round trips from the client and pushes the combination logic onto every client instead of the API. Option B (AppSync pipeline resolver) executes its functions in sequence, so three 1-3 second queries can take up to about 9 seconds, exceeding the limit. Option C (single sequential Lambda) also adds the query times together (up to about 9 seconds), and caching does not help the first request meet the 4-second requirement.

stem: A company has a multi-Region architecture with an Application Load Balancer in each Region. Cross-Region data transfer between the ALBs and backend services accounts for 40% of networking costs. Which architecture change reduces cross-Region data transfer costs?

options.text: Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of all ALBs with aggressive caching policies to reduce the number of origin requests that generate cross-Region backend service communication.
Use VPC peering between all Regions with data compression enabled on the peering connections to reduce the effective bandwidth consumed by cross-Region data transfers.
Deploy backend services in each Region alongside the ALB to process requests locally, using DynamoDB global tables or Aurora Global Database for cross-Region data replication.
Replace the per-Region ALBs with a single AWS Global Accelerator endpoint that routes all traffic to one Region to eliminate cross-Region data transfer between services.

explanation: Deploying backend services in each Region alongside the ALB ensures requests are processed locally, eliminating cross-Region data transfer for request processing. Data replication through global tables or Aurora Global Database is more efficient than per-request cross-Region calls. Option D (single Region) concentrates all traffic in one Region, increasing latency for remote users. Option A (CloudFront caching) reduces origin requests but does not eliminate cross-Region backend calls for cache misses. Option B (VPC peering with compression) does not reduce the fundamental data transfer volume and VPC peering does not support compression.

stem: A company has a Lambda function that needs to connect to an Amazon RDS database in a VPC. The function runs hundreds of times per minute and each invocation opens a new database connection. The RDS instance is running out of connections. Which solution resolves this issue?

options.text: Increase the RDS instance size to a larger instance class that supports more concurrent database connections and adjust the max_connections parameter accordingly.
Add an ElastiCache for Redis layer between Lambda and RDS to cache database query results and reduce the frequency of direct database connections from Lambda functions.
Configure Lambda reserved concurrency to limit the number of simultaneous function executions to a value below the RDS maximum connection limit for throttled access.
Deploy Amazon RDS Proxy between the Lambda functions and the RDS instance to pool and share database connections, reducing the number of connections to the database.

explanation: RDS Proxy manages a pool of database connections and multiplexes Lambda requests across them, dramatically reducing the number of connections to the RDS instance. It also handles connection failover. Option A (larger instance) provides more connections but does not solve the fundamental issue of Lambda creating new connections per invocation. Option C (reserved concurrency) limits Lambda throughput, potentially degrading application performance. Option B (ElastiCache) reduces read load but write operations still require direct database connections.

stem: A company needs to implement a circuit breaker pattern for calls from a microservice running on ECS to an external third-party API. When the external API is down, the microservice should fail fast instead of waiting for timeouts. Which approach implements this pattern?

options.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 health checks for the external API and use a failover routing policy to redirect traffic to a fallback endpoint when the primary API is unhealthy.
Implement the circuit breaker pattern in the application code using a library such as resilience4j or Polly, with configurable failure thresholds and recovery timeouts.
Configure an Application Load Balancer health check for the external API endpoint and remove the API from the ALB target group when health checks fail repeatedly.
Use AWS App Mesh with an Envoy sidecar proxy configured with circuit breaker policies that trip after a specified number of consecutive failures to the external endpoint.

explanation: A circuit breaker library such as resilience4j or Polly tracks failures on outbound calls to the third-party API and opens the circuit after a configured failure threshold, so the microservice fails fast instead of waiting for timeouts and probes for recovery through a half-open state. Option A (Route 53 failover) operates at the DNS layer with health-check intervals and TTL propagation delays, not real-time per-call circuit breaking. Option C (ALB health checks) manages targets behind a load balancer the company controls; an external third-party API cannot be registered as an ALB target. Option D (App Mesh) cannot be adopted: AWS closed App Mesh to new customers in 2024 and it reaches end of support in September 2026, so it is not a viable choice for a new implementation.

stem: A company needs to run SQL queries across data in Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and Amazon Aurora from a single query interface. Analysts should be able to join tables across these data sources without moving data. The company already uses its Redshift cluster for analytics and does not want to deploy additional query infrastructure. Which service provides this capability?

options.text: Use AWS Lake Formation to build a centralized data lake by copying data from Redshift and Aurora into S3, then use Athena to query all data from the unified S3 location.
Use Amazon Redshift with Redshift Spectrum for S3 data and federated queries for Aurora data, enabling cross-source SQL joins through the Redshift query editor interface.
Use Amazon Athena with federated query connectors for Redshift and Aurora data sources, enabling cross-source SQL joins through the Athena query editor interface.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew to create a unified dataset from S3, Redshift, and Aurora sources, then query the combined dataset using Amazon Athena for cross-source analysis.

explanation: Redshift queries S3 data in place through Redshift Spectrum and reaches Aurora in place through federated queries, so analysts can join all three sources with native Redshift tables in a single SQL statement on the cluster the company already runs. Option A (Lake Formation with Athena) requires copying Redshift and Aurora data into S3, contradicting the no-data-movement requirement. Option C (Athena federated queries) can join the sources but requires deploying and managing Lambda-based connector functions for Redshift and Aurora, which is additional query infrastructure the company wants to avoid. Option D (Glue DataBrew) is a visual data preparation tool that produces new datasets, not a cross-source query engine.

stem: A company has 200 TB of infrequently accessed data in Amazon S3 Standard that must be available within 12 hours when requested. The data is accessed approximately twice per year. Which S3 storage class provides the LOWEST storage cost while meeting the retrieval requirement?

options.text: Transition the data to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval which provides low storage costs with millisecond retrieval for data accessed approximately once per quarter or less frequently.
Transition the data to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access which provides reduced storage costs compared to Standard with immediate retrieval for infrequently accessed data.
Transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval which provides low storage costs with standard retrieval available within 3-5 hours for the twice-yearly access pattern.
Transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive which provides the lowest per-GB storage cost with standard retrieval available within 12 hours for infrequent access patterns.

explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class in S3 at approximately $0.00099/GB/month. Standard retrieval (within 12 hours) meets the requirement. With only twice-yearly access, the low retrieval frequency minimizes retrieval costs. Option C (Glacier Flexible Retrieval) costs more per GB than Deep Archive. Option A (Glacier Instant Retrieval) costs significantly more than Deep Archive and millisecond retrieval is not needed. Option B (Standard-IA) costs much more per GB than any Glacier tier.

stem: A company needs to audit and track all changes to AWS resource configurations across all accounts in the organization. The audit data must be queryable and retained for 3 years. Which service provides continuous configuration auditing?

options.text: Enable AWS Trusted Advisor across all accounts with organizational view to monitor resource configurations and export the configuration data to S3 for long-term retention.
Enable AWS CloudTrail with an organization trail to log all API calls across all accounts and deliver logs to a centralized S3 bucket with Athena queries for audit analysis.
Enable Amazon Inspector across all accounts to continuously assess resource configurations for compliance violations and store assessment findings in Security Hub for 3 years.
Enable AWS Config with an aggregator across all accounts to record resource configuration changes and deliver configuration snapshots to a centralized S3 bucket for Athena queries.

explanation: AWS Config records detailed resource configuration history and changes over time. Config aggregator centralizes data across accounts. Configuration snapshots in S3 enable Athena queries for audit. Option B (CloudTrail) logs API calls but does not track the resulting resource configuration state. Option C (Inspector) assesses software vulnerabilities, not configuration change tracking. Option A (Trusted Advisor) provides best practice recommendations, not continuous configuration recording.

stem: A company builds an application using AWS Lambda that orchestrates a complex workflow with multiple steps, conditional branching, parallel execution, and error handling. Some steps call external APIs and the overall workflow takes up to 30 minutes. Which approach should be used to orchestrate this workflow?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions Express Workflows for the fastest execution with all state types including Map states for parallel processing and integrated error handling capabilities.
Use a single Lambda function with conditional logic that calls other Lambda functions sequentially, with try-catch blocks for error handling and DynamoDB for workflow state tracking.
Use AWS Step Functions Standard Workflows with states for each step, Choice states for branching, Parallel states for concurrent execution, and Catch/Retry for error handling.
Use Amazon SQS queues between each workflow step with Lambda consumers, using dead-letter queues for error handling and S3 for passing data between workflow step functions.

explanation: Step Functions Standard Workflows support long-running workflows up to 1 year (easily handles 30 minutes), with built-in support for branching (Choice), parallelism (Parallel), error handling (Catch/Retry), and visual monitoring. Option B (single Lambda orchestrator) hits the 15-minute Lambda timeout for a 30-minute workflow. Option D (SQS between steps) requires building custom workflow state management and branching logic. Option A (Express Workflows) have a 5-minute maximum duration, insufficient for 30-minute workflows.

stem: A company needs to implement a data lake architecture that allows different teams to query data using their preferred tools: SQL analysts use Athena, data scientists use Spark on EMR, and BI teams use Redshift. All teams need access to the same datasets. Which architecture enables this multi-tool access?

options.text: Store all data in Amazon S3 with the AWS Glue Data Catalog as the central metadata store, accessible by Athena, EMR with Spark, and Redshift Spectrum for unified data access.
Store copies of all data in separate formats optimized for each tool: Parquet in S3 for Athena, HDFS on EMR for Spark, and loaded tables in Redshift for the BI team.
Store all data in Amazon DynamoDB as the central data store and provide access through DynamoDB SQL-compatible queries for analysts and DynamoDB SDK for data scientists.
Store all data in Amazon Redshift as the central data warehouse and provide access through Redshift SQL for analysts, JDBC connections for Spark, and Redshift BI connectors.

explanation: S3 as the data lake with Glue Data Catalog as the central metastore enables all tools to access the same data. Athena queries S3 directly, EMR Spark reads from S3, and Redshift Spectrum queries S3 without loading data. This avoids data duplication. Option D (Redshift only) limits data scientists who prefer Spark and S3 access. Option C (DynamoDB) is not designed for analytical queries and does not support Spark or Athena natively. Option B (multiple copies) creates data management challenges with synchronization and storage costs.

stem: A company is setting up a new AWS account and needs to follow security best practices for the root user. Which set of actions should the solutions architect recommend for securing the root account?

options.text: Enable MFA on the root user, delete root access keys if they exist, create an IAM admin user for daily tasks, and enable CloudTrail to log all root user activity.
Enable MFA on the root user, create root access keys for programmatic access stored in Parameter Store, and use the root user only for billing and account management.
Create a strong password for the root user, share the password with the security team through Secrets Manager, and use root credentials for all administrative tasks.
Disable the root user login entirely through the IAM console, create an IAM admin user with full permissions, and use the IAM admin user for all account management tasks.

explanation: AWS best practices for a new account are to enable MFA on the root user, remove any root access keys, create an IAM administrative identity for daily work, and log all activity including root usage with CloudTrail. Option B (root access keys in Parameter Store) violates best practice because root access keys should never exist, regardless of where they are stored. Option C (sharing the root password via Secrets Manager) uses root for daily administration and shares the most privileged credential, violating least privilege. Option D (disabling root login in the IAM console) is not available for a standalone account; removing root credentials is possible only for member accounts through AWS Organizations centralized root access management, which does not apply to a new standalone account.

stem: A company needs to implement a disaster recovery strategy for an application running on EC2 instances with data stored in Amazon RDS. The DR solution must support an RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 1 hour. Which TWO components should be included to meet these objectives MOST cost-effectively? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Copy manual RDS snapshots to the DR Region on a 6-hour schedule and restore the most recent snapshot to a new database instance during a disaster event.
Create AMIs of the EC2 instances and copy them to the DR Region, then use CloudFormation templates to launch the infrastructure from AMIs during a disaster event.
Run identical EC2 instances in the DR Region at full production capacity to ensure immediate traffic redirection with zero compute provisioning time during failover.
Create an RDS cross-Region read replica in the DR Region with continuous replication to achieve an RPO of seconds, and promote the replica to primary during failover.

explanation: A cross-Region read replica replicates continuously (RPO of seconds, well within 1 hour) and can be promoted quickly during failover, and pre-copied AMIs launched through CloudFormation restore the compute tier well within the 4-hour RTO. Together they are the lowest-cost pair that meets both objectives because no idle compute runs in the DR Region. Option A (manual snapshot copies every 6 hours) can lose up to 6 hours of data, missing the 1-hour RPO. Option C (full-capacity standby fleet in the DR Region) meets the objectives but doubles compute spend, which is unnecessary for a 4-hour RTO and not cost-effective.

stem: A company wants to reduce the cost of running 50 t3.medium EC2 instances that host a microservices application on Amazon ECS. The instances run 24/7 and CPU utilization averages 10% across the fleet. Which approach provides the MOST cost reduction?

options.text: Right-size the instances by switching from t3.medium to t3.small and reduce the instance count from 50 to 25 by increasing task density per instance through better bin packing.
Purchase 50 t3.medium Reserved Instances with 1-year All Upfront payment to receive the maximum discount while maintaining the current fleet size and configuration.
Enable ECS cluster auto scaling with a managed termination protection capacity provider to dynamically adjust the instance count based on actual container resource needs.
Migrate from EC2 launch type to Fargate launch type and configure task CPU and memory to match the actual resource requirements of each individual microservice container.

explanation: With only 10% CPU utilization, the fleet is massively over-provisioned. Switching to smaller instances and improving bin packing reduces both instance size and count, potentially cutting costs by 75%+. Option B (Reserved Instances) saves on the current oversized fleet but does not address the fundamental waste. Option D (Fargate) may cost more than right-sized EC2 instances for 24/7 workloads. Option C (auto scaling) adjusts instance count but may not right-size individual instances.

stem: A company needs to encrypt data at the application level before storing it in Amazon DynamoDB. The encryption keys must be managed by AWS KMS with envelope encryption. Which approach correctly implements envelope encryption?

options.text: Enable DynamoDB server-side encryption with a customer managed KMS key and configure the table to use the specified KMS key for automatic encryption of all stored items.
Use the AWS Encryption SDK to generate a data key from KMS, encrypt data with the plaintext data key, and store the encrypted data key alongside the ciphertext in DynamoDB.
Generate encryption keys locally in the application using a cryptographic library, encrypt the data with the local key, and store the local key in KMS for safekeeping.
Call KMS Encrypt API directly with the data as the plaintext input and store the returned ciphertext in DynamoDB, using the KMS key for each encryption operation.

explanation: The AWS Encryption SDK implements envelope encryption: it calls KMS GenerateDataKey to get a plaintext and encrypted data key, encrypts data locally with the plaintext key, then stores the encrypted data key with the ciphertext. On decryption, KMS decrypts the data key. Option D (direct KMS Encrypt) has a 4 KB plaintext limit and makes a KMS API call for every encryption, which is slow and expensive. Option A (DynamoDB server-side encryption) is not application-level encryption. Option C (local key in KMS) is not envelope encryption as KMS is only used for key storage, not key generation and protection.

stem: A company has a critical application database on Amazon RDS PostgreSQL with a 500 GB storage volume. The database requires a maintenance operation that involves a major version upgrade. The company needs to minimize downtime and have a rollback plan. Which approach should be used?

options.text: Create a read replica running the new version, test the application against the replica, then promote the replica to a standalone instance and redirect the application endpoint.
Use the RDS Blue/Green Deployment feature to create a green environment with the new version, test it, and switch over with minimal downtime and automatic rollback capability.
Create a manual snapshot before the upgrade, perform the in-place major version upgrade during a maintenance window, and restore from the snapshot if rollback is needed.
Export the database to S3 using the RDS snapshot export feature, import it into a new RDS instance running the new version, and switch the application endpoint after verification.

explanation: RDS Blue/Green Deployments create a staging environment (green) with the new version using logical replication from the production (blue) environment. After testing, switchover takes about one minute with automatic rollback if issues are detected. Option C (in-place upgrade with snapshot) requires significant downtime during the upgrade and snapshot restoration for rollback is slow. Option A (read replica promotion) does not support major version upgrades on the replica directly. Option D (S3 export/import) is extremely slow for 500 GB and requires significant downtime.

stem: A company needs to deliver live streaming video content to 100,000 concurrent viewers worldwide with minimal latency. The video is encoded in HLS format from a media server running on EC2. Which service should distribute the live stream?

options.text: Use AWS Elemental MediaLive for live encoding and AWS Elemental MediaPackage for origin and packaging, with Amazon CloudFront for global distribution to all viewers.
Use AWS Global Accelerator to route viewer connections to the nearest EC2 media server instance deployed in multiple Regions for localized live stream delivery.
Use Amazon CloudFront with the media server as the origin, configuring low TTL cache behaviors for HLS segments and real-time log delivery for viewer analytics monitoring.
Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to ingest the live video and configure HLS playback sessions for each viewer to stream directly from the Kinesis Video Streams endpoint.

explanation: CloudFront distributes HLS live streams globally through 400+ edge locations, caching video segments close to viewers. Low TTL on segments ensures near-live latency while the CDN handles 100,000 concurrent viewers easily. Option A (MediaLive with MediaPackage) is a complete solution but adds unnecessary encoding infrastructure when the media server already produces HLS. Option D (Kinesis Video Streams) is designed for device-to-cloud video ingestion, not large-scale live streaming distribution. Option B (Global Accelerator to EC2) would require deploying media servers in every Region and cannot scale to 100,000 viewers per server.

stem: A company uses Amazon S3 to store 500 million objects with an average size of 1 KB each. The company receives many GET requests for these small objects. S3 request costs are the dominant expense. Which optimization reduces S3 request costs the MOST?

options.text: Enable S3 Requester Pays on the bucket to shift the request costs from the bucket owner to the requesting account or user for all GET request operations.
Move the objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically optimize storage costs based on access patterns and reduce the per-request cost through tiered pricing benefits.
Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of S3 to cache frequently accessed objects at edge locations, reducing the number of GET requests that reach S3 from repeated access.
Consolidate multiple small objects into larger aggregate objects (e.g., bundle 1,000 objects into 1 MB files) and implement an index in DynamoDB to map individual keys to aggregates.

explanation: CloudFront caches objects at edge locations, dramatically reducing the number of S3 GET requests. For frequently accessed objects, the cache hit ratio can be very high, cutting S3 request costs significantly. Option D (object consolidation) reduces request count but requires application changes and an index system, adding complexity. Option B (Intelligent-Tiering) optimizes storage costs, not request costs. Option A (Requester Pays) shifts costs to requesters but does not reduce total request costs.

stem: A company runs a web application that collects user data subject to GDPR. Users must be able to request deletion of all their personal data within 30 days. The data is stored across Amazon S3, Amazon RDS, and Amazon DynamoDB. Which architecture facilitates GDPR data deletion requests?

options.text: Implement a centralized data catalog in AWS Glue that tracks where each user's data is stored across S3, RDS, and DynamoDB to enable targeted deletion across all data stores.
Configure automated S3 Lifecycle rules, RDS snapshot deletion schedules, and DynamoDB TTL to automatically delete all data after 30 days without requiring individual requests.
Store all user data exclusively in Amazon S3 using a user ID prefix structure, then delete the entire prefix when a deletion request is received using the S3 batch delete API.
Enable Amazon Macie across all data stores to automatically discover and classify personal data, then use Macie findings to identify and delete data for specific user requests.

explanation: A centralized data catalog tracks the location of each user's data across all services, enabling targeted deletion from S3, RDS, and DynamoDB when a request is received. This is the architectural pattern for GDPR right-to-erasure compliance. Option C (S3-only storage) requires re-architecting the entire data layer. Option D (Macie) discovers sensitive data but does not facilitate targeted deletion of specific user data across services. Option B (automatic deletion after 30 days) deletes all data indiscriminately, not specific user data on request.

stem: A company has an event-driven application where an S3 upload triggers a sequence of processing steps: thumbnail generation, metadata extraction, and database update. If any step fails, the entire sequence should be retried. Which orchestration approach is MOST reliable?

options.text: Configure S3 event notifications to trigger an EventBridge rule that invokes three Lambda functions through separate targets, with EventBridge retry policies on each target.
Configure S3 event notifications to trigger a Step Functions Standard Workflow that executes each step with Retry and Catch error handling for automatic retry on any failure.
Configure S3 event notifications to trigger a Lambda function that calls three other Lambda functions in sequence, with try-catch blocks to retry the entire chain on failure.
Configure S3 event notifications to publish to an SNS topic with three Lambda function subscriptions, one for each step, executing all steps simultaneously and independently.

explanation: Step Functions with Retry and Catch states provides reliable orchestration with automatic retry for failed steps, visual workflow monitoring, and state management. The entire sequence is treated as a single workflow with guaranteed completion. Option C (Lambda chain) requires custom retry logic and the orchestrator Lambda may timeout for long sequences. Option D (SNS fanout) executes steps in parallel and independently, not sequentially with retry-on-failure semantics. Option A (EventBridge with separate targets) treats each step independently without sequential dependency or full-sequence retry.

stem: A company migrates a legacy application to AWS that uses a relational database with stored procedures, triggers, and complex multi-table transactions. The database is 2 TB and must support ACID transactions. The company wants a managed service with minimal migration effort. Which service should be used?

options.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB transactions enabled and rewrite stored procedures as Lambda functions triggered by DynamoDB Streams for event-driven processing.
Use Amazon DocumentDB with MongoDB compatibility mode to store relational data as JSON documents and implement transactions using the DocumentDB multi-document ACID support.
Use Amazon RDS for the same database engine as the source (MySQL, PostgreSQL, or Oracle) to maintain full compatibility with stored procedures, triggers, and transactions.
Use Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 which provides MySQL or PostgreSQL compatibility with automatic scaling and full support for stored procedures and ACID transactions.

explanation: Amazon RDS for the same database engine (e.g., RDS for Oracle if source is Oracle) provides maximum compatibility with stored procedures, triggers, and transaction semantics, minimizing migration effort. Option A (DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database that requires complete application rewrite. Option D (Aurora Serverless v2) works for MySQL or PostgreSQL sources but may require modifications for Oracle or SQL Server-specific stored procedures. Option B (DocumentDB) is a document database requiring data model redesign.

stem: A company has deployed an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with a db.r5.4xlarge writer and two db.r5.4xlarge reader instances. The application uses the writer for all operations including reads. The reader instances are idle. Which action optimizes cost while maintaining the existing architecture?

options.text: Remove one of the idle reader instances to immediately reduce costs by one-third while keeping one reader for failover and configuring the application to use the reader endpoint.
Configure the application to use the Aurora reader endpoint for read queries and keep both reader instances to distribute the read load away from the writer instance.
Downsize the idle reader instances from db.r5.4xlarge to db.r5.large since they are only needed for failover and do not need the same compute capacity as the writer.
Remove both reader instances entirely and rely on Aurora's automatic failover to create a new instance from the shared storage volume if the writer instance fails.

explanation: Since readers are idle and only serve as failover targets, downsizing them to db.r5.large significantly reduces costs while maintaining failover capability. Aurora failover does not require readers to match the writer size. Option A (remove one reader) reduces redundancy and configuring read routing requires application changes. Option B (use reader endpoint) is the right approach for utilizing readers but does not address the immediate cost problem. Option D (remove all readers) eliminates automatic failover capability, risking extended downtime.

stem: A company needs to provide temporary AWS console access to 500 corporate employees who authenticate through the company's existing SAML 2.0 identity provider. The company does not want to create individual IAM users. Which solution provides federated console access?

options.text: Create 500 IAM users with programmatic access and configure a custom portal that authenticates users against the corporate IdP before providing IAM user credentials.
Deploy Amazon Cognito user pools federated with the corporate SAML 2.0 provider and configure Cognito to issue temporary AWS credentials for console access through identity pools.
Configure AWS IAM Identity Center with the corporate SAML 2.0 identity provider and assign permission sets to groups that map to corporate directory groups for role-based access.
Configure an IAM SAML identity provider and create IAM roles for each department, then build a custom single sign-on portal that calls STS AssumeRoleWithSAML.

explanation: IAM Identity Center (SSO) natively integrates with SAML 2.0 identity providers and provides a managed SSO portal for AWS console access. Permission sets define access levels and map to corporate groups without creating IAM users. Option A (individual IAM users) violates the no-IAM-users requirement. Option D (custom SSO portal) works but requires building and maintaining custom infrastructure. Option B (Cognito) is designed for application authentication, not AWS console access.

stem: A company runs an Amazon EKS cluster that serves a production API. The cluster needs to handle node failures gracefully without impacting API availability. Pods must be rescheduled to healthy nodes within 60 seconds of a node failure. Which configuration ensures this behavior?

options.text: Configure the EKS cluster with a single large node and use Kubernetes pod restart policies to automatically restart failed pods on the same node after detecting health check failures.
Configure the EKS cluster with managed node groups across multiple AZs and set pod disruption budgets to ensure minimum available replicas during node replacement operations.
Configure the EKS cluster with self-managed nodes and a custom Lambda function that monitors node health through CloudWatch and terminates unhealthy nodes for Auto Scaling replacement.
Configure the EKS cluster with Fargate profiles for all pods to eliminate node management entirely and rely on Fargate's automatic pod rescheduling on infrastructure failures.

explanation: Managed node groups across multiple AZs provide automatic node replacement and Kubernetes reschedules pods to healthy nodes. Pod disruption budgets ensure minimum replicas remain available during disruptions. This architecture handles node failures within seconds. Option A (single node) has no redundancy and pod restart on the same failed node does not help. Option C (custom Lambda monitoring) adds latency beyond 60 seconds and is fragile. Option D (Fargate) may have longer pod startup times due to provisioning new Fargate capacity.

stem: A company needs to process 1 million images per day through a classification model. Each image takes 2 seconds to classify. The workload is spread evenly throughout the day. The company wants the MOST cost-effective serverless solution. Which architecture should be used?

options.text: Upload images to S3, send notifications to SQS, and process images using SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoints that scale automatically based on the number of queued requests.
Upload images to S3, trigger Lambda functions through S3 event notifications for each image, and run the classification model within the Lambda function at 2048 MB memory.
Upload images to S3, configure an EventBridge rule to batch-trigger Step Functions Express Workflows that process images in parallel using Map states with Lambda task functions.
Upload images to S3, trigger Lambda functions for each image, and call Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels API for classification instead of hosting the model in Lambda.

explanation: Lambda is the most cost-effective serverless option for this workload. At 1M images/day (11.5 images/sec), Lambda can handle this with moderate concurrency (~23 concurrent invocations at 2 seconds each). Per-invocation billing at 2 seconds x 2048 MB is cost-efficient. Option A (SageMaker Serverless) has minimum billing per invocation and higher per-second costs than Lambda for lightweight classification. Option D (Rekognition Custom Labels) charges per inference and per training hour, which is more expensive for high-volume classification. Option C (Step Functions) adds orchestration costs and complexity for a simple per-image processing workload.

stem: A company operates a public-facing API that receives requests from known partner IP ranges and unknown public users. Partner requests should bypass rate limiting while public users should be rate-limited to 100 requests per 5 minutes. Which solution implements this differentiated access?

options.text: Configure Amazon API Gateway with a usage plan for partners using API keys that bypass throttling and a default usage plan with 100-request-per-5-minute throttling for public users.
Configure Amazon CloudFront with a signed URL policy for partner access and configure Lambda@Edge to count and block public user requests exceeding 100 per 5-minute window.
Configure Network ACLs on the ALB subnet to allow partner IPs without restriction and apply security group rules with connection limiting for all other source IP addresses.
Configure AWS WAF with an IP set containing partner IPs and create a rule that allows partner IP requests without rate limiting while applying rate-based rules to all other traffic.

explanation: AWS WAF IP sets allow creating rules that match partner IPs and skip rate limiting. A rate-based rule applies to all non-partner traffic, limiting public users to the specified threshold. This provides differentiated access at the infrastructure level. Option C (NACLs and security groups) cannot implement rate limiting at the network layer. Option A (API Gateway usage plans) works but requires partners to use API keys rather than IP-based identification. Option B (CloudFront with Lambda@Edge) requires building custom rate limiting logic and managing request counting state.

stem: A company needs to replicate data from an Amazon Aurora MySQL database to an Amazon Redshift cluster in the same AWS Region in near real-time for analytics. Which solution provides continuous data replication with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Schedule an AWS Glue ETL job to run every 5 minutes that reads new records from Aurora using bookmarks and loads incremental data into the Redshift cluster for analytics.
Use AWS DMS with a replication instance configured for ongoing CDC replication from Aurora to Redshift, with table mappings to transform data during the replication process.
Create a Lambda function triggered by Aurora event notifications that reads changed records and writes them to the Redshift cluster using the Redshift Data API for insertions.
Use Aurora zero-ETL integration with Amazon Redshift to automatically replicate Aurora data changes to the Redshift cluster in near real-time without managing ETL pipelines.

explanation: Aurora zero-ETL integration with Amazon Redshift is a fully managed service-to-service integration that replicates Aurora data changes to Redshift in near real-time within a Region, with no pipelines, replication servers, or custom code to operate. Option A (scheduled Glue ETL job) is batch processing with at least 5-minute latency plus ongoing job maintenance, not continuous replication. Option B (DMS with ongoing CDC) works but requires provisioning, sizing, monitoring, and patching a replication instance. Option C (Lambda with the Redshift Data API) requires custom code and can miss changes because Aurora event notifications do not deliver row-level change data.

stem: A company has a web application that serves personalized content. The application makes 50 database queries per page load, and each page load takes 3 seconds. The database is Amazon Aurora MySQL with 70% CPU utilization. Which optimization has the HIGHEST impact on page load time?

options.text: Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to cache frequently accessed query results, reducing the number of database round trips per page load from 50 to approximately 5.
Scale up the Aurora writer instance to the next larger instance class to reduce query execution time by providing more CPU and memory for database query processing.
Enable Aurora query caching at the database level and optimize the database schema with additional indexes on frequently queried columns to reduce per-query execution time.
Add Aurora read replicas and configure the application to send all 50 read queries to the reader endpoint for horizontal read scaling and reduced writer instance load.

explanation: Caching 90% of queries in ElastiCache reduces database round trips from 50 to ~5, dramatically reducing page load time since network round trips are the dominant latency factor. Sub-millisecond Redis responses replace multi-millisecond database queries. Option B (scale up) reduces individual query time marginally but does not eliminate the 50 round trips. Option D (read replicas) distributes load but each page still requires 50 round trips. Option C (query cache and indexes) provides marginal improvements per query but does not reduce the fundamental 50-round-trip problem.

stem: A company uses Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3. The data arrives in small files (1-5 MB each) resulting in millions of small files in S3. This causes slow Amazon Athena query performance and high S3 request costs. Which optimization addresses both issues?

options.text: Switch from S3 delivery to Amazon Redshift Streaming Ingestion to eliminate small file problems by writing data directly into Redshift's columnar storage for fast queries.
Run a periodic AWS Glue compaction job that merges small files in S3 into larger files grouped by partition key and converts them from JSON to Parquet columnar format.
Configure Kinesis Data Firehose buffer hints with a larger buffer size (128 MB) and longer buffer interval (900 seconds) to produce fewer, larger files delivered to S3.
Configure Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver data to S3 with dynamic partitioning enabled and Parquet format conversion to optimize file size and query scan efficiency.

explanation: Increasing Firehose buffer size and interval produces fewer, larger files (up to 128 MB), directly reducing both the number of S3 objects (reducing request costs) and the number of files Athena must scan (improving query performance). Option D (dynamic partitioning with Parquet) improves query patterns but does not consolidate small files if the buffer settings remain small. Option B (Glue compaction) is reactive and adds ongoing operational costs. Option A (Redshift) changes the architecture and adds Redshift costs.

stem: A company is running an application on Amazon EC2 that needs to read objects from an S3 bucket in another AWS account. The company does not want to use access keys. Which cross-account access configuration should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Configure the S3 bucket policy in the other account to grant s3:GetObject permission to the IAM role attached to the EC2 instance profile in the application account.
Create IAM access keys in the S3 bucket account and store them in AWS Secrets Manager in the application account for the EC2 application to retrieve and use for S3 access.
Create an IAM role in the S3 bucket account with an S3 read policy and a trust policy allowing the EC2 instance's role to assume it, then call STS AssumeRole from the application.
Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication from the other account's bucket to a bucket in the application account and have the EC2 instance read from the local replicated bucket.

explanation: An S3 bucket policy can grant cross-account access to the EC2 instance's IAM role ARN. The EC2 instance uses its instance profile credentials (no access keys) and the bucket policy authorizes access. This is the simplest cross-account S3 access pattern. Option C (AssumeRole) works but adds complexity by requiring the application to call STS and manage assumed role sessions. Option B (access keys in Secrets Manager) violates the no-access-keys requirement. Option D (replication) adds storage cost and replication lag for read-only access.

stem: A company runs a production workload on a fleet of EC2 instances. The operations team needs to apply OS security patches to all instances with minimal downtime. The patches must be tested on a staging group before production deployment. Which approach provides safe, staged patching with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Lambda functions with Systems Manager Run Command to execute patch installation scripts on all instances simultaneously during off-peak hours for fastest completion.
SSH into each production instance manually during a maintenance window and run OS-level package update commands, verifying each instance after patching before proceeding.
Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager with patch baselines, deploy patches to a staging group first using a maintenance window, then deploy to production after verification.
Create a new AMI with the latest patches, test it on staging instances, then update the Auto Scaling group launch template and perform a rolling replacement of production instances.

explanation: Systems Manager Patch Manager applies approved patch baselines through maintenance windows and patch groups, so patches roll out to a staging group first and then to production with no infrastructure to rebuild — safe, staged patching with minimal effort. Option A (Run Command on all instances simultaneously) skips staging validation and patches every production instance at once. Option B (manual SSH patching) is error-prone, slow, and does not scale across a fleet. Option D (golden AMI with rolling replacement) also achieves safe staged patching, but building, testing, and rolling out a new AMI every patch cycle carries more operational overhead than Patch Manager.

stem: A company builds a REST API using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The API experiences cold starts of 5-10 seconds for the Java-based Lambda function. The company needs to reduce cold start latency to under 500 milliseconds for all invocations. Which solution achieves this?

options.text: Enable Lambda SnapStart on the published function version so invocations resume from a cached snapshot of the initialized execution environment instead of running full initialization.
Rewrite the Lambda function in Python to reduce cold start time and increase the memory allocation to 3008 MB to get proportionally more CPU for faster initialization.
Configure API Gateway caching with a 60-second TTL to serve repeated requests from cache and reduce the number of Lambda invocations that experience cold start latency.
Deploy the Lambda function in a VPC with a NAT Gateway for internet access and enable RDS Proxy for database connection pooling to reduce connection initialization time.

explanation: Lambda SnapStart caches a snapshot of the fully initialized Java execution environment and resumes new environments from that snapshot, cutting cold starts from seconds to typically well under 500 ms with no code changes. Note that SnapStart cannot be combined with provisioned concurrency, which is a separate, mutually exclusive way to avoid cold starts. Option B (rewrite in Python with more memory) is a major code rewrite and still incurs cold starts that may exceed the target. Option C (API Gateway caching) helps only repeated identical requests; uncached invocations still hit the full cold start. Option D (VPC deployment with RDS Proxy) addresses database connection reuse, not Lambda initialization latency.

stem: A company operates a global application with users in 10 countries. The application backend runs in us-east-1 only. The company uses Amazon CloudFront for content delivery. The CloudFront bill shows charges for edge locations in all global Regions. How can the company reduce CloudFront costs if 80% of users are in North America and Europe?

options.text: Configure CloudFront geo-restriction to block users from countries outside North America and Europe to eliminate all traffic charges from other global edge locations.
Configure CloudFront Price Class 200 which includes North America, Europe, Asia, Middle East, and Africa edge locations while excluding more expensive South American and Australian edges.
Configure CloudFront Origin Shield in us-east-1 to consolidate origin fetches and reduce the number of requests reaching the origin from global edge locations.
Configure CloudFront Price Class 100 which includes only North America and Europe edge locations, reducing per-GB pricing by excluding more expensive global edge locations.

explanation: Price Class 100 limits CloudFront to the least expensive edge locations in North America and Europe, where 80% of users are located. This reduces per-GB costs while still serving the majority of users from nearby edges. Option B (Price Class 200) includes more regions than needed, not maximizing savings. Option A (geo-restriction) blocks 20% of users entirely which is unacceptable. Option C (Origin Shield) reduces origin fetch costs but does not reduce edge delivery charges.

stem: A company runs a Docker container application on Amazon ECS and needs to pull container images from a private Amazon ECR repository. The ECS tasks run on EC2 instances in private subnets without internet access. Which configuration allows ECR image pulls?

options.text: Create VPC interface endpoints for Amazon ECR (ecr.api, ecr.dkr) and Amazon S3 (gateway endpoint) to allow private connectivity for pulling container images without internet access.
Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet and add a route from the private subnet to the NAT Gateway to allow EC2 instances to reach the public ECR endpoints over the internet.
Copy container images from ECR to an S3 bucket in the same Region and configure the ECS task definition to pull images from the S3 bucket using an S3 VPC gateway endpoint.
Configure the ECR repository policy to allow access from the VPC CIDR range and enable ECR public endpoint access for the private subnet through a VPC endpoint routing rule.

explanation: VPC interface endpoints for ECR API and Docker (ecr.api, ecr.dkr) plus an S3 gateway endpoint allow private image pulls without internet access. ECR stores image layers in S3, so the S3 endpoint is required. Option B (NAT Gateway) provides internet access but the requirement states no internet access. Option D (repository policy with CIDR) does not enable private connectivity without VPC endpoints. Option C (S3-based image pull) is not a supported ECS image pull mechanism.

stem: A company has an application that writes transaction records to Amazon DynamoDB. During a peak sales event, the application receives WriteThrottleEvents. The company has already enabled DynamoDB auto scaling but it is not scaling fast enough. Which immediate action resolves the throttling?

options.text: Switch the table to on-demand capacity mode which instantly scales to handle any write traffic volume without throttling and does not require capacity management during events.
Add an SQS queue in front of DynamoDB to buffer writes and process them at the current provisioned rate, smoothing the burst traffic during the peak sales event.
Manually increase the provisioned write capacity to a level that can handle the expected peak traffic, then let auto scaling manage capacity after the event concludes.
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to absorb the write traffic through the write-through cache and reduce direct writes to the DynamoDB table during peak periods.

explanation: Switching to on-demand mode immediately eliminates throttling by automatically handling any traffic level. This is the fastest resolution as the capacity adjustment is instant. After the event, the company can switch back to provisioned if desired. Option C (manual increase) requires knowing the exact peak level and auto scaling target changes take time to take effect. Option B (SQS buffering) adds latency and requires application changes. Option D (DAX) is primarily a read cache and write-through DAX still writes to DynamoDB at the same rate.

stem: A company is building a data analytics platform that must support both real-time dashboards and batch reporting. Real-time data arrives from IoT devices and must be available in dashboards within 60 seconds. Daily batch reports analyze 24 hours of aggregated data. Which TWO components should the architecture include? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon SQS to queue IoT data messages and process them with Lambda functions that update a DynamoDB table used by the real-time dashboard for immediate data display.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver IoT data to Amazon S3 in near real-time and use AWS Glue ETL jobs scheduled daily to aggregate 24 hours of data for batch reports.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest real-time IoT data and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to process and deliver data to the real-time dashboard within 60 seconds.
Use Amazon SNS to fan out IoT data to both a real-time processing Lambda function and a batch S3 storage path simultaneously for dual real-time and batch analytics.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams with Apache Flink provides real-time processing within 60 seconds for dashboards. Kinesis Data Firehose delivers data to S3 for long-term storage, and Glue ETL processes the daily batch aggregation for reports. This is the Lambda architecture pattern. Option A (SQS with Lambda to DynamoDB) is viable for real-time but DynamoDB is not optimal for complex batch aggregation queries. Option D (SNS fanout) does not guarantee ordered delivery and is not designed for high-volume IoT data ingestion.

stem: A company has an AWS account with multiple development teams. Each team creates resources but often forgets to clean up unused resources. The company wants to identify and track resource ownership for cost allocation. Which approach provides the BEST cost visibility per team?

options.text: Enable AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to identify unexpected cost increases by team and configure SNS notifications to alert team leads when their team's spending spikes.
Create a separate AWS account for each development team using AWS Organizations and use consolidated billing to view per-account (per-team) costs in the management account.
Implement a tagging strategy with mandatory cost allocation tags (e.g., Team, Project) and enable the tags in AWS Cost Explorer for per-team cost breakdown and analysis.
Deploy AWS Trusted Advisor across all teams and review the cost optimization recommendations weekly to identify unused resources that teams should clean up manually.

explanation: Cost allocation tags with team identifiers enable granular cost breakdown in Cost Explorer by team. This provides direct visibility into which team owns which resources and their associated costs. Option B (separate accounts) is heavy-handed for development teams and adds management complexity. Option A (anomaly detection) identifies spikes but does not provide ongoing cost breakdown by team. Option D (Trusted Advisor) provides general recommendations but does not track ownership or allocate costs by team.

stem: A company has an application running on EC2 that accesses an Amazon RDS database. The security team requires that the database connection uses SSL/TLS encryption and that the application verifies the server certificate to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks. Which configuration meets this requirement?

options.text: Enable the rds.force_ssl parameter in the RDS parameter group to require all connections to use SSL, and configure the application to connect without specifying certificate verification.
Enable RDS storage encryption with a KMS customer managed key to encrypt all data at rest and in transit between the application EC2 instance and the RDS database instance.
Download the AWS RDS root CA certificate bundle, configure the application's database driver to require SSL connections and verify the server certificate against the CA bundle.
Configure a VPC interface endpoint for RDS and route database traffic through the endpoint to ensure encryption through AWS PrivateLink without application-level SSL configuration.

explanation: Downloading the RDS CA certificate bundle and configuring the driver to verify server certificates ensures encrypted connections and prevents MITM attacks through certificate validation. Option A (force_ssl without verification) encrypts the connection but without certificate verification, the application cannot detect MITM attacks. Option D (VPC endpoint) provides private connectivity but does not encrypt the database protocol traffic. Option B (storage encryption) encrypts data at rest, not the connection between the application and database.

stem: A company deploys a web application across two Availability Zones using an Auto Scaling group. The application stores user session state in memory on each EC2 instance. When instances are terminated by Auto Scaling, users lose their sessions. Session reads and writes must complete with sub-millisecond latency. Which solution maintains session persistence across scaling events?

options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use a scale-in protection policy on instances with active sessions and only terminate instances after all sessions have naturally expired.
Externalize session storage to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with automatic failover enabled, and configure the application to read and write session data from the Redis cluster.
Enable ALB sticky sessions with application-based cookies that route returning users to the same instance and configure session replication between all instances in the group.
Store session data in Amazon DynamoDB with a TTL attribute matching the session expiration time, and configure the application to use DynamoDB as the session store backend.

explanation: ElastiCache for Redis stores sessions in memory outside the instances, delivering sub-millisecond reads and writes, and sessions survive any instance termination; automatic failover keeps the session store available. Option A (scale-in protection until sessions expire) blocks scale-in, defeating the purpose of Auto Scaling, and still loses sessions on instance failure. Option C (sticky sessions with instance-level replication) still loses sessions when the pinned instance is terminated before replication completes. Option D (DynamoDB with TTL) persists sessions across terminations but provides single-digit-millisecond latency, missing the sub-millisecond requirement.

stem: A company needs to serve a static single-page application (SPA) built with React. The application consists of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and image files. The company wants the MOST cost-effective hosting solution with global low-latency delivery. Which architecture should be used?

options.text: Deploy the SPA files to Amazon EFS mounted on EC2 instances behind an ALB with CloudFront providing CDN caching and origin failover for high availability and performance.
Deploy the SPA on AWS Amplify Hosting which provides a fully managed CI/CD pipeline with global CDN distribution, HTTPS certificates, and branch-based preview environments.
Deploy the SPA on Amazon EC2 instances running Nginx behind an Application Load Balancer with Auto Scaling configured across multiple Availability Zones for availability.
Host the SPA files in an Amazon S3 bucket with static website hosting enabled and place Amazon CloudFront in front of S3 for global CDN distribution and HTTPS support.

explanation: S3 static hosting with CloudFront is the most cost-effective architecture for static SPAs. S3 provides durable object storage at cents per GB, and CloudFront provides global low-latency delivery with HTTPS. No compute instances are needed. Option C (EC2 with Nginx) is significantly more expensive than S3 for serving static files. Option B (Amplify) is a managed service with higher cost than raw S3+CloudFront for simple static hosting. Option A (EFS with EC2) adds unnecessary compute and storage complexity for static files.

stem: A company needs to allow an application running on Amazon ECS to publish messages to an Amazon SNS topic and write logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Following the principle of least privilege, which IAM configuration should be used?

options.text: Store SNS access keys and CloudWatch API keys in AWS Secrets Manager and configure the ECS task definition to inject them as environment variables for the container application.
Create an ECS task role with permissions for sns:Publish to the specific topic ARN and logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents to the specific log group ARN for the container.
Create an ECS task execution role with permissions for sns:Publish to the specific topic ARN and logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents to the specific log group ARN.
Attach the AWS managed policy AmazonSNSFullAccess and CloudWatchLogsFullAccess to the ECS task role to provide complete access to both SNS and CloudWatch Logs services.

explanation: The ECS task role (not task execution role) provides permissions for the application container. Scoping permissions to specific resource ARNs follows least privilege. Option C (task execution role) is used by the ECS agent for pulling images and logging, not by the application container itself. Option D (full access managed policies) violates least privilege by granting access to all SNS topics and CloudWatch log groups. Option A (access keys in Secrets Manager) is unnecessary when IAM roles provide temporary credentials automatically.

stem: A company needs to design a highly available architecture for a backend service that processes API requests. The service must maintain 99.99% availability and handle up to 50,000 requests per second. Which architecture provides this level of availability with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy the service on Amazon ECS with Fargate across three Availability Zones with ECS Service Auto Scaling based on target tracking of ALBRequestCountPerTarget metric.
Deploy the service on a single large EC2 instance with enhanced monitoring and auto-recovery enabled to automatically restart the instance on hardware failure detection.
Deploy the service on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer with health checks and cross-zone load balancing.
Deploy the service as an AWS Lambda function behind Amazon API Gateway with provisioned concurrency configured to handle 50,000 concurrent requests without cold starts.

explanation: ECS on Fargate across three Availability Zones delivers 99.99% availability through automatic task replacement with no servers to patch, size, or manage, and target tracking on request count per target scales the service to sustain 50,000 requests per second. Option B (single large EC2 instance with auto-recovery) is a single point of failure and cannot achieve 99.99% availability. Option C (EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an ALB) meets the availability target but requires managing, patching, and right-sizing EC2 instances, adding operational overhead. Option D (Lambda behind API Gateway) faces the default API Gateway account throttle of 10,000 requests per second and very large Lambda concurrency quotas, both requiring limit increases and quota management at this scale.

stem: A company uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ deployment. The database stores 2 TB of data with 500 GB of automated backups. The company notices that RDS storage costs are higher than expected. Which storage optimization reduces costs?

options.text: Switch from Provisioned IOPS (io1) storage to General Purpose (gp3) storage if the database workload does not require consistently high IOPS beyond the gp3 baseline of 3,000.
Switch from Multi-AZ to Single-AZ deployment to eliminate the standby instance storage cost, and rely on automated backups for recovery in case of an AZ failure event.
Enable RDS storage auto scaling with a maximum storage threshold to prevent over-provisioning and allow the database to start with a smaller initial storage allocation.
Disable automated backups to eliminate the backup storage charges and instead create manual snapshots on a weekly schedule to reduce the total backup storage volume.

explanation: Provisioned IOPS (io1) storage costs significantly more than General Purpose (gp3) storage. If the workload does not require more than gp3's baseline 3,000 IOPS, switching to gp3 can reduce storage costs by 50% or more. Option D (disabling backups) eliminates recovery capability and is a dangerous practice for production databases. Option B (Single-AZ) eliminates high availability, risking extended downtime during AZ failures. Option C (auto scaling) prevents over-provisioning but does not reduce the per-GB storage cost.

stem: A company deploys applications across multiple AWS accounts and needs to centrally manage all security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and other security services. Which service provides a unified security findings dashboard?

options.text: Enable AWS Config across all accounts with a Config aggregator in the management account to collect all security-related configuration compliance findings centrally.
Enable Amazon CloudWatch across all accounts and create a centralized CloudWatch dashboard that displays custom metrics from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie findings.
Enable AWS Security Hub across all accounts with a delegated administrator to aggregate findings from all integrated security services into a centralized compliance dashboard.
Enable AWS CloudTrail with an organization trail and use Amazon Athena queries on the centralized CloudTrail logs to identify security findings from all integrated services.

explanation: AWS Security Hub aggregates, organizes, and prioritizes findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and other AWS and third-party security services into a centralized dashboard. It provides automated compliance checks and cross-account visibility. Option B (CloudWatch) is a monitoring service, not a security findings aggregator. Option A (Config aggregator) tracks configuration compliance but does not aggregate findings from security services. Option D (CloudTrail with Athena) logs API calls but does not provide a security findings dashboard.

stem: A company uses Amazon S3 to store critical business documents. The company needs to ensure that accidentally deleted documents can be recovered and that all document versions are retained. Which S3 configuration provides this protection?

options.text: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication to a backup bucket in another Region to maintain a copy of all documents that can be used for recovery if originals are deleted.
Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance mode with a 365-day retention period to prevent any document deletion and maintain all versions for the specified retention window.
Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket, which preserves all versions of objects including when they are deleted (via delete markers) allowing recovery of any previous version.
Configure AWS Backup with a daily backup plan for the S3 bucket to create daily recovery points that can be used to restore deleted documents from backup copies.

explanation: S3 Versioning preserves every version of every object. When an object is deleted, S3 creates a delete marker rather than removing data. Previous versions remain accessible and recoverable. Option A (CRR) replicates deletions to the backup bucket, so deleted documents are removed from both locations. Option B (Object Lock) prevents all deletion, not just accidental deletion, which may be too restrictive for normal operations. Option D (AWS Backup) provides daily recovery points but does not retain every version of every document.

stem: A company has a monolithic application running on a single large EC2 instance. The application handles web serving, background job processing, and file processing. CPU usage spikes to 100% during background job processing, degrading web response times. Which architectural change resolves this issue?

options.text: Decouple the background job processing into a separate Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that pull jobs from an SQS queue, isolating compute from the web serving tier.
Upgrade the single EC2 instance to a larger instance type with more CPU cores to provide sufficient compute capacity for both web serving and background processing simultaneously.
Enable EC2 burstable performance credits on the instance by switching to a t3 instance type to handle CPU spikes using burst credits accumulated during low-usage periods.
Configure CPU-based process priority on the EC2 instance using nice/renice commands to give web serving processes higher priority than background processing tasks.

explanation: Decoupling background jobs to a separate tier with SQS eliminates CPU contention between web serving and job processing. Each tier scales independently based on its own workload characteristics. Option B (larger instance) is a temporary fix that does not address the contention issue as workloads grow. Option D (process priority) reduces background job throughput and does not provide additional compute capacity. Option C (burstable instances) only helps if spikes are infrequent and burst credits are available.

stem: A company transfers 5 TB of data daily between AWS services in the same Region. The data flows from S3 to EC2 instances for processing, then back to S3, and finally to Redshift. The company wants to minimize data transfer costs. Which statement about same-Region data transfer pricing is correct?

options.text: All data transfers between AWS services within the same Region incur a flat rate of $0.01 per GB regardless of the direction or the specific services involved in the transfer.
Data transfer from S3 to EC2 within the same AZ is free but cross-AZ transfers incur charges, so placing EC2 instances in the same AZ as S3 minimizes transfer costs.
Data transfer from S3 to EC2 within the same Region is free, EC2 to S3 is free, and S3 to Redshift using COPY command is free, so there are no data transfer charges.
Data transfer from S3 to EC2 incurs standard data transfer out charges, but using S3 VPC gateway endpoints eliminates these charges by routing traffic privately.

explanation: Data transfer between S3 and EC2 in the same Region is free. Data transfer from EC2 to S3 in the same Region is free. COPY from S3 to Redshift in the same Region is free. All these intra-Region transfers between services incur no data transfer charges. Option B incorrectly implies S3-to-EC2 has cross-AZ charges (S3 is a Regional service). Option A states an incorrect flat rate. Option D incorrectly describes S3-to-EC2 transfer pricing.

stem: A company needs to implement a defense-in-depth network security architecture for a VPC hosting a web application. Which TWO layers of network security should be implemented? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Deploy AWS Network Firewall in the VPC with stateful inspection rules that examine traffic at the packet level and block malicious traffic based on threat intelligence feeds.
Enable VPC Flow Logs on all subnets and analyze the logs with Amazon Athena to identify suspicious traffic patterns and generate reports for the security team review.
Configure security groups on all EC2 instances and load balancers to allow only required inbound ports and protocols, using the principle of least privilege for network access.
Enable Amazon Inspector network assessments to scan all EC2 instances for network exposure and open ports, generating findings for remediation of network security gaps.

explanation: Network Firewall provides deep packet inspection at the VPC level (first defense layer), while security groups provide instance-level stateful filtering (second defense layer). Together they implement defense-in-depth at different network layers. Option B (VPC Flow Logs with Athena) is monitoring, not an active security control. Option D (Inspector) identifies vulnerabilities but does not actively block traffic.

stem: A company runs a batch processing system that creates hundreds of temporary EC2 instances daily. Each instance processes data for 1-2 hours and then terminates. The company needs to ensure that processing results from failed instances can be recovered. Which strategy protects against data loss?

options.text: Configure the instances to write intermediate results to Amazon S3 at regular checkpoints, allowing failed instances to be replaced with new instances that resume from the last checkpoint.
Attach an Amazon EBS volume to each instance with deletion protection enabled to preserve the data volume when the instance terminates or fails during processing.
Store processing results in the EC2 instance store for fastest I/O performance and configure CloudWatch alarms to create EBS snapshots before instances are scheduled to terminate.
Deploy the instances in a placement group with enhanced networking enabled to reduce the likelihood of hardware failures and ensure consistent network performance during processing.

explanation: Writing checkpoints to S3 provides durable storage independent of any instance. If an instance fails, a new instance reads the last checkpoint from S3 and resumes processing, preventing data loss and minimizing rework. Option B (EBS with delete protection) prevents volume deletion on termination but if the instance crashes, data may be inconsistent. Option C (instance store with snapshots) loses data instantly on failure since instance store is ephemeral and snapshots cannot be created fast enough. Option D (placement groups) reduces failure probability but does not protect data when failures do occur.

stem: A company builds an application that needs to maintain WebSocket connections for real-time chat between users. The application must handle 100,000 concurrent WebSocket connections. Which AWS service should serve as the WebSocket endpoint?

options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with WebSocket support in front of EC2 instances running a Node.js WebSocket server to handle persistent connections with sticky session routing.
Use Amazon API Gateway WebSocket APIs to manage WebSocket connections with Lambda functions handling connect, disconnect, and message events for up to 100,000 concurrent connections.
Use Amazon CloudFront with WebSocket protocol support to terminate WebSocket connections at edge locations and route messages to the origin Lambda functions for processing.
Use a Network Load Balancer with TCP listeners to maintain persistent WebSocket connections to EC2 instances running a custom WebSocket server for real-time message delivery.

explanation: API Gateway WebSocket APIs provide a serverless, managed WebSocket endpoint that scales to handle concurrent connections. Lambda handles connection lifecycle and message routing without managing infrastructure. Option A (ALB with EC2) requires managing WebSocket server infrastructure and connection state across instances. Option C (CloudFront) supports WebSocket passthrough but does not manage WebSocket connections or message routing. Option D (NLB with EC2) maintains TCP connections but requires managing the WebSocket server infrastructure.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all Amazon S3 object access is logged for security auditing. The logs must capture who accessed which objects, when, and whether the request was successful. Compliance rules require guaranteed log delivery and support for log file integrity validation. Which solution should be implemented?

options.text: Enable S3 server access logging on each bucket with log delivery to a centralized logging bucket, capturing requester, object key, timestamp, and HTTP status for each request.
Enable S3 Storage Lens with advanced metrics to capture bucket-level access statistics and request counts aggregated by Region, storage class, and requester account.
Enable S3 Event Notifications for all event types and route them to an SQS queue, then process the notifications with Lambda to build a custom access audit log in DynamoDB.
Enable CloudTrail S3 data events for all buckets in the account to record object-level API calls including GetObject, PutObject, and DeleteObject with request metadata.

explanation: CloudTrail S3 data events record object-level API calls such as GetObject, PutObject, and DeleteObject with the caller identity, source IP, timestamp, and response status, and CloudTrail provides reliable delivery with log file integrity validation, meeting the compliance requirements.
