Option A (server access logging) does capture requester, object key, timestamp, and HTTP status, but delivery is best effort with no completeness guarantee and no log file integrity validation, making it unsuitable as the sole security audit trail. Option B (Storage Lens) provides aggregated storage and activity metrics, not per-request audit records. Option C (event notifications) does not fire for read requests such as GetObject and requires building custom processing to assemble an audit log.

stem: A company has an application that writes to an Amazon SQS queue. Multiple consumer instances process messages from the queue. The company needs to ensure that messages are processed in the exact order they were sent, grouped by customer ID. Which configuration meets this requirement?

options.text: Use an SQS FIFO queue with a single message group ID for all messages to enforce strict global ordering across all customers and all consumer instances.
Use separate SQS standard queues for each customer ID and configure the producer to route messages to the customer-specific queue for independent ordered processing.
Use an SQS FIFO queue with the customer ID as the message group ID to maintain ordering within each customer group while allowing parallel processing across different customers.
Use an SQS standard queue with a sequence number attribute in each message and configure the consumer to sort messages by sequence number before processing them.

explanation: FIFO queues with customer ID as message group ID guarantee ordering within each customer group. Different customer groups can be processed in parallel by different consumers, providing both ordering and scalability. Option D (standard queue with sorting) cannot guarantee delivery order and consumer sorting is unreliable. Option A (single group ID) enforces global ordering which limits throughput to a single consumer. Option B (separate queues) creates management complexity with potentially millions of queues.

stem: A company needs to migrate a 50 TB Oracle data warehouse to AWS. The company wants to use a fully managed cloud-native data warehouse service. The existing queries use complex SQL with window functions, CTEs, and multi-table joins. Which target service should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Athena with data stored in S3 in Parquet format to run serverless SQL queries, migrating data using AWS DataSync to transfer files from the Oracle export to S3.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with Global Secondary Indexes and PartiQL for SQL-compatible queries, migrating data using DMS with table transformations to fit the DynamoDB data model.
Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with large instance types to run the complex analytical queries, migrating the Oracle schema and data using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool and DMS.
Use Amazon Redshift with RA3 nodes to leverage columnar storage and massively parallel processing for complex SQL analytics, migrating data using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool and DMS.

explanation: Amazon Redshift is a purpose-built cloud data warehouse with columnar storage, MPP architecture, and full SQL support including window functions, CTEs, and complex joins. RA3 nodes provide managed storage up to 128 TB. Option C (Aurora) is an OLTP database not optimized for large analytical workloads. Option A (Athena) may be too slow for complex 50 TB warehouse queries compared to Redshift's dedicated compute. Option B (DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database that does not support complex SQL analytics.

stem: A company uses Java-based AWS Lambda functions in a VPC that are triggered by Amazon API Gateway and connect to Amazon RDS through RDS Proxy. Each cold start takes 5 seconds because of Spring framework and dependency initialization. Provisioned concurrency eliminates cold starts but costs $50/month. Which alternative reduces cold start impact at lower cost?

options.text: Move the Lambda functions outside the VPC and connect to the RDS Proxy endpoint over the public internet, avoiding VPC networking overhead while retaining connection pooling.
Enable Lambda SnapStart on the functions so new environments resume from a snapshot of the initialized runtime, cutting cold starts to under a second at no charge for Java.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke each function every 5 minutes with a warmup event so execution environments are never reclaimed and recycled by the service.
Increase the Lambda memory allocation to the maximum 10 GB so the proportionally higher CPU allocation speeds up framework and dependency initialization on every cold start.

explanation: Lambda SnapStart snapshots the execution environment after initialization and resumes new environments from the cached snapshot, cutting Java framework startup from seconds to sub-second, and SnapStart adds no charge for Java runtimes (it is priced only for Python and .NET). Database connections are not preserved across restore, but they are re-established quickly through RDS Proxy's connection pool. Option A (move outside the VPC) is not possible because RDS Proxy endpoints are reachable only from within the VPC and cannot be made publicly accessible. Option C (scheduled warmup invocations) adds recurring invocation cost and does not stop Lambda from reclaiming environments or creating new cold environments under concurrent load. Option D (maximum memory) sharply increases per-invocation cost and still leaves multi-second framework initialization on every cold start.

stem: A company is implementing a zero-trust architecture for microservices that run on Amazon EKS in a VPC. All traffic between microservices must be mutually authenticated and encrypted, even within the VPC. Which solution enforces mutual TLS (mTLS) between services?

options.text: Configure Network ACLs with strict allow rules for each service-to-service communication path and enable VPC Flow Logs to monitor all traffic between services.
Deploy AWS PrivateLink endpoints for each microservice and configure endpoint policies to restrict which services can connect, using IAM policies for authentication.
Deploy an Istio service mesh on the EKS cluster with Envoy sidecar proxies enforcing mutual TLS between all services, using AWS Private CA to issue service certificates.
Configure security groups on each service to allow traffic only from specific security group IDs and enable VPC encryption in transit for all inter-instance network traffic.

explanation: An Istio service mesh injects Envoy sidecar proxies that enforce mutual TLS, so both client and server present certificates before any connection is accepted, providing workload identity, authentication, and encryption at the application layer. AWS Private CA integrates through cert-manager to issue and rotate the service certificates. Option A (NACLs with Flow Logs) provides network-level filtering and traffic monitoring only, with no authentication or encryption. Option B (PrivateLink endpoints) provides private connectivity with IAM-based endpoint policies but does not perform certificate-based mutual TLS between services. Option D (security groups) filters at the network level and cannot authenticate workloads or encrypt application traffic between services.

stem: A company runs a serverless application using Lambda, DynamoDB, and S3. The company needs to implement distributed tracing to identify performance bottlenecks across all service components. Which service provides end-to-end distributed tracing?

options.text: Enable AWS X-Ray tracing on Lambda functions, DynamoDB, and S3 to capture request traces across all service components and visualize the service map with latency analysis.
Enable Amazon CloudWatch ServiceLens to collect metrics from Lambda, DynamoDB, and S3 and correlate them in a single dashboard with trace-level performance analysis.
Enable CloudWatch Logs Insights across all services and run queries to correlate request IDs across Lambda, DynamoDB, and S3 log groups for manual trace reconstruction.
Deploy Amazon Managed Grafana with the AWS data source plugin to create custom dashboards that visualize performance metrics from Lambda, DynamoDB, and S3 in one view.

explanation: AWS X-Ray provides distributed tracing across Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, and other AWS services. It traces requests end-to-end, generates service maps, and identifies latency bottlenecks. Option B (CloudWatch ServiceLens) uses X-Ray under the hood and does not add independent tracing capability. Option C (Logs Insights) requires manual correlation and does not provide automatic trace visualization. Option D (Managed Grafana) provides dashboarding but does not perform distributed tracing.

stem: A company needs to deploy a relational database that automatically scales both compute and storage based on workload demand. The database must be MySQL-compatible and handle unpredictable traffic patterns ranging from near-zero to thousands of transactions per second. Which database configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy Amazon RDS for MySQL with a burstable t3.medium instance type and storage auto scaling enabled to handle variable workloads with burst CPU credits for peak periods.
Deploy Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 with a minimum capacity of 0.5 ACU and maximum of 128 ACU, providing MySQL compatibility with automatic compute scaling based on demand.
Deploy Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity mode using the PartiQL SQL-compatible interface for relational-style queries that scale automatically with traffic patterns.
Deploy Amazon Aurora MySQL provisioned with Auto Scaling read replicas that scale out during high traffic and scale in during low traffic to adjust read capacity dynamically.

explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 automatically scales compute capacity (ACUs) in fine-grained increments based on actual database load. It handles near-zero to thousands of TPS seamlessly with MySQL compatibility. Storage scales automatically. Option A (RDS t3) has fixed compute capacity and burst credits deplete under sustained load. Option D (Aurora provisioned with replicas) scales reads but not the writer, and does not scale down to near-zero. Option C (DynamoDB) is not a relational database and PartiQL has limited relational query capabilities.

stem: A company runs a microservices application on Amazon EKS. The company discovers that many pods request more CPU and memory than they actually use, leading to low cluster utilization (20% average). Which Kubernetes feature helps right-size pod resource requests?

options.text: Implement the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to reduce the number of EKS worker nodes when cluster utilization drops below a threshold, right-sizing the underlying infrastructure.
Implement Kubernetes resource quotas per namespace to limit the total CPU and memory that each team's pods can request, preventing excessive resource reservation.
Implement the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) to scale the number of pod replicas based on CPU utilization and reduce the total number of running pods during low traffic.
Implement the Kubernetes Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA) to automatically adjust pod CPU and memory requests based on historical usage data and reduce over-provisioning.

explanation: VPA analyzes actual pod resource usage and automatically adjusts CPU and memory requests to match real consumption, eliminating over-provisioning at the pod level. This increases cluster utilization from 20% to a healthier level. Option C (HPA) scales the number of pods, not the resource requests per pod. Option B (resource quotas) limits maximum resources but does not help individual pods right-size their requests. Option A (Cluster Autoscaler) adjusts node count based on pending pods but does not address pod-level over-provisioning.

stem: A company has a VPC with a CIDR block of 10.0.0.0/16. The company needs to add more IP addresses because the current CIDR is running out. The company cannot change the existing CIDR block. Which solution adds more IP address space to the VPC?

options.text: Associate an additional secondary IPv4 CIDR block (e.g., 10.1.0.0/16) with the existing VPC to extend the available IP address range without recreating the VPC or its resources.
Enable IPv6 on the existing VPC and assign IPv6 addresses to all resources, effectively doubling the available address space without changing the IPv4 CIDR configuration.
Create a new VPC with a larger CIDR block (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8), set up VPC peering with the existing VPC, and gradually migrate resources from the old VPC to the new one.
Submit a support request to AWS to expand the existing VPC CIDR block from /16 to /8, which allows AWS to modify the CIDR range in place without impacting running resources.

explanation: VPCs support adding secondary CIDR blocks (up to 5 IPv4 CIDRs per VPC) without affecting existing resources. New subnets can be created in the additional CIDR range. Option C (new VPC with migration) is disruptive and requires moving all resources. Option B (IPv6) provides a different address family but does not add more IPv4 addresses which existing applications may require. Option D (modifying existing CIDR) is not possible in AWS; CIDR blocks cannot be resized after creation.

stem: A company runs a stateless API on AWS Lambda behind API Gateway. The API processes 100 requests per second on average with spikes to 1,000 requests per second. Response times must remain under 200ms. Which Lambda configuration ensures consistent performance during traffic spikes?

options.text: Configure API Gateway with a response caching strategy using a 60-second TTL to serve repeated requests from cache and reduce the number of Lambda invocations during spikes.
Configure Lambda reserved concurrency at 1,000 to guarantee capacity during spikes and set the function timeout to 200ms to enforce the response time requirement.
Configure Lambda with maximum memory (10 GB) allocation to get proportionally more CPU power and faster execution, reducing response times during both normal and spike traffic.
Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency at 1,000 to keep execution environments warm and eliminate cold starts during traffic spikes, ensuring consistent sub-200ms response times.

explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps 1,000 execution environments initialized and warm, eliminating cold starts that would cause response times to exceed 200ms during spikes. This ensures consistent performance. Option C (maximum memory) reduces execution time but does not eliminate cold start initialization delay. Option B (reserved concurrency) guarantees capacity but does not prevent cold starts when scaling up. Option A (caching) only helps for cacheable responses and does not address unique request processing.

stem: A company needs to store and serve 10 million user profile images averaging 500 KB each. Images are uploaded once and read hundreds of times. The service must handle 50,000 image retrievals per second globally with low latency. Which architecture provides this performance?

options.text: Store images in Amazon S3 with S3 Transfer Acceleration enabled and configure the application to generate presigned URLs with 24-hour expiration for each image retrieval request.
Store images as binary data in Amazon DynamoDB with DAX caching enabled to serve reads from the in-memory cache for sub-millisecond retrieval of frequently accessed profile images.
Store images in Amazon EFS and serve them from EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB, with multiple Availability Zones for availability and request distribution.
Store images in Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront CDN in front, using S3 as the origin and CloudFront edge caching for high-frequency reads from globally distributed edge locations.

explanation: S3 provides highly durable object storage for 10M images (5 TB total). CloudFront caches frequently accessed images at 400+ edge locations globally, easily handling 50,000+ requests per second with low latency. Option C (EFS with EC2) is expensive and cannot match CloudFront's global edge performance. Option B (DynamoDB with DAX) has a 400 KB item size limit, too small for 500 KB images. Option A (S3 with Transfer Acceleration) is for uploads, not optimizing download performance, and presigned URLs do not improve read performance.

stem: A company runs a CI/CD pipeline that builds and tests code using Amazon EC2 instances. Build jobs run for 15-30 minutes each, with 50 builds per day during business hours and very few at night. The build instances currently use On-Demand pricing. Which approach minimizes build compute costs?

options.text: Use EC2 On-Demand instances with Auto Scaling configured to launch instances only when builds are queued and terminate them after build completion to reduce idle time.
Purchase Reserved Instances for the build instance type with a 1-year commitment to receive discounted hourly pricing on the instances used for the CI/CD pipeline.
Switch build jobs to AWS CodeBuild which provides managed build environments billed per build-minute, eliminating idle compute costs between builds during business hours.
Use EC2 Spot Instances for build jobs with a Spot Fleet across multiple instance types, accepting occasional interruptions and retrying failed builds automatically.

explanation: CodeBuild provides per-build-minute billing, so you pay only for actual build time (50 builds x ~22 min = ~1,100 minutes/day). No idle compute costs between builds. This is significantly cheaper than running EC2 instances. Option D (Spot Instances) saves money but build interruptions require retry logic and may delay deployments. Option B (Reserved Instances) pays for 24/7 capacity when builds run only during business hours. Option A (Auto Scaling) still has startup/shutdown overhead and minimum billing periods.

stem: A company needs to establish private connectivity between its VPC and AWS services like S3, DynamoDB, SQS, and SNS without any traffic traversing the internet. Some services support gateway endpoints and others require interface endpoints. Which combination of endpoints covers all four services?

options.text: Create gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB (free, route-table based) and interface endpoints for SQS and SNS (powered by PrivateLink with private IP addresses).
Create gateway endpoints for all four services (S3, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS) since all AWS services support gateway endpoints for free traffic routing within the VPC.
Create interface endpoints for all four services (S3, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS) using PrivateLink to provide private IP addresses in the VPC for consistent endpoint configuration.
Create a single VPC endpoint for all four services using a shared PrivateLink configuration that provides private connectivity to multiple AWS services through one endpoint.

explanation: S3 and DynamoDB support gateway endpoints (free, configured in route tables). SQS and SNS require interface endpoints (PrivateLink). This combination provides private connectivity for all four services. Option C (all interface endpoints) works but uses paid interface endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB when free gateway endpoints are available. Option B (all gateway endpoints) is incorrect because SQS and SNS only support interface endpoints. Option D (single shared endpoint) does not exist; each service requires its own endpoint.

stem: A company operates an e-commerce application where order processing involves multiple steps: payment validation, inventory check, order creation, and notification sending. If any step fails, all previous steps must be compensated (reversed). Which pattern should be implemented?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions with a saga pattern implementation, where each step has a corresponding compensation step that runs if a subsequent step fails to roll back changes.
Use a distributed two-phase commit protocol implemented across all services using DynamoDB transactions to ensure atomicity across all four order processing steps.
Use Amazon SQS with separate queues for each step and dead-letter queues for failed steps, relying on manual intervention to reverse completed steps when failures occur.
Use Amazon EventBridge with event rules for each step and configure error destinations that route failure events to Lambda functions for manual notification and investigation.

explanation: Step Functions implements the saga pattern with Catch states that trigger compensation steps when failures occur. Each step can have a defined reverse action. The workflow ensures all compensations run in the correct order. Option C (SQS with DLQ) does not provide automatic compensation and requires manual intervention. Option B (two-phase commit) does not work across distributed services like payment gateways and notification systems. Option D (EventBridge with error routing) only detects failures but does not orchestrate compensating transactions.

stem: A company runs an application that needs to process 500 GB of data in Amazon S3 using Apache Spark. The processing runs daily and takes approximately 2 hours. The company wants a managed solution that minimizes operational overhead, runs its existing open-source Apache Spark application code unchanged, and lets the team pin a specific Apache Spark release version. Which service should be used?

options.text: Use Amazon EMR with a transient cluster that starts daily, runs the Spark job, and terminates after completion, with S3 as the input/output storage for data persistence.
Use Amazon EC2 instances with Apache Spark installed in an Auto Scaling group that processes the data from S3 and terminates instances after the daily job completes.
Use Amazon EMR Serverless with Apache Spark application type to submit jobs without managing clusters, paying only for the compute resources consumed during the 2-hour processing.
Use AWS Glue with PySpark ETL jobs that read from and write to S3, leveraging the serverless Spark runtime and automatic scaling without managing any Spark infrastructure.

explanation: EMR Serverless runs open-source Apache Spark releases with no cluster to manage: the team selects the EMR release matching its required Spark version, submits jobs with its existing Spark code unchanged, and pays only for resources consumed during the 2-hour run. Option A (EMR transient cluster) runs open-source Spark but requires configuring, sizing, and managing cluster lifecycle, adding operational overhead. Option B (EC2 with Spark) requires installing and operating the entire Spark stack. Option D (AWS Glue) is serverless but uses Glue's own runtime, where the Spark version is tied to the chosen Glue version and jobs follow Glue conventions, so existing open-source Spark code cannot be guaranteed to run unchanged against a pinned Spark release.

stem: A company uses Amazon EBS gp2 volumes for all its EC2 instances. The company has noticed that many volumes are larger than 1 TB but have low IOPS requirements (under 3,000 IOPS). The company wants to reduce EBS storage costs. Which change should be made?

options.text: Enable EBS Elastic Volumes to dynamically resize gp2 volumes down to the minimum required size, reducing the per-GB charges for over-provisioned storage volumes.
Migrate the gp2 volumes to gp3 volumes which provide 3,000 baseline IOPS regardless of volume size, allowing the same performance at a lower per-GB storage cost.
Migrate the gp2 volumes to io2 Block Express volumes which provide the highest IOPS performance and lower per-IOPS pricing for volumes requiring consistent performance.
Migrate the gp2 volumes to st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD) volumes which provide lower per-GB cost for large volumes with sequential read/write access patterns.

explanation: gp3 provides 3,000 baseline IOPS regardless of volume size at a lower per-GB price than gp2 (20% cheaper). For volumes over 1 TB with low IOPS needs, gp3 provides the same or better performance at lower cost. Option C (io2) is more expensive than gp3 and designed for high-IOPS workloads. Option D (st1) only supports sequential workloads and cannot serve as boot volumes. Option A (Elastic Volumes resizing) reduces volume size but does not change the per-GB pricing of gp2.

stem: A company has a Lambda function that processes events from multiple sources including API Gateway, SQS, and S3. The function needs different IAM permissions depending on the event source. The company wants to follow the principle of least privilege. Which approach should be used?

options.text: Create a single Lambda function with a role that has no permissions and use resource-based policies on the downstream services to grant access based on the Lambda function ARN.
Create a single Lambda function with an execution role that has the union of all permissions needed for all three event sources, since a Lambda function can only have one role.
Create a single Lambda function that assumes different IAM roles at runtime based on the event source, using STS AssumeRole to get source-specific temporary credentials.
Create three separate Lambda functions with dedicated execution roles for each event source, granting only the minimum permissions required for each function's specific workload.

explanation: Separate Lambda functions with dedicated roles ensure each function has only the permissions it needs for its specific event source, following least privilege. This prevents a function triggered by S3 from having permissions it only needs when triggered by API Gateway. Option B (single function with all permissions) violates least privilege by granting unnecessary permissions. Option A (resource-based policies only) does not work for all AWS actions and is not a substitute for execution role permissions. Option C (runtime AssumeRole) adds complexity and latency and still requires the base role to have AssumeRole permissions.

stem: A company runs a critical application with an RPO of zero (no data loss) and an RTO of 5 minutes. The application uses Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Which Aurora configuration meets both the RPO and RTO requirements?

options.text: Deploy Aurora with automated backups and point-in-time recovery enabled with a 5-minute backup retention granularity to restore the database within the required RTO window.
Deploy Aurora Global Database with a secondary Region for cross-Region failover with typical replication lag of under 1 second for near-zero RPO and fast Regional recovery.
Deploy Aurora with a single writer instance and enable Aurora Backtrack to rewind the database to any second within the configured backtrack window for instant recovery.
Deploy Aurora with Multi-AZ read replicas in the same Region with automatic failover priority configured, where the replica promotion maintains all committed transactions.

explanation: Aurora Multi-AZ with read replicas uses shared storage with synchronous replication within the cluster, ensuring zero data loss (RPO=0). Automatic failover promotes a replica within 30 seconds, well within the 5-minute RTO. Option B (Global Database) has sub-second replication lag, which means RPO is not strictly zero. Option A (PITR from backups) takes longer than 5 minutes to restore and has second-level RPO, not zero. Option C (Backtrack) is for MySQL only and is used for logical errors, not instance failures.

stem: A company needs to build an API that aggregates data from three microservices into a single response. Each microservice has its own REST API. The client application needs only specific fields from each service. Which API approach minimizes over-fetching and simplifies the client integration?

options.text: Build an Application Load Balancer with path-based routing that directs clients to each microservice separately and let the client combine the three responses on its own.
Build an AWS AppSync GraphQL API with resolvers that query each microservice in parallel and return only the fields requested by the client in a single GraphQL response.
Build a Lambda function behind API Gateway that makes HTTP calls to all three microservices, aggregates the responses, and returns the combined data as a single API response.
Build an API Gateway REST API that calls all three microservices sequentially using VTL mapping templates and combines the responses into a single JSON response body.

explanation: AppSync GraphQL allows clients to specify exactly which fields they need, eliminating over-fetching. Resolvers query microservices in parallel and return a single aggregated response with only requested fields. Option D (API Gateway with VTL) is complex and sequential, increasing latency. Option C (Lambda aggregation) works but the client still receives all fields and sequential HTTP calls add latency. Option A (ALB path routing) requires three client requests and client-side aggregation.

stem: A company has a VPC with a NAT Gateway processing 10 TB of data per month. Most of the traffic is to Amazon S3 for log uploads. The NAT Gateway data processing charges are $450/month. How can the company eliminate most of this cost?

options.text: Replace the NAT Gateway with a NAT instance on a t3.micro EC2 instance to reduce the per-GB data processing charge while maintaining outbound internet connectivity.
Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration for the log bucket to optimize the upload path and reduce the amount of data traversing the NAT Gateway through compression.
Move the EC2 instances from private subnets to public subnets with public IP addresses to access S3 directly over the internet without going through the NAT Gateway.
Create an S3 VPC gateway endpoint and update the private subnet route tables to route S3 traffic through the gateway endpoint, bypassing the NAT Gateway for S3 traffic.

explanation: S3 VPC gateway endpoints route S3 traffic directly from private subnets to S3 without going through the NAT Gateway. Gateway endpoints are free, eliminating the $0.045/GB NAT Gateway processing charge for S3 traffic. Option A (NAT instance) still charges for data transfer and has limited bandwidth. Option B (Transfer Acceleration) adds cost and does not bypass the NAT Gateway. Option C (public subnets) exposes instances to the internet, violating security best practices.

stem: A company deploys a containerized application on Amazon ECS Fargate. The containers need to access secrets stored in AWS Secrets Manager at startup. The company does not want secret values stored in plaintext in the task definition or baked into container images. Which approach securely injects secrets into the container?

options.text: Store secrets as encrypted environment variables in the ECS task definition using KMS encryption, and configure the container runtime to decrypt them at launch time.
Reference the Secrets Manager secret ARN in the ECS task definition's secrets property to inject the secret value into the container environment at task launch time automatically.
Use the AWS SDK in the container entrypoint script to call Secrets Manager GetSecretValue at startup, using the task role credentials to authenticate the API call.
Store secrets in an encrypted S3 object and configure the ECS task definition to download the object at startup using a pre-signed URL embedded in the task definition.

explanation: ECS integrates natively with Secrets Manager through the task definition's secrets property: ECS fetches the secret value at task launch and injects it into the container, while the task definition stores only the secret's ARN, never the plaintext value. Option A (encrypted environment variables) describes a mechanism ECS does not provide, and it still places secret material in the task definition where readers of the definition can access it. Option C (SDK call in entrypoint) works but requires writing and maintaining custom retrieval code in every container image. Option D (S3 pre-signed URL) embeds a usable download URL in the task definition, exposing the secret to anyone who can read the task definition.

stem: A company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS management. The company needs to route traffic to different endpoints based on the health of each endpoint and the geographic location of users. If the nearest endpoint is unhealthy, traffic should go to the next nearest healthy endpoint. Which routing configuration achieves this?

options.text: Configure Route 53 latency-based routing with health checks on each endpoint to route users to the lowest-latency endpoint and failover to the next lowest if unhealthy.
Configure Route 53 multivalue answer routing with health checks on each endpoint to return multiple healthy IP addresses and let the client choose the nearest endpoint.
Configure Route 53 geolocation routing with health checks on each endpoint to route users to the geographically closest endpoint and failover to another location if unhealthy.
Configure Route 53 weighted routing with equal weights on all endpoints and health checks to distribute traffic evenly and remove unhealthy endpoints from rotation.

explanation: Latency-based routing directs users to the endpoint with the lowest network latency (effectively the nearest). Health checks automatically remove unhealthy endpoints, and Route 53 routes to the next lowest-latency healthy endpoint. Option C (geolocation) routes based on user location but requires explicit geographic mappings and may not have a perfect fallback chain. Option D (weighted) distributes traffic evenly, not based on proximity. Option B (multivalue answer) returns multiple IPs but leaves endpoint selection to the client.

stem: A company has a web application that generates PDF reports on demand. Each report takes 30-60 seconds to generate and the application receives 200 concurrent report requests during peak hours. Users currently wait for the report to be generated before receiving a response. Which architecture improves the user experience?

options.text: Scale up the EC2 instances to a larger instance type with more CPU to generate reports faster and reduce the wait time for users from 30-60 seconds to under 10 seconds.
Deploy additional EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group to handle 200 concurrent requests and increase the ALB timeout to 120 seconds to prevent gateway timeout errors.
Pre-generate all possible reports on a nightly schedule using AWS Batch and store them in S3, serving pre-generated PDFs instantly when users request them during business hours.
Accept the report request and return a job ID immediately, queue the request in SQS, process with Lambda, store the PDF in S3, and notify the user via WebSocket when ready.

explanation: Asynchronous processing returns immediately with a job ID, improving the user experience. SQS buffers requests, Lambda generates PDFs, S3 stores them, and WebSocket notifications alert users when ready. Users are not blocked waiting. Option A (larger instances) still makes users wait 10+ seconds. Option C (pre-generation) is wasteful if not all reports are requested and does not handle dynamic report parameters. Option B (more instances with longer timeout) still blocks users for 30-60 seconds waiting for synchronous responses.

stem: A company has a disaster recovery environment in a secondary Region that remains idle during normal operations. The DR environment includes RDS read replicas, EC2 instances in a stopped state, and S3 cross-Region replication. Which costs does the company still incur for the idle DR environment?

options.text: The company pays only for S3 storage in the DR Region since both RDS read replicas and EC2 instances can be completely stopped to eliminate all compute charges.
The company pays for the RDS read replica (running continuously for replication), S3 storage in the DR Region, and EBS volumes attached to the stopped EC2 instances.
The company pays only for S3 cross-Region replication data transfer since RDS read replicas and stopped EC2 instances incur no charges when not actively serving traffic.
The company pays for all components at the same rate as the production environment since DR resources are provisioned and available for immediate failover activation.

explanation: RDS read replicas run continuously and incur full compute and storage charges (they cannot be stopped while replicating). Stopped EC2 instances do not incur compute charges but EBS volumes still incur storage charges. S3 CRR incurs storage in the DR Region and data transfer. Option C incorrectly states read replicas incur no charges. Option D overstates costs, since stopped EC2 instances do not incur compute charges and are not billed at production rates. Option A incorrectly states read replicas can be stopped.

stem: A company needs to set up a hybrid DNS architecture where on-premises servers can resolve AWS private hosted zone records and AWS resources can resolve on-premises DNS records. The company uses AWS Direct Connect for connectivity. Which solution enables bidirectional DNS resolution?

options.text: Deploy a custom BIND DNS server on EC2 in the VPC that forwards queries to both Route 53 and the on-premises DNS server based on domain name zone configuration.
Configure the VPC DHCP options set with the on-premises DNS server IP address to allow EC2 instances to resolve on-premises records through the Direct Connect connection.
Enable DNS hostnames and DNS resolution in the VPC settings and configure the on-premises DNS server to forward AWS domain queries to the VPC DNS server at 169.254.169.253.
Configure Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints for on-premises to AWS resolution and outbound endpoints with forwarding rules for AWS to on-premises DNS resolution.

explanation: Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints allow on-premises DNS servers to forward queries to Route 53 for AWS private hosted zone resolution. Outbound endpoints with forwarding rules allow Route 53 to forward queries to on-premises DNS servers. This provides complete bidirectional hybrid DNS. Option A (custom BIND server) requires managing DNS infrastructure. Option B (DHCP options) replaces the VPC DNS resolver with on-premises, breaking Route 53 private hosted zone resolution. Option C (forwarding to VPC DNS) does not work because the VPC DNS IP is not accessible from on-premises.

stem: A company runs a web application on EC2 instances behind an ALB. The application stores data in Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ. During a recent failover, the application experienced 60 seconds of downtime because connections to the old primary were not released. Which change reduces failover impact?

options.text: Switch from RDS Multi-AZ to Aurora MySQL which provides faster failover times of approximately 30 seconds compared to RDS Multi-AZ failover of 60 to 120 seconds.
Deploy Amazon RDS Proxy between the application and the RDS instance to manage connection pooling and automatically redirect connections to the new primary during failover events.
Configure the application connection string with a shorter TCP keepalive timeout and implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient database connection failures.
Increase the RDS instance size to reduce the likelihood of failover by providing more compute and memory resources for handling peak workloads on the primary database.

explanation: RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool and automatically redirects connections to the new primary during failover, reducing application disruption. It handles connection draining from the old primary transparently. Option A (Aurora) improves failover time but does not address connection management during the failover window. Option C (keepalive and retry tuning) helps the application recover but still requires establishing new connections after failover. Option D (larger instance) reduces the likelihood of load-related failover but does nothing to shorten failover or manage connections when it occurs.

stem: A company needs to run Apache Kafka workloads on AWS. The company wants a fully managed service that provides Apache Kafka compatibility without managing brokers, ZooKeeper, or infrastructure. Which service should be used?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with the Kafka-compatible consumer API to provide similar pub/sub messaging capabilities without managing any Kafka infrastructure.
Use Amazon MSK Provisioned with a three-broker cluster in three Availability Zones, manually configuring the broker instance types and EBS storage for each broker.
Use Amazon MQ for Apache Kafka which provides a managed Kafka broker with automatic scaling, multi-AZ deployment, and integrated ZooKeeper management built in.
Use Amazon MSK Serverless which provides fully managed Apache Kafka clusters that automatically scale compute and storage capacity based on throughput and retention needs.

explanation: MSK Serverless provides fully managed Kafka without managing brokers, ZooKeeper, or storage. It automatically scales based on workload. Option A (Kinesis) is not Kafka-compatible. Option B (MSK Provisioned) requires managing broker sizing and storage. Option C (Amazon MQ) does not support Kafka; it supports ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ.

stem: A company has 100 TB of data in Amazon S3 Standard that is accessed frequently for the first 60 days and then never accessed again but must be retained for 10 years. Which lifecycle configuration provides the LOWEST total storage cost?

options.text: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering for the entire 10-year retention period to automatically move data to the most cost-effective tier based on access frequency without lifecycle rules.
Keep data in S3 Standard for 60 days, transition to S3 One Zone-IA after 60 days for single-AZ cost savings, then transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 180 days.
Keep data in S3 Standard for 60 days, transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 60 days for the remaining 10-year retention period at the lowest per-GB archival storage cost.
Keep data in S3 Standard for 60 days, transition to S3 Standard-IA after 60 days for infrequent access, then transition to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 180 days for archival.

explanation: Since data is never accessed after 60 days, moving directly to Glacier Deep Archive provides the lowest storage cost for the 10-year retention. There is no need for intermediate tiers if the data is never accessed. Option D adds unnecessary intermediate tier costs with Standard-IA and stops at Glacier Flexible Retrieval, which costs more than Deep Archive. Option A charges per-object monitoring fees and does not immediately move to the cheapest tier. Option B uses One Zone-IA, which risks data loss and adds an unnecessary intermediate tier.

stem: A company wants to enforce that all new EC2 instances in the organization must be launched from pre-approved AMIs that have been hardened by the security team. Which preventive control should be implemented?

options.text: Create a Lambda function triggered by EC2 RunInstances CloudTrail events that checks the AMI ID and terminates instances launched from non-approved AMI sources.
Create an AWS Config rule that checks the AMI ID of launched EC2 instances against a list of approved AMIs and triggers auto-remediation to terminate non-compliant instances.
Create an IAM policy attached to all roles that denies ec2:RunInstances with a condition that the ec2:ImageId does not match any AMI ID in the approved list.
Create an SCP in AWS Organizations that denies ec2:RunInstances unless the ec2:ImageId condition matches a list of pre-approved AMI IDs maintained by the security team.

explanation: SCPs provide organization-wide preventive control that cannot be overridden by individual account policies. The ec2:ImageId condition restricts launches to only approved AMIs. Option B (Config rule) is reactive and allows non-compliant instances to run briefly. Option C (IAM policy) must be attached to every role and can be removed by account admins. Option A (Lambda) is reactive and instances run before being terminated.

stem: A company uses Amazon DynamoDB global tables for a multi-Region application. The application writes to the table in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Users report occasional data conflicts when the same item is updated simultaneously in both Regions. How does DynamoDB resolve these conflicts?

options.text: DynamoDB global tables use conditional writes with optimistic concurrency to reject the second write if the item version has changed, returning a ConditionalCheckFailedException.
DynamoDB global tables use a last-writer-wins reconciliation strategy based on the timestamp of each write, automatically resolving conflicts by keeping the most recent update.
DynamoDB global tables prevent conflicts entirely by implementing distributed locking that blocks writes in one Region until the other Region confirms the previous write is replicated.
DynamoDB global tables queue conflicting writes and present them to the application for manual resolution through a conflict resolution callback configured in the table settings.

explanation: DynamoDB global tables use a last-writer-wins strategy based on the timestamp of each write. The write with the latest timestamp prevails when the same item is updated in multiple Regions simultaneously. Option D (manual conflict resolution) is not a DynamoDB feature. Option C (distributed locking) would add significant latency and is not how global tables work. Option A (conditional writes) must be explicitly implemented by the application and is not the default behavior.

stem: A company has a web application that generates dynamic content for each user. The content personalization logic runs on Lambda functions. Even though the base HTML template is the same, each response is different. Which caching strategy reduces Lambda invocations while still serving personalized content?

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache the personalization rules and user preferences, reducing the computation time in each Lambda function without reducing invocation count.
Use Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge functions that personalize cached base templates at the edge, reducing origin Lambda invocations while serving personalized responses from edge locations.
Use Amazon API Gateway caching with a unique cache key per user to store each user's personalized response in the API Gateway cache for subsequent requests from the same user.
Use Amazon CloudFront with full page caching and cache-control headers set to no-cache to bypass the CDN cache entirely, routing every request to the Lambda origin for personalization.

explanation: Lambda@Edge personalizes cached base templates at edge locations, combining CDN caching with personalization. The base template is cached and Lambda@Edge adds user-specific content, reducing full origin Lambda invocations. Option D (no-cache) does not reduce Lambda invocations at all. Option C (per-user cache) creates millions of cache entries and may not reduce invocations for first-time visitors. Option A (ElastiCache) reduces execution time but not invocation count.

stem: A company has deployed an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with one writer and three reader instances all sized at db.r5.2xlarge. The writer CPU averages 40% and reader CPUs average 15%. Which optimization reduces costs while maintaining read availability?

options.text: Replace the three static reader instances with Aurora Auto Scaling that scales between 1 and 3 readers based on CPU utilization, eliminating idle reader capacity during low-traffic periods.
Purchase Reserved Instances for all four instances with 3-year All Upfront payment to receive the maximum discount on the current cluster configuration without changing instance sizes.
Remove two of the three reader instances and keep one reader at db.r5.2xlarge for failover purposes, since the low utilization indicates only one reader is needed for the workload.
Downsize the three reader instances from db.r5.2xlarge to db.r5.large to match the low 15% utilization while keeping the writer at db.r5.2xlarge to handle the higher write workload.

explanation: Readers at 15% CPU are significantly over-provisioned. Downsizing to db.r5.large reduces per-reader costs by ~75% while still providing ample headroom. Keeping three readers maintains read availability across AZs. Option C (remove readers) reduces redundancy. Option A (Auto Scaling) may not scale fast enough for sudden traffic. Option B (Reserved Instances) saves money but on oversized infrastructure.

stem: A company needs to implement tag-based access control so that developers can only manage EC2 instances tagged with their team name. Which IAM policy configuration enforces this?

options.text: Create an IAM policy with ec2:* actions conditioned on aws:ResourceTag/Team matching the developer's team name using the aws:PrincipalTag/Team variable for dynamic matching.
Create separate IAM policies for each team that explicitly list the instance IDs of each team's EC2 instances in the Resource element of the Allow statement.
Create an AWS Config rule that monitors EC2 instance tag compliance and automatically revokes IAM permissions for users who access instances without their team tag.
Create an SCP that denies ec2:* actions unless the aws:ResourceTag/Team tag matches the requesting user's team attribute configured in the corporate identity provider.

explanation: An IAM policy that conditions ec2:* actions on aws:ResourceTag/Team matching the aws:PrincipalTag/Team variable implements attribute-based access control (ABAC), dynamically scoping each developer to instances tagged with their team name without per-team policies. Option B (explicit instance IDs) is static and requires constant policy updates as instances are launched and terminated. Option C (Config rule) is a detective control that reports noncompliance after the fact; it does not prevent access in real time. Option D (SCP) is an organization guardrail that can only restrict access -- it cannot grant developers their baseline EC2 permissions, and the question asks for an IAM policy configuration; the ABAC policy in Option A both grants and scopes access.

stem: A company needs to implement a multi-Region active-active architecture for a web application. Both Regions must serve traffic simultaneously and data must be synchronized between Regions in near real-time. Which database supports this active-active pattern?

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore for Redis with active-active write capability in both Regions and automatic conflict resolution for simultaneous write operations.
Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with cross-Region read replicas in both Regions and configure the application to write to the primary in one Region and read from the local replica.
Use Amazon DynamoDB global tables with write capabilities in both Regions, providing automatic multi-Region replication with sub-second latency and last-writer-wins conflict resolution.
Use Amazon Aurora Global Database with write forwarding enabled in the secondary Region, allowing applications in both Regions to send write requests through the global cluster.

explanation: DynamoDB global tables support active-active with write capabilities in all Regions, sub-second replication, and automatic last-writer-wins conflict resolution. Option D (Aurora Global Database) has a single writer Region; write forwarding routes writes to the primary Region, not true active-active. Option B (RDS read replicas) is active-passive with writes only in the primary Region. Option A (ElastiCache Global Datastore) has active-passive replication, not active-active writes.

stem: A company is building a serverless data processing pipeline that ingests JSON events, transforms them, and stores the results in S3 in Parquet format. The pipeline must handle variable throughput from 100 to 10,000 events per second. Which TWO services should be included in the pipeline? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon SQS to buffer incoming events and an AWS Glue ETL job triggered every 5 minutes to batch-process queued events and convert them to Parquet format in S3.
Use AWS Glue Data Catalog to define the schema for the Parquet output format, which Kinesis Data Firehose references during the automatic format conversion transformation.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest events with built-in buffering, automatic Parquet format conversion through an AWS Glue table schema, and direct S3 delivery.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest events with configurable shard capacity and a Lambda consumer function that converts each event from JSON to Parquet format.

explanation: Kinesis Data Firehose handles variable throughput with automatic scaling, buffers events, and converts JSON to Parquet using the Glue Data Catalog schema definition before delivering to S3. Glue Data Catalog defines the Parquet schema. Option D (Kinesis Data Streams with Lambda) requires managing shard scaling and custom Parquet conversion. Option A (SQS with Glue) has 5-minute batch processing delay rather than near-real-time delivery.

stem: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic IP addresses assigned to each instance. The company has 20 Elastic IPs but only 12 are currently associated with running instances. The remaining 8 are unassociated. What is the cost implication?

options.text: All 20 Elastic IP addresses incur the same charge per hour because AWS now charges for all public IPv4 addresses regardless of association status with running instances.
All 20 Elastic IP addresses are free of charge because they are all within the same AWS account and Region, regardless of whether they are associated with instances.
Only the 12 associated Elastic IP addresses incur charges since they are consuming public IPv4 addresses, while unassociated Elastic IPs are free until they are used.
The 8 unassociated Elastic IP addresses each incur a small hourly charge because AWS charges for Elastic IPs that are allocated but not associated with running instances.

explanation: Since February 2024, AWS charges $0.005/hour for all public IPv4 addresses, whether associated or not. Both the 12 associated and 8 unassociated EIPs incur charges. Previously only unassociated EIPs were charged, but the new policy charges for all public IPv4 addresses. Option D (only unassociated charged) was the old pricing model. Option B (all free) is incorrect under current pricing. Option C (only associated charged) inverts even the old model: before 2024 it was the unassociated addresses that were billed, and under current pricing all public IPv4 addresses are billed.

stem: A company needs to connect 15 VPCs across 5 AWS Regions. Each VPC must be able to communicate with every other VPC. The company currently uses VPC peering, but the mesh topology is becoming unmanageable. The company wants a policy-driven service that automatically provisions inter-Region routing and network segmentation from a central dashboard, without manually configuring peering between Regions. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy a single AWS Transit Gateway in one central Region and attach all 15 VPCs from all 5 Regions to the single Transit Gateway using cross-Region VPC attachments.
Deploy AWS Transit Gateway in each Region and configure Transit Gateway inter-Region peering between all Regions, creating a hub-and-spoke topology that simplifies routing management.
Replace VPC peering with AWS PrivateLink connections between each pair of VPCs, creating service endpoints that allow inter-VPC communication over the AWS private network.
Deploy AWS Cloud WAN with a global network policy that defines segments and connectivity rules, automatically managing the multi-Region network mesh across all 15 VPCs.

explanation: AWS Cloud WAN builds a global core network from a central policy document: it automatically provisions core network edges in each Region, manages inter-Region routing, and applies segmentation rules, all administered from a single dashboard with no manual peering. Option A (single Transit Gateway) is not possible because a Transit Gateway is Regional and cannot attach VPCs located in other Regions. Option B (Transit Gateway per Region with peering) can connect all the VPCs but requires manually creating inter-Region peering and maintaining static routes in every Region, with no central policy or segmentation management. Option C (PrivateLink) exposes individual services through endpoints and does not provide full network-level connectivity between VPCs.

stem: A company builds an event-driven application where a single event must trigger exactly one processing action, even if the event is delivered multiple times. The processing must be idempotent. Which messaging pattern ensures exactly-once processing semantics?

options.text: Use Amazon SNS with delivery retry policies configured and implement client-side deduplication by maintaining a list of processed message IDs in application memory for comparison.
Use Amazon SQS standard queue with a visibility timeout of 5 minutes and configure the consumer to delete the message immediately after receiving it to prevent redelivery.
Use Amazon SQS FIFO queue with content-based deduplication enabled and implement idempotent processing in the consumer by checking a DynamoDB idempotency table before processing.
Use Amazon EventBridge with a dead-letter queue configured and implement duplicate detection in the target Lambda function by checking the event ID against CloudWatch Logs entries.

explanation: SQS FIFO with deduplication prevents duplicate messages from entering the queue. The DynamoDB idempotency table provides a persistent record of processed messages, ensuring exactly-once semantics even if the consumer processes a message twice. Option B (standard queue with immediate delete) may lose messages if processing fails after deletion. Option A (SNS with in-memory deduplication) loses state on restart. Option D (EventBridge with CloudWatch log checking) is unreliable and slow for deduplication.

stem: A company has a data warehouse on Amazon Redshift that analysts query during business hours. Queries have become slower as data volume has grown to 50 TB. The most common queries filter on date ranges and join across 10 tables. Which Redshift optimization has the HIGHEST impact on query performance?

options.text: Enable Redshift Concurrency Scaling to add temporary capacity during peak hours when multiple analysts run queries simultaneously, reducing queue wait times between queries.
Create materialized views for the most common 10-table join queries and schedule them to refresh every hour so analysts query pre-computed results instead of raw tables.
Configure distribution keys on the most frequently joined columns and sort keys on the date column to optimize data co-location for joins and range filtering for date queries.
Increase the number of Redshift nodes by adding more compute to the cluster to provide additional CPU, memory, and storage for handling the 50 TB dataset and complex queries.

explanation: Distribution keys on join columns ensure joined rows are co-located on the same node, eliminating data redistribution. Sort keys on date columns enable zone map optimization for date range filtering, skipping irrelevant data blocks. These optimizations have the highest impact. Option D (more nodes) helps but without proper keys, queries still redistribute data. Option A (Concurrency Scaling) helps with concurrent queries, not individual query speed. Option B (materialized views) helps specific queries but requires maintenance and storage.

stem: A company runs a development environment with 20 Amazon RDS instances for different microservice teams. The instances sit idle during nights and weekends. The company wants to automatically stop the instances each evening and start them each weekday morning, using only native service features without deploying a prepackaged CloudFormation solution stack. Which approach automates this?

options.text: Configure Amazon RDS to automatically stop instances after 7 days of inactivity and manually restart them when developers need them for their microservice testing work.
Migrate all development databases to Aurora Serverless v2 with minimum capacity of 0 ACU to automatically scale compute to zero when idle and scale up when queries arrive.
Create Lambda functions triggered by EventBridge scheduled rules to call StopDBInstance at 7 PM and StartDBInstance at 7 AM on weekdays for all tagged development instances.
Use AWS Instance Scheduler to automatically stop RDS instances at 7 PM and start them at 7 AM on weekdays, based on tags applied to each instance indicating the desired schedule.

explanation: Lambda functions triggered by EventBridge scheduled rules can call StopDBInstance and StartDBInstance for all tagged development instances on the required weekday schedule, using only native service features with no additional solution stack to deploy. Option A (auto-stop after inactivity) describes a feature that does not exist -- RDS has no inactivity-based auto-stop, stopped instances are automatically started again after 7 days, and manual restarts fail the automation requirement. Option B (Aurora Serverless v2 at 0 ACU) can pause compute when idle, but it requires migrating all 20 RDS databases to Aurora and adds resume latency on the first connection each morning. Option D (Instance Scheduler) natively schedules RDS instances by tag but is deployed as a prepackaged CloudFormation solution stack with Lambda and DynamoDB resources, which the company ruled out.

stem: A company needs to prevent data exfiltration from Amazon S3 buckets. The security team wants to ensure that S3 objects can only be accessed from within the company's VPC and never from the public internet, even by authorized IAM users. Which control prevents public internet access to S3 objects?

options.text: Configure S3 bucket policies with a condition that denies all access unless the request comes from the company's VPC endpoint using the aws:sourceVpce condition key.
Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level to prevent any S3 bucket from being made publicly accessible through bucket policies or access control lists.
Enable Amazon Macie to monitor S3 access patterns and generate findings when objects are accessed from outside the VPC, alerting the security team for investigation.
Configure VPC endpoint policies on the S3 gateway endpoint to restrict which S3 buckets can be accessed from the VPC, preventing unauthorized bucket access.

explanation: S3 bucket policies with aws:sourceVpce condition deny all access unless it comes through the VPC endpoint, preventing access from the public internet even by IAM users with valid credentials. Option B (Block Public Access) prevents anonymous public access but does not prevent authenticated IAM users from accessing S3 over the internet. Option D (VPC endpoint policy) restricts what the VPC can access, not who can access the bucket from outside. Option C (Macie) is detective, not preventive.

stem: A company deploys a microservices application using AWS Lambda. The company needs to implement a retry strategy for transient failures when calling external APIs. If all retries fail, the failed event must be preserved for later investigation, and the preserved record must include the function's error response and stack trace along with the original event payload. Which Lambda configuration provides this behavior?

options.text: Configure an EventBridge rule to detect Lambda function errors through CloudWatch alarms and automatically re-invoke the Lambda function with the same event payload.
Configure the Lambda function with a maximum retry attempts of 2 for asynchronous invocations and a dead-letter queue (SQS) to capture events that exhaust all retry attempts.
Configure the Lambda function with a destination configuration that routes failed events to an SQS queue after the built-in retry mechanism exhausts the maximum retry attempts.
Implement try-catch blocks in the Lambda function code with a retry loop of 3 attempts and write failed events to a DynamoDB table for later investigation by the team.

explanation: An on-failure destination sends a complete invocation record — the original request payload plus the response context, error message, and stack trace — to the SQS queue after Lambda's built-in asynchronous retries are exhausted, meeting every stated requirement. Option A (EventBridge re-invocation via alarms) creates an unbounded retry loop with no termination condition and does not preserve error details with the event. Option B (async retries with an SQS dead-letter queue) preserves the original event with only brief error attributes; DLQ messages do not include the function's error response or stack trace. Option D (try-catch with DynamoDB writes) requires custom retry and persistence code and captures only whatever the code explicitly records.

stem: A company needs to deploy a container-based machine learning inference service that must start processing requests within 2 seconds of receiving them. The service receives sporadic traffic with 0-100 requests per minute. Which compute platform provides the fastest cold start for containers?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoints that scale to zero when idle and provision compute for inference within a cold start time of a few seconds.
Use Amazon ECS with Fargate and Application Auto Scaling that scales to zero tasks when idle and provisions new tasks when requests arrive through an ALB.
Use AWS Lambda with container image support to deploy the ML model as a container function, leveraging Lambda's sub-second cold start for lightweight containers.
Use Amazon EKS with Karpenter node autoscaler that provisions new nodes within 60 seconds and schedules pods on the new nodes for the inference workload.

explanation: Lambda container images provide sub-second cold starts for containers up to 10 GB in size. For sporadic traffic with 0-100 requests per minute, Lambda's pay-per-invocation model and fast cold starts are ideal. Option B (Fargate) takes 30-60 seconds to provision new tasks from zero. Option D (EKS with Karpenter) takes 60+ seconds for node provisioning. Option A (SageMaker Serverless) has cold starts of several seconds to minutes depending on model size.

stem: A company uses Amazon CloudWatch for monitoring with 500 custom metrics published every minute. The CloudWatch custom metrics cost is higher than expected. Which approach reduces custom metric charges the MOST while continuing to use CloudWatch?

options.text: Use CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) to publish metrics as structured log data, which is automatically extracted as metrics at the same cost but with richer context.
Reduce the metric publishing frequency from every minute to every 5 minutes for non-critical metrics to reduce the number of PutMetricData API calls by 80 percent.
Switch from CloudWatch to a self-hosted Prometheus server on EC2 to eliminate custom metric charges while maintaining the same monitoring and alerting capabilities.
Reduce dimension cardinality by removing high-cardinality dimensions such as per-instance IDs and pre-aggregating values, lowering the number of unique metric and dimension combinations billed.

explanation: CloudWatch bills every unique combination of metric name and dimension values as a separate custom metric, so removing high-cardinality dimensions (such as per-instance IDs) and pre-aggregating values directly reduces the number of billed custom metrics — the dominant part of the charge. Option A (Embedded Metric Format) changes how metrics are ingested, but each extracted metric is still billed as a custom metric at the same per-metric rate. Option B (lower publishing frequency) reduces PutMetricData request charges only; each unique metric is billed its monthly per-metric charge regardless of how often data points arrive. Option C (self-hosted Prometheus) abandons CloudWatch, which the requirement excludes, and trades metric charges for EC2 infrastructure cost and operational overhead.

stem: A company is migrating to AWS and needs to establish a secure hybrid connection between the on-premises data center and AWS VPC. The connection must be encrypted and established quickly within a few hours. Which connectivity option should be used?

options.text: Set up an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection with MACsec encryption at the physical layer, which provides a private, high-bandwidth connection to the AWS network.
Set up AWS Client VPN to allow on-premises servers to establish individual VPN tunnels to the VPC through a client VPN endpoint with certificate-based authentication.
Set up an AWS Direct Connect hosted connection through a Direct Connect partner with a VPN overlay for encryption, combining private connectivity with IPSec encryption.
Set up an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet using IPSec encryption, which can be configured within hours using a virtual private gateway and customer gateway.

explanation: Site-to-Site VPN provides encrypted IPSec connectivity over the internet and can be set up within hours. It requires only a virtual private gateway in AWS and a compatible customer gateway device on-premises. Option A (Direct Connect) takes weeks to months to provision. Option C (Direct Connect hosted) also takes time to provision through a partner. Option B (Client VPN) is for individual client connections, not site-to-site data center connectivity.

stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon ECS that stores uploaded files on Amazon EFS. The company needs to create a disaster recovery copy of the EFS file system in another Region. Which solution provides cross-Region replication for EFS?

options.text: Configure AWS DataSync with a scheduled task that synchronizes files from the source EFS to a destination EFS in the DR Region every 15 minutes for near-continuous replication.
Enable Amazon EFS replication to automatically replicate the file system to a destination Region with recovery point objectives of approximately 15 minutes for cross-Region protection.
Create an AWS Backup plan that takes daily EFS backups and configure cross-Region backup copy rules to replicate the backup vault to the disaster recovery Region automatically.
Deploy a Lambda function triggered by EFS access events through CloudTrail that copies modified files to an S3 bucket with Cross-Region Replication to the disaster recovery Region.

explanation: Amazon EFS replication provides automatic, continuous cross-Region replication with approximately 15-minute RPO. It creates and maintains a read-only replica in the destination Region. Option A (DataSync) works but requires managing scheduled tasks and DataSync infrastructure. Option C (AWS Backup with cross-Region copy) provides daily copies, not continuous replication. Option D (Lambda with S3 CRR) is overly complex and does not maintain an EFS file system in the DR Region.

stem: A company needs to build a notification system that sends push notifications to millions of mobile devices. The system must support iOS (APNs), Android (FCM), and SMS delivery channels. Which AWS service provides this multi-channel notification capability?

options.text: Use Amazon Pinpoint to manage user segments and send push notifications through APNs and FCM channels and SMS messages through the built-in SMS messaging capability.
Use Amazon SNS with platform application endpoints for APNs and FCM push notifications and SMS message publishing for text notifications to reach all device types.
Use Amazon SQS with separate queues for each platform (iOS, Android, SMS) and deploy Lambda consumers that call platform-specific APIs to deliver each notification.
Use Amazon SES for sending email notifications to all users and configure the mobile applications to poll for new notifications through an API Gateway REST API endpoint.

explanation: Amazon SNS supports direct push notifications to APNs (iOS) and FCM (Android) through platform applications, and SMS messages through the SMS publishing feature. It scales to millions of devices. Option A (Pinpoint) works for campaigns but adds complexity for simple push notifications. Option D (SES) is for email only and polling is not real-time push. Option C (SQS with Lambda) requires building custom platform integration logic.

stem: A company operates a data lake on Amazon S3 with 500 TB of data. Data scientists run ad-hoc queries using Amazon Athena that frequently scan the entire dataset. Monthly Athena query costs exceed $5,000. Which optimization provides the LARGEST cost reduction for Athena queries?

options.text: Migrate the data lake from S3 to Amazon Redshift Serverless and have data scientists query Redshift instead of Athena to benefit from Redshift's columnar storage optimization.
Convert all data from CSV format to Apache Parquet with Snappy compression and partition by the most commonly filtered columns to minimize the data scanned per query.
Enable Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the data lake bucket to automatically move infrequently accessed data to lower-cost storage tiers and reduce the per-GB storage costs.
Create Amazon Athena workgroups with per-query data scan limits to prevent individual queries from scanning more than 10 GB and alert users when they approach the limit.

explanation: Converting to Parquet with partitioning can reduce data scanned by 90-99% since Athena reads only required columns (Parquet) and skips irrelevant partitions. Athena charges $5 per TB scanned, so reducing scans dramatically cuts costs. Option D (workgroup limits) prevents expensive queries but does not reduce the cost of legitimate queries. Option A (Redshift) adds infrastructure costs. Option C (Intelligent-Tiering) reduces storage costs, not query costs.

stem: A company uses AWS Lambda functions that process sensitive customer data. The company needs to ensure that Lambda environment variables are encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS key. Which Lambda configuration meets this requirement?

options.text: Configure the Lambda function to use a customer managed KMS key for encrypting environment variables at rest and enable the function to use the key for decryption at runtime.
Store sensitive data in AWS Secrets Manager instead of environment variables and configure the Lambda function IAM role to access specific secrets using the Secrets Manager API.
Configure the Lambda function's deployment package with client-side encryption using an AWS CloudHSM-backed key before uploading it to the Lambda service for deployment.
Enable AWS Config encryption compliance rules to verify that all Lambda functions in the account use customer managed KMS keys for environment variable encryption.

explanation: Lambda lets you specify a customer managed KMS key to encrypt a function's environment variables at rest, and the service uses that key to decrypt them when the function is invoked, giving the company full control of the key. Option B (Secrets Manager) moves the sensitive values out of environment variables entirely; it does not encrypt the environment variables themselves with a customer managed key. Option C (client-side encryption of the deployment package) targets the code artifact, not environment variables, and is not how Lambda applies encryption. Option D (AWS Config rules) is detective only — it reports noncompliance but does not configure any encryption.

stem: A company uses Amazon API Gateway REST APIs to expose microservices. During deployments, the company wants to gradually shift traffic from the current API version to a new version, rolling back if error rates increase. Which API Gateway feature supports this?

options.text: Configure API Gateway canary deployments on the production stage to route a configurable percentage of traffic to the new deployment while monitoring error rates for automatic rollback.
Create a new API Gateway stage for the new version and use Route 53 weighted routing to gradually shift traffic from the old stage URL to the new stage URL based on weights.
Use API Gateway throttling settings to limit traffic to the new deployment by reducing the rate limit to 10% of normal and gradually increasing it as confidence in the new version grows.
Deploy the new version as a separate API Gateway REST API and use CloudFront with origin groups to failover from the new API to the old API if error rates exceed thresholds.

explanation: API Gateway canary deployments allow directing a percentage of traffic to a new deployment within the same stage. CloudWatch metrics monitor error rates, and the deployment can be rolled back instantly if issues arise. Option B (separate stages with Route 53) adds DNS propagation delay and requires managing two stages. Option D (separate APIs with CloudFront) is overly complex. Option C (throttling) limits all traffic, not selective traffic splitting.

stem: A company needs to implement real-time fraud detection for financial transactions. Each transaction must be evaluated against complex rules within 100 milliseconds. The system processes 10,000 transactions per second. Which architecture meets the latency requirement?

options.text: Store transactions in Amazon S3 and run Amazon Athena queries every second against the latest transactions to identify fraudulent patterns using SQL-based detection rules.
Send transactions to Amazon EventBridge and route them to Step Functions Express Workflows that execute fraud detection rules as a series of sequential Lambda function invocations.
Send transactions to Amazon SQS and process them with Lambda functions that evaluate fraud rules against a DynamoDB rules table for each transaction independently.
Ingest transactions through Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and process them with Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink using a sliding window for real-time rule evaluation within milliseconds.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams with Apache Flink provides sub-100ms processing latency for streaming data. Flink's sliding windows enable complex rule evaluation across transaction patterns in real-time. Option C (SQS with Lambda) may exceed 100ms due to SQS polling latency and Lambda cold starts. Option A (S3 with Athena) is batch processing, not real-time. Option B (EventBridge with Step Functions) adds orchestration overhead exceeding 100ms.

stem: A company uses AWS Fargate for running containerized applications. The company has predictable workloads that run 24/7 with consistent resource usage. Fargate costs are a significant portion of the monthly bill. Which purchasing option reduces Fargate costs?

options.text: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan with a 1-year or 3-year commitment that covers Fargate usage, providing up to 50% discount on Fargate compute costs for committed workloads.
Migrate from ECS Fargate to EKS Fargate which provides lower per-vCPU and per-GB pricing for Kubernetes-based container orchestration workloads on Fargate.
Switch from Fargate to EC2 launch type with Reserved Instances for the underlying ECS cluster to reduce per-hour compute costs for predictable container workloads.
Configure Fargate Spot for all tasks to receive up to 70% discount on Fargate pricing, accepting the risk of task interruption during capacity shortages.

explanation: Compute Savings Plans provide up to 50% discount on Fargate usage with 1-year or 3-year commitments. For predictable 24/7 workloads, this is the most straightforward cost reduction. Option C (EC2 with RIs) reduces costs but adds infrastructure management overhead. Option D (Fargate Spot) risks task interruption, unacceptable for 24/7 production. Option B (EKS Fargate) has the same pricing as ECS Fargate.
