explanation: S3 Standard-IA stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones at low cost for data accessed less than once per month, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval offers standard retrievals in 3-5 hours, meeting the few-hours audit requirement at archival prices. Option A (Intelligent-Tiering) adds per-object monitoring fees across a very large number of log objects, raising costs. Option C (One Zone-IA then Deep Archive) stores 30-90 day data in a single AZ, losing availability if that AZ fails, and Deep Archive retrievals take up to 12 hours. Option D (Glacier Instant Retrieval then Deep Archive) also relies on Deep Archive, whose 12-hour standard retrievals miss the few-hours audit requirement.

stem: A company must ensure that all API calls made in its AWS accounts are logged and that the log files cannot be tampered with. Which TWO actions should the solutions architect implement? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Enable AWS Config rules to evaluate API call compliance and automatically remediate non-compliant API actions by reverting unauthorized changes detected across all accounts.
Configure Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent on all EC2 instances to capture API call logs locally and forward them to a centralized CloudWatch log group for analysis and alerting.
Enable AWS CloudTrail in all AWS Regions with management events logging enabled and configure the trail to deliver log files to a centralized S3 bucket in a dedicated security account.
Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation to generate a hash digest for each log file delivered, allowing verification that logs have not been modified or deleted after delivery.

explanation: CloudTrail logs all API calls across all Regions, and log file integrity validation uses SHA-256 hashing to detect any tampering with delivered log files. Together they provide comprehensive, tamper-evident API logging. Option B (CloudWatch Logs agent) captures application logs, not API call logs. Option A (AWS Config) evaluates resource configuration compliance, not API call logging.

stem: A company runs a stateful web application on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Users report losing their session data when they are routed to a different instance. Which solution maintains session persistence without modifying the application code?

options.text: Store session data in Amazon ElastiCache for Redis and configure the application to read and write session data from the shared Redis cluster across all instances.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the least outstanding requests routing algorithm so that users are distributed evenly and consistently across the available instances.
Store session data in Amazon DynamoDB with TTL enabled and configure the application to persist sessions to DynamoDB instead of local instance memory or disk storage.
Enable ALB sticky sessions using duration-based cookies generated by the load balancer with a duration of 1 hour so each user's requests reach the same backend instance.

explanation: Duration-based sticky sessions use the load-balancer-generated AWSALB cookie to bind each user to a specific target, so subsequent requests reach the same instance with no application code changes. Option A (ElastiCache for Redis) requires modifying the application to read and write session data to Redis. Option B (routing algorithm) balances request distribution but provides no session affinity to a specific instance. Option C (DynamoDB sessions) requires application code changes to persist sessions externally.

stem: A company has a data analytics application that runs complex SQL queries against petabytes of data stored in Amazon S3. The queries are ad-hoc and need to return results within seconds. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case?

options.text: Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to extend Redshift queries to S3 data without loading it, combining the Redshift query engine with S3 storage for petabyte-scale analytics.
Use Amazon EMR with Apache Hive to process SQL queries against S3 data using a managed Hadoop cluster optimized for large-scale batch processing and analytics.
Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the aws_s3 extension to query S3 data directly from the relational database, combining SQL familiarity with S3 storage scalability.
Use Amazon Athena to run serverless SQL queries directly against data stored in S3, leveraging columnar format and partitioning for fast query performance on petabyte-scale data.

explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service that runs SQL directly against S3 data. It uses Presto engine and supports columnar formats like Parquet for fast results on petabyte-scale data. Option A (Redshift Spectrum) requires a provisioned Redshift cluster as a prerequisite. Option B (EMR with Hive) is suited for batch processing, not interactive ad-hoc queries. Option C (RDS PostgreSQL) is not designed for petabyte-scale analytics and has storage limitations.

stem: A company runs a batch processing application that can tolerate interruptions and typically takes 4 hours to complete. The application requires 100 EC2 instances for processing. Which purchasing option provides the lowest cost?

options.text: Use EC2 On-Demand Instances for all 100 instances to ensure guaranteed capacity availability throughout the 4-hour batch processing window without interruption risk.
Use EC2 Spot Instances with a diversified allocation strategy across multiple instance types and Availability Zones to reduce the likelihood of simultaneous interruptions.
Use EC2 Dedicated Hosts with On-Demand pricing to ensure the batch processing workload has dedicated physical servers for consistent performance during the 4-hour run.
Purchase EC2 Reserved Instances with a 1-year term and no upfront payment for the 100 instances to receive a significant discount compared to On-Demand pricing.

explanation: Spot Instances provide up to 90% discount compared to On-Demand pricing. Since the workload tolerates interruptions, Spot is ideal. Diversified allocation across instance types and AZs reduces interruption probability. Option A (On-Demand) is significantly more expensive. Option D (Reserved Instances) requires a 1-year commitment, which is wasteful for batch workloads that may not run continuously. Option C (Dedicated Hosts) is the most expensive option and unnecessary for batch processing.

stem: A company needs to provide temporary AWS credentials to a mobile application so users can upload files directly to an S3 bucket. The application authenticates users through a custom identity provider. Which service enables secure, temporary AWS access for authenticated mobile users?

options.text: Use Amazon API Gateway with a Lambda authorizer to validate the identity provider token and proxy S3 upload requests through the API Gateway endpoint.
Use AWS STS AssumeRole directly from the mobile application by embedding IAM role credentials that allow the app to assume a role for S3 upload access.
Use Amazon Cognito identity pools (federated identities) to exchange the custom identity provider token for temporary AWS credentials scoped to the user's S3 upload prefix.
Use AWS IAM users with programmatic access keys embedded in the mobile application, with each user mapped to a specific S3 prefix for isolated upload access.

explanation: Cognito identity pools federate with custom identity providers and vend temporary, scoped AWS credentials (via STS) to authenticated users. This enables direct S3 uploads without proxying. Option D (IAM users with embedded keys) is insecure; credentials in mobile apps can be extracted. Option B (STS AssumeRole from mobile) requires embedding IAM credentials, which is insecure. Option A (API Gateway proxy) adds latency and cost by proxying uploads through Lambda.

stem: A company has a three-tier web application deployed in a single Availability Zone. The company wants to redesign the architecture to survive an AZ failure with minimal downtime. Which architecture change provides AZ-level resilience?

options.text: Deploy EC2 instances in a single AZ with AMI backups taken hourly, configure RDS automated snapshots, and use an S3 bucket with cross-Region replication for shared storage.
Deploy EC2 instances across multiple Regions using Route 53 latency-based routing, with Aurora Global Database for cross-Region database replication and S3 for shared files.
Deploy EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple AZs behind an ALB, use RDS Multi-AZ for the database, and store shared files on Amazon EFS mounted across AZs.
Deploy EC2 instances in a single AZ with enhanced monitoring and configure CloudWatch alarms to trigger a Lambda function that re-launches the infrastructure in another AZ on failure.

explanation: Multi-AZ Auto Scaling with ALB distributes instances across AZs for automatic failover. RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby in another AZ. EFS provides multi-AZ shared storage. Option A (single AZ with backups) requires manual recovery from snapshots during an AZ failure. Option B (multi-Region) exceeds the requirement and adds complexity. Option D (Lambda re-launch) is reactive with significant downtime during failover.

stem: A company has a REST API that receives 10,000 requests per second during peak hours. The API responses are identical for the same request parameters and change only every 5 minutes. Which architecture reduces backend load while maintaining low latency?

options.text: Scale the API backend horizontally using Auto Scaling with target tracking on request count per target to handle 10,000 requests per second with sufficient compute capacity.
Deploy Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the API and the database to cache query results with a 5-minute TTL, reducing database queries for identical parameters.
Enable API Gateway caching with a 5-minute TTL on the API stage to cache responses at the API Gateway level and reduce the number of requests forwarded to the backend.
Deploy Amazon CloudFront in front of the API Gateway endpoint and configure a cache TTL of 5 minutes to serve repeated API responses from edge locations worldwide.

explanation: API Gateway built-in caching stores responses at the API level with configurable TTL. This reduces backend invocations for identical requests without requiring additional infrastructure. Option D (CloudFront) adds edge caching but introduces another layer and CDN costs. Option B (ElastiCache) caches database queries but the API still processes each request. Option A (Auto Scaling) handles load but does not reduce backend processing for identical requests.

stem: A company runs a production workload on Amazon EC2 with steady, predictable usage 24/7 year-round. The workload has been running for 2 years and is expected to continue for at least 3 more years. Which EC2 purchasing option provides the greatest cost savings?

options.text: Use EC2 On-Demand Instances with AWS Budgets alerts to monitor spending and optimize costs by right-sizing instances based on CloudWatch utilization metrics.
Purchase a 1-year Standard Reserved Instance with partial upfront payment and renew annually to maintain flexibility while receiving a significant discount over On-Demand pricing.
Purchase a 3-year EC2 Savings Plan with all upfront payment to receive the maximum discount for the committed compute usage over the three-year term.
Purchase a 3-year Convertible Reserved Instance with no upfront payment to receive a discount while retaining the ability to change instance families during the term.

explanation: A 3-year Savings Plan with all upfront payment provides the highest discount (up to 72% vs On-Demand). Since usage is steady and expected to continue for 3+ years, the long commitment maximizes savings. Option B (1-year RI) provides less discount than a 3-year commitment. Option A (On-Demand) is the most expensive option. Option D (Convertible RI no upfront) provides a lower discount than all upfront Savings Plans.

stem: A company wants to ensure that no AWS IAM user can launch EC2 instances in any Region other than us-east-1 and eu-west-1. The restriction must apply across all accounts in the AWS Organization. Which approach enforces this restriction?

options.text: Configure AWS Config rules to detect EC2 instances launched outside us-east-1 and eu-west-1, with automatic remediation to terminate non-compliant instances immediately.
Create an IAM policy with a Deny statement for ec2:RunInstances in all Regions and attach it to every IAM user, then create Allow statements for us-east-1 and eu-west-1 only.
Use AWS Control Tower guardrails to restrict EC2 instance launches to approved Regions and configure mandatory controls for us-east-1 and eu-west-1 across the Organization.
Create a Service Control Policy (SCP) with a Deny statement for ec2:RunInstances with a StringNotEquals condition on aws:RequestedRegion for us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

explanation: SCPs enforce permission boundaries across all accounts in an Organization. A Deny on ec2:RunInstances with StringNotEquals on aws:RequestedRegion blocks launches in non-approved Regions. Option B (IAM policies) requires attaching to every user and does not prevent new users from bypassing the restriction. Option A (AWS Config) is detective and reactive, not preventive. Option C (Control Tower guardrails) provides Region deny guardrails but SCPs are the direct mechanism.

stem: A company is designing a disaster recovery solution for a critical database with an RPO of 1 hour and an RTO of 15 minutes. Which TWO components should be part of the solution? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Deploy the database on EC2 with EBS snapshots copied to the secondary Region every 6 hours and a CloudFormation template to launch a recovery instance from the snapshot.
Configure RDS automated backups with cross-Region backup replication enabled, ensuring backup copies are available in the secondary Region within the 1-hour RPO window.
Implement Amazon DynamoDB global tables with multi-Region active-active replication to provide automatic failover and near-zero RPO for the critical database workload.
Use Amazon Aurora with cross-Region read replicas to maintain a near-real-time copy of the database in a secondary Region that can be promoted to primary within minutes.

explanation: Aurora cross-Region read replicas provide near-real-time replication and can be promoted within minutes (meeting 15-minute RTO). Cross-Region backup replication provides an additional recovery point within the 1-hour RPO. Option A (6-hour snapshots) exceeds the 1-hour RPO requirement. Option C (DynamoDB global tables) changes the database technology and is only applicable if the workload uses DynamoDB.

stem: A gaming company needs a database that provides single-digit millisecond read latency for player session data. The data model is key-value with simple lookups by player ID. The workload has unpredictable traffic spikes during game events. Which database solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Neptune graph database to model player relationships and session data, providing fast traversal queries for looking up player sessions by unique identifiers.
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with cluster mode enabled to store player session data in memory, providing sub-millisecond read latency with automatic sharding.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity mode to automatically scale read and write throughput in response to traffic spikes while providing single-digit millisecond latency.
Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with provisioned IOPS storage and read replicas to distribute read traffic and achieve low latency for player session lookups by player ID.

explanation: DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond latency for key-value lookups, and on-demand mode handles unpredictable traffic spikes by automatically scaling capacity. Option D (Aurora MySQL) is a relational database with higher latency for simple key-value lookups. Option B (ElastiCache) provides sub-millisecond latency but requires managing cache invalidation and is not a persistent database. Option A (Neptune) is designed for graph queries, not simple key-value lookups.

stem: A company uses Amazon RDS MySQL with a db.r5.4xlarge instance. CloudWatch metrics show the database CPU averages 15% utilization and memory usage is at 25% capacity. Which action reduces costs while maintaining acceptable performance?

options.text: Downsize the RDS instance from db.r5.4xlarge to db.r5.xlarge based on the low CPU and memory utilization, then monitor performance metrics to verify the smaller instance is sufficient.
Migrate the RDS MySQL database to Aurora Serverless v2 which automatically scales compute capacity between a minimum and maximum ACU based on actual database workload demands.
Enable RDS storage autoscaling and switch from provisioned IOPS to General Purpose SSD storage to reduce storage costs while maintaining the current compute instance configuration.
Convert the RDS instance from On-Demand to a 1-year Reserved Instance with all upfront payment to reduce the hourly cost while keeping the current db.r5.4xlarge instance size.

explanation: With only 15% CPU and 25% memory utilization, the instance is significantly oversized. Downsizing to db.r5.xlarge (4x smaller) would still provide headroom while reducing costs by approximately 75%. Option B (Aurora Serverless) requires migration effort and may not be the cheapest option for steady workloads. Option D (Reserved Instance) locks in costs for an oversized instance. Option C (storage changes) addresses storage costs, not the compute over-provisioning issue.

stem: A company has a VPC with public and private subnets. Applications in private subnets need to access Amazon S3 without traffic traversing the internet. Which VPC feature provides private connectivity to S3?

options.text: Create a VPC gateway endpoint for S3 and add a route in the private subnet route table pointing S3 prefix list traffic to the gateway endpoint for private connectivity.
Create a VPC interface endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) for S3 with a private DNS entry and configure security groups on the endpoint to allow S3 API traffic on port 443.
Configure an S3 bucket policy that restricts access to requests originating from the VPC CIDR range and use the VPC's internet gateway for S3 API connectivity.
Create a NAT gateway in the public subnet and configure the private subnet route table to route S3 traffic through the NAT gateway for internet-based S3 access.

explanation: VPC gateway endpoints for S3 provide private connectivity from VPC to S3 without traversing the internet. Traffic stays on the AWS network via a route table entry. Gateway endpoints are free. Option D (NAT gateway) routes S3 traffic through the internet and incurs data transfer charges. Option B (interface endpoint) works but costs more than the free gateway endpoint. Option C (bucket policy with IGW) still routes traffic through the internet.

stem: A company has a microservices application where Service A calls Service B synchronously. When Service B is unavailable, Service A also fails, causing cascading failures across the application. Which pattern prevents these cascading failures?

options.text: Deploy Service B behind an Application Load Balancer with health checks to automatically remove unhealthy instances and route traffic only to healthy Service B instances.
Deploy Service B in multiple Availability Zones with Auto Scaling to ensure sufficient capacity is always available to handle requests from Service A without failures.
Implement a circuit breaker pattern in Service A that stops calling Service B after detecting repeated failures and returns a cached or default response until Service B recovers.
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff in Service A to automatically retry failed requests to Service B with increasing delays between each attempt.

explanation: The circuit breaker pattern detects failures and stops sending requests to the failing service, preventing cascading failures. It returns fallback responses and periodically checks if the service has recovered. Option A (ALB with health checks) helps with instance failures but not complete service outages. Option D (retry with backoff) can worsen cascading failures by increasing load on the failing service. Option B (Multi-AZ with Auto Scaling) improves availability but does not address complete service failures.

stem: A company needs to process and analyze streaming data from IoT sensors at a rate of 1 GB per second. The data must be available for real-time dashboards and stored in S3 for historical analysis. Which architecture handles this streaming workload?

options.text: Use Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) to ingest sensor data, EC2 consumer applications for real-time analysis, and S3 Sink Connector for archival storage.
Use Amazon EventBridge to receive IoT sensor events, Step Functions to orchestrate real-time processing workflows, and EventBridge archive rules to store events in S3 for analysis.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest sensor data, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for real-time analysis and dashboards, and Kinesis Data Firehose for S3 delivery.
Use Amazon SQS FIFO queues to ingest sensor data in order, Lambda functions to process each message for dashboard updates, and another Lambda to batch and write data to S3.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams handles GB/s ingestion rates. Managed Apache Flink provides real-time analytics for dashboards. Kinesis Data Firehose delivers data to S3 automatically. This is a fully managed, integrated streaming architecture. Option D (SQS with Lambda) is not designed for streaming at 1 GB/s throughput. Option A (MSK) works but requires more operational management than the Kinesis ecosystem. Option B (EventBridge) is designed for event routing, not high-throughput streaming.

stem: A company wants to reduce its monthly AWS data transfer costs. Analysis shows significant data transfer charges for traffic between VPCs in the same Region and for internet-bound traffic. Which TWO actions reduce data transfer costs? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Deploy Amazon CloudFront to cache and serve static content to end users, reducing the amount of data transferred from origin servers through the internet gateway each month.
Use VPC peering instead of Transit Gateway for VPC-to-VPC communication in the same Region, as VPC peering data transfer within the same AZ is free while Transit Gateway charges per GB.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on all S3 buckets to reduce data transfer costs by routing uploads through CloudFront edge locations closer to the uploading clients.
Migrate EC2 instances from multiple AZs to a single AZ to eliminate cross-AZ data transfer charges that are incurred when instances communicate across Availability Zone boundaries.

explanation: VPC peering in the same AZ has no data transfer charge, while Transit Gateway charges per GB processed. CloudFront reduces origin data transfer by serving cached content from edge locations. Option D (single AZ) reduces cross-AZ costs but eliminates high availability. Option C (S3 Transfer Acceleration) increases costs by adding acceleration fees on top of regular transfer charges.

stem: A company discovers that an IAM access key has been exposed in a public GitHub repository. Which series of actions should the solutions architect take first to mitigate the security risk?

options.text: Rotate the exposed access key by creating a new key first, updating all applications to use the new key, then deactivating the old key after confirming applications work correctly.
Enable MFA on the IAM user account associated with the exposed key and add an IAM policy condition requiring MFA for all API calls made with the compromised access key.
Delete the IAM user account associated with the exposed key, create a new IAM user with a new access key, and update all applications that were using the compromised credentials.
Immediately deactivate the exposed IAM access key, review CloudTrail logs for unauthorized activity during the exposure period, and create a new access key for the affected user.

explanation: The immediate priority is to deactivate the exposed key to prevent unauthorized use, then investigate CloudTrail for any unauthorized activity. A new key can be created afterward. Option C (delete user) is disruptive and may break applications unnecessarily. Option A (rotate key) leaves the compromised key active while creating the new one, allowing continued unauthorized access. Option B (MFA) does not prevent programmatic access with the exposed key.

stem: A company needs to deploy a message queue that decouples a web tier from a processing tier. Messages must be processed exactly once and in the exact order they were sent. Which messaging configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard to maintain message ordering and enable enhanced fan-out for exactly-once message delivery to the consumer application.
Use Amazon SQS FIFO queue with message deduplication enabled and a single message group ID to ensure strict ordering and exactly-once processing of all messages in the queue.
Use Amazon SNS FIFO topic with an SQS Standard queue subscription to provide ordered message delivery from the topic to the processing tier through the queue subscriber.
Use Amazon SQS Standard queue with visibility timeout set to 30 seconds and long polling enabled to reduce empty responses and ensure efficient message processing.

explanation: SQS FIFO queues guarantee exactly-once processing and strict message ordering within a message group. Using a single message group ID ensures all messages are processed in the exact order sent. Option D (Standard queue) provides at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering, not exactly-once or strict ordering. Option C (SNS FIFO to Standard SQS) loses FIFO guarantees when delivered to a Standard queue. Option A (Kinesis) provides ordering within a shard but at-least-once delivery, not exactly-once.

stem: A company has a global user base and needs to serve a single-page application (SPA) with the lowest possible latency worldwide. The SPA consists of static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and image files. Which architecture provides optimal global performance?

options.text: Deploy the SPA as a containerized application on Amazon ECS Fargate in multiple Regions with AWS Global Accelerator routing user traffic to the nearest healthy Region endpoint.
Host the SPA files on an Amazon EFS file system mounted on EC2 instances across multiple AZs behind an ALB, with CloudFront caching responses from the ALB origin.
Deploy the SPA on EC2 instances in multiple Regions behind an Application Load Balancer in each Region, with Route 53 latency-based routing directing users to the nearest Region.
Host the SPA files in an Amazon S3 bucket configured for static website hosting and distribute content globally through Amazon CloudFront with edge locations caching the static assets.

explanation: S3 with CloudFront is the standard architecture for global SPA delivery. CloudFront caches static files at 400+ edge locations worldwide, providing the lowest latency. S3 provides durable, scalable origin storage. Option C (EC2 multi-Region) is over-engineered for static content and costly. Option B (EFS with EC2) adds unnecessary compute for serving static files. Option A (ECS Fargate multi-Region) is over-engineered for static content delivery.

stem: A company processes large datasets using Amazon EMR clusters that run for 8 hours each night. The clusters use 50 core nodes and 100 task nodes. Which node purchasing strategy minimizes EMR cluster costs while ensuring the nightly jobs complete reliably without risking HDFS data loss?

options.text: Use Spot Instances for both core and task nodes to achieve maximum cost savings, with instance fleet diversification across multiple instance types to reduce interruption risk.
Use On-Demand Instances for all 150 nodes to guarantee capacity availability throughout the 8-hour processing window and avoid job failures from Spot interruptions.
Use On-Demand Instances for the core nodes to ensure HDFS data durability and use Spot Instances for task nodes which only process data and can tolerate interruptions.
Use Reserved Instances for core nodes with a 1-year commitment and On-Demand Instances for task nodes to balance cost savings on predictable capacity with flexibility.

explanation: Core nodes store HDFS data and should run On-Demand for reliability, while task nodes only process data and can tolerate interruptions, making them ideal for Spot Instances with up to 90% savings. Option A (all Spot) leaves core nodes exposed to Spot interruptions, which would lose HDFS data and fail the nightly jobs; diversification reduces but does not eliminate that risk. Option B (all On-Demand) guarantees capacity but is the most expensive strategy, paying full price for task nodes that could safely run on Spot. Option D (Reserved Instances for core nodes) wastes money because the cluster runs only 8 hours nightly, far too little utilization to justify a 1-year commitment.

stem: A financial services company must detect and alert on any changes to security group rules, Network ACLs, or IAM policies across all AWS accounts. Which service provides continuous monitoring and alerting for these configuration changes?

options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty across all accounts to detect unauthorized network configuration changes and IAM policy modifications using threat intelligence and anomaly detection.
Enable AWS Config with managed rules for security group, NACL, and IAM policy changes across all accounts using an aggregator, with SNS notifications for non-compliant resources.
Enable AWS Security Hub with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard to continuously assess security configurations and alert on deviations from security baselines.
Configure AWS CloudTrail to log all management events and create CloudWatch metric filters that trigger alarms when security group, NACL, or IAM policy API calls are detected.

explanation: AWS Config continuously monitors and records resource configurations. Managed rules evaluate changes to security groups, NACLs, and IAM policies. The aggregator provides cross-account visibility, and SNS delivers alerts. Option A (GuardDuty) detects threats, not configuration changes. Option D (CloudTrail with CloudWatch) can detect API calls but requires custom metric filter creation for each resource type. Option C (Security Hub) aggregates findings but relies on other services for detection.

stem: A company has an application deployed on EC2 instances that stores user-uploaded files on instance store volumes. When instances are terminated during Auto Scaling scale-in events, user files are lost. Which storage solution preserves files across instance lifecycle events MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Configure Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to copy files from instance store volumes to Amazon S3 before the instance terminates, then download files to new instances during launch.
Migrate file storage from instance store volumes to Amazon S3 with the application using the AWS SDK to upload, download, and manage user files in a dedicated S3 bucket.
Migrate file storage from instance store volumes to Amazon EBS volumes attached to each instance, enabling the files to persist independently of the EC2 instance lifecycle.
Migrate file storage from instance store volumes to Amazon EFS which provides shared, persistent file storage accessible from multiple EC2 instances across Availability Zones.

explanation: Amazon S3 provides highly durable object storage that is independent of any EC2 instance and is the lowest-cost option for storing user-uploaded files, preserving them through every scale-in event. Option A (lifecycle hooks copying to S3) adds operational complexity, delays termination, and still risks losing files if the copy fails or the instance dies unexpectedly. Option C (EBS volumes) ties files to a single instance and Availability Zone, and volumes are not automatically reattached when Auto Scaling replaces instances. Option D (EFS) also preserves files across instance lifecycles but costs significantly more per GB than S3 for this object-style workload.

stem: A company runs a PostgreSQL database on Amazon RDS. Application queries include complex reporting queries that take several minutes and impact the performance of transactional OLTP queries. Which solution isolates reporting queries from OLTP workloads?

options.text: Enable RDS Performance Insights to identify slow reporting queries and optimize them with better indexes and query plans to reduce their impact on OLTP workload.
Implement connection pooling using Amazon RDS Proxy to efficiently manage database connections and reduce the resource contention between reporting and OLTP queries.
Create an RDS read replica and direct all reporting queries to the read replica, keeping the primary instance dedicated to transactional OLTP queries without reporting load.
Upgrade the RDS instance to a larger instance type with more CPU and memory to handle both reporting and OLTP queries concurrently without performance degradation.

explanation: Read replicas offload read-heavy reporting queries from the primary instance. The primary handles OLTP writes and reads, while the replica serves reporting queries with its own compute resources. Option D (larger instance) increases capacity but does not isolate workloads; reporting still impacts OLTP. Option A (Performance Insights) helps identify issues but does not isolate workloads. Option B (RDS Proxy) manages connections but does not separate reporting from OLTP processing.

stem: A company runs a development environment with 20 EC2 instances that are used only during business hours (8 AM to 6 PM) on weekdays. The instances are currently running 24/7. Which solution reduces costs without impacting developer productivity?

options.text: Purchase 1-year Reserved Instances for the 20 development EC2 instances with no upfront payment to reduce the hourly cost while maintaining 24/7 availability for developers.
Migrate all development workloads from EC2 instances to AWS Lambda functions to eliminate the need for always-on compute resources and pay only for actual execution time.
Convert the 20 EC2 instances to Spot Instances to reduce hourly costs by up to 90% while keeping them running 24/7 for developer convenience and immediate availability.
Create an AWS Instance Scheduler solution using CloudFormation that starts instances at 8 AM and stops them at 6 PM on weekdays based on resource tags identifying development instances.

explanation: Instance Scheduler automatically stops instances outside business hours, reducing runtime from 168 to 50 hours per week (70% savings). Tags identify which instances to schedule. Option B (Lambda migration) requires significant application refactoring. Option C (Spot Instances) risks interruptions during development work. Option A (Reserved Instances) locks in costs for 24/7 operation when instances are only needed 10 hours per weekday.

stem: A company needs to protect its web application from common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS), and also protect against DDoS attacks. Which TWO services should the solutions architect configure? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Enable Amazon Macie on the S3 buckets used by the web application to detect and protect sensitive data from being exposed through SQL injection or XSS attack vectors.
Configure AWS WAF with managed rule groups for SQL injection and XSS protection on the Application Load Balancer to inspect and filter malicious HTTP requests.
Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the Application Load Balancer to provide enhanced DDoS protection with real-time attack visibility and access to the AWS DDoS Response Team.
Configure Amazon Inspector to scan the web application for SQL injection and XSS vulnerabilities in the application code and automatically patch identified security weaknesses.

explanation: AWS WAF protects against web exploits (SQLi, XSS) by inspecting HTTP requests against rule sets. Shield Advanced provides DDoS protection with 24/7 support from the DDoS Response Team. Option D (Inspector) scans for infrastructure vulnerabilities, not web application exploits. Option A (Macie) discovers sensitive data in S3, not web exploit protection.

stem: A company has an Auto Scaling group with a minimum of 2 instances, desired capacity of 4, and maximum of 8. During a deployment, the company wants to ensure that at least 2 healthy instances are always serving traffic, without provisioning any instances beyond the current desired capacity. Which deployment strategy meets these requirements?

options.text: Use a blue-green deployment by creating a new Auto Scaling group with the updated application, then switching the ALB target group to the new group after validation.
Use an immutable deployment that creates 4 new instances with the updated application in a temporary Auto Scaling group, then replaces the original instances after health checks.
Use a rolling deployment with a minimum healthy percentage of 50% to maintain at least 2 instances serving traffic while updating the remaining instances in batches.
Use an all-at-once deployment that updates all 4 instances simultaneously to minimize deployment time and reduce the window during which mixed versions are serving traffic.

explanation: A rolling deployment with a 50% minimum healthy percentage updates the 4 instances in batches while keeping at least 2 in service, and it works entirely within the existing capacity without launching extra instances. Option A (blue-green with a new ASG) keeps instances serving traffic but requires provisioning a full duplicate fleet, exceeding the current desired capacity. Option B (immutable deployment) likewise launches 4 additional instances in a temporary group, temporarily doubling capacity. Option D (all-at-once) takes all 4 instances out of service simultaneously, violating the 2-healthy-instance requirement.

stem: A company needs to run machine learning inference on images uploaded to S3. The inference takes 100 milliseconds per image and the workload varies from 0 to 10,000 images per minute. The company wants to minimize operational overhead. Which compute solution handles this workload?

options.text: Use Amazon ECS tasks on Fargate triggered by S3 events through EventBridge to run inference containers that scale based on the number of pending S3 upload notifications.
Use AWS Lambda functions triggered by S3 upload events to run inference on each image, leveraging automatic scaling to handle 0 to 10,000 concurrent invocations per minute.
Use EC2 GPU instances in an Auto Scaling group with scaling policies based on SQS queue depth to process inference requests queued from S3 upload event notifications.
Use Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints with auto-scaling configured based on the number of invocations per minute to dynamically adjust endpoint instance count.

explanation: Lambda provides serverless execution triggered by S3 events, scaling automatically from 0 to thousands of concurrent invocations. At 100ms per inference, Lambda is well within its 15-minute timeout and cost-effective for variable workloads. Option D (SageMaker endpoints) requires maintaining provisioned endpoints and has minimum costs even at zero traffic. Option A (ECS Fargate) has slower scaling for burst workloads. Option C (EC2 GPU) requires infrastructure management and does not scale to zero.

stem: A company has 100 TB of data in Amazon S3 Standard that includes a mix of frequently and infrequently accessed objects. The company cannot predict which objects will be accessed frequently. Which S3 storage class automatically optimizes costs based on access patterns?

options.text: Use S3 Analytics Storage Class Analysis to generate recommendations and manually transition objects between storage classes based on the quarterly access pattern report.
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering which automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on access patterns, with no retrieval fees or performance impact.
Use S3 Lifecycle policies to transition all objects to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days based on a fixed time-based schedule.
Use S3 Standard-IA for all objects and accept the retrieval fee on the subset of objects that are accessed frequently, since the storage savings offset the retrieval costs.

explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on usage patterns with no retrieval fees. It is designed for unpredictable access patterns. Option D (Standard-IA) charges retrieval fees which can be costly for frequently accessed objects. Option C (lifecycle policies) uses time-based rules, not access patterns, and may archive actively accessed objects. Option A (S3 Analytics) requires manual action based on reports.

stem: A company needs to establish a private, dedicated network connection between its on-premises data center and AWS that provides consistent network performance. The connection must support 10 Gbps throughput. Which connectivity option meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet with two IPsec tunnels for redundancy, achieving up to 10 Gbps throughput with encrypted connectivity to the VPC.
Use AWS Transit Gateway with multiple VPN connections aggregated together to achieve 10 Gbps aggregate throughput between the on-premises data center and multiple VPCs.
Provision AWS Cloud WAN with a 10 Gbps connection to create a global network that connects the on-premises data center to AWS using a software-defined wide area network.
Provision an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection with 10 Gbps capacity from the company's data center to an AWS Direct Connect location for private, consistent connectivity.

explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated, private network connection with consistent performance. A 10 Gbps dedicated connection meets the throughput requirement without internet variability. Option A (Site-to-Site VPN) traverses the internet with variable performance and typically supports up to 1.25 Gbps per tunnel. Option B (Transit Gateway VPN aggregation) still uses internet-based VPN connections. Option C (Cloud WAN) is a network management service, not a physical connectivity option.

stem: A company needs to ensure that an S3 bucket containing critical business data is protected against accidental deletion. Even if an IAM administrator accidentally deletes objects, the company must be able to recover the data. Which S3 feature provides this protection?

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket to preserve previous versions of objects when they are overwritten or deleted, allowing recovery of any prior version of the data.
Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy all objects to a bucket in another Region, providing a backup copy that survives accidental deletion in the primary bucket.
Enable MFA Delete on the bucket which requires multi-factor authentication for any object deletion request, preventing accidental deletion by requiring a second factor of verification.
Configure S3 Object Lock in governance mode on the bucket to prevent objects from being deleted for a specified retention period, even by users with administrative permissions.

explanation: S3 Versioning preserves all versions of objects, including deleted objects (stored as delete markers). Accidentally deleted objects can be recovered by restoring the previous version. Option B (CRR) replicates deletions to the target bucket, so accidental deletion affects both copies. Option D (Object Lock governance) can be overridden by administrators. Option C (MFA Delete) prevents deletion but does not allow recovery of already-deleted objects.

stem: A company has a web application that serves dynamic content from an API backend and static assets from S3. The application has users in North America, Europe, and Asia. Which architecture provides the best performance for all users MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Deploy Amazon CloudFront with two origins: an S3 bucket for static assets and an ALB for dynamic API content, using cache behaviors to route requests to the appropriate origin.
Deploy the application in three AWS Regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) with Route 53 latency-based routing directing users to the nearest Regional deployment.
Deploy the application in us-east-1 with an ALB and use AWS Global Accelerator to route traffic from all Regions through the AWS global network to the single application deployment.
Deploy the application in us-east-1 with CloudFront caching all content (static and dynamic) at edge locations with a long TTL to minimize requests reaching the origin servers.

explanation: CloudFront with an S3 origin for static assets and an ALB origin for the API caches static content at edge locations worldwide and accelerates dynamic requests over the AWS backbone, delivering strong global performance from a single application deployment. Option B (three-Region deployment) reduces dynamic latency further but roughly triples infrastructure and operational cost, far exceeding the single-deployment CloudFront design. Option C (Global Accelerator only) optimizes network routing but provides no edge caching, so static assets travel the full distance on every request. Option D (long TTL for all content) serves stale API responses because dynamic content changes too frequently to cache with a long TTL.

stem: A company uses Amazon EBS gp2 volumes for its EC2 instances. Several volumes are provisioned at 500 GB to achieve the desired baseline IOPS, even though only 50 GB of storage is actually used. Which EBS volume type eliminates the need to over-provision storage for IOPS?

options.text: Migrate from gp2 to io2 volumes which allow provisioning exact IOPS independently from volume size, providing guaranteed performance at any storage capacity configuration.
Migrate from gp2 to gp3 volumes which decouple IOPS from volume size, allowing the company to provision 50 GB of storage with independently configured IOPS at a lower cost.
Migrate from gp2 to st1 Throughput Optimized HDD volumes which provide high throughput regardless of volume size, suitable for workloads that need sequential read performance.
Keep gp2 volumes but enable EBS Elastic Volumes to dynamically resize the volumes to the actual 50 GB needed without downtime, reducing the over-provisioned storage capacity.

explanation: gp3 decouples IOPS from volume size, unlike gp2 where IOPS scales with volume size (3 IOPS per GB). With gp3, the company can provision 50 GB and independently set the desired IOPS. gp3 is also 20% cheaper per GB than gp2. Option A (io2) provides independent IOPS but costs significantly more than gp3. Option C (st1) is HDD-based with low IOPS. Option D (Elastic Volumes) resizes gp2 but reduces IOPS proportionally with the smaller size.

stem: A company must ensure that all Amazon EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances are encrypted. If an unencrypted EBS volume is detected, the company wants to be automatically notified. Which solution provides continuous compliance monitoring and notification?

options.text: Create a Lambda function that runs daily using a CloudWatch Events scheduled rule, calls the EC2 DescribeVolumes API to check encryption status, and sends alerts via SNS.
Enable AWS Config with the encrypted-volumes managed rule to continuously evaluate EBS volumes and configure an SNS topic to send notifications when non-compliant volumes are detected.
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor to check for unencrypted EBS volumes and configure Trusted Advisor refresh alerts to send email notifications when the check status changes.
Enable Amazon Inspector to continuously scan EC2 instances and their attached EBS volumes for encryption compliance, sending findings to Security Hub for notification.

explanation: AWS Config's encrypted-volumes managed rule continuously evaluates EBS volume encryption compliance. Non-compliant resources trigger SNS notifications automatically. Option A (Lambda daily check) only checks once per day, not continuously. Option D (Inspector) scans for software vulnerabilities, not EBS encryption compliance. Option C (Trusted Advisor) provides periodic checks but lacks continuous monitoring and configurable notifications.

stem: A company runs an application that writes to an Amazon DynamoDB table. The application occasionally experiences throttling during traffic spikes that exceed the provisioned write capacity. The company does not want to over-provision capacity for occasional spikes. Which solution handles traffic spikes without throttling?

options.text: Switch the DynamoDB table from provisioned capacity mode to on-demand capacity mode, which automatically scales to accommodate any traffic level without throttling or capacity planning.
Configure the application to use exponential backoff retry logic when DynamoDB returns throttling errors, automatically retrying the failed write operations with increasing delay.
Implement a write-through cache using DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to buffer write requests during traffic spikes and write to the underlying table at the provisioned capacity rate.
Enable DynamoDB auto scaling on the table with a target utilization of 70%, which automatically adjusts provisioned capacity in response to actual traffic patterns and spikes.

explanation: On-demand capacity mode handles any traffic level without throttling, scaling instantly to accommodate spikes. There is no capacity planning required. Option D (auto scaling) takes several minutes to adjust capacity, during which throttling occurs. Option C (DAX) accelerates reads, not writes. Option B (exponential backoff) mitigates throttling impact but does not prevent it.

stem: A company needs to migrate a 500 TB on-premises data warehouse to Amazon Redshift. The migration must complete within 2 weeks. The company has a 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection. Which migration approach meets the timeline?

options.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) with a replication instance to continuously replicate data from the on-premises data warehouse to Amazon Redshift over Direct Connect.
Use the Redshift UNLOAD command to export data from the on-premises warehouse to local storage, then use AWS Transfer Family SFTP to upload the files to S3 for Redshift loading.
Transfer the data over the 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection to S3 using AWS DataSync, then use the Redshift COPY command to load the data from S3 into Redshift tables.
Use AWS Snowball Edge devices to physically transfer the 500 TB dataset to AWS, then load the data from S3 into Amazon Redshift using the COPY command for bulk data ingestion.

explanation: At 1 Gbps, transferring 500 TB takes approximately 46 days, exceeding the 2-week deadline. Snowball Edge devices can transfer 500 TB within 2 weeks using physical shipping. The data lands in S3, then COPY loads it into Redshift. Option C (Direct Connect transfer) takes 46 days, missing the 2-week deadline. Option A (DMS) requires the same Direct Connect bandwidth bottleneck. Option B (UNLOAD) is a Redshift command that cannot export from on-premises databases.

stem: A company wants to identify opportunities to reduce its overall AWS spending. Which TWO AWS tools provide cost optimization recommendations? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory to collect software and configuration data from EC2 instances and generate cost reports based on the installed software licensing requirements.
Use AWS Compute Optimizer to analyze EC2, Lambda, and EBS usage patterns and receive recommendations for right-sizing compute resources based on actual utilization metrics.
Use Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to visualize EC2 CPU and memory utilization metrics across all instances and manually identify instances that appear underutilized.
Use AWS Cost Explorer's right-sizing recommendations to identify EC2 instances that are underutilized and receive specific instance type downsizing suggestions based on CloudWatch data.

explanation: Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze usage patterns and recommends optimal instance types for EC2, Lambda, and EBS. Cost Explorer right-sizing recommendations identify underutilized EC2 instances with specific downsizing suggestions. Option C (CloudWatch dashboards) shows metrics but does not provide automated recommendations. Option A (SSM Inventory) collects inventory data, not cost optimization recommendations.

stem: A company is deploying a Lambda function that needs to access a relational database in a private subnet. The Lambda function must not have any internet access. Which networking configuration enables database connectivity while preventing internet access?

options.text: Deploy the Lambda function in the same VPC and private subnet as the database, with security groups allowing traffic between the Lambda function and the database on the database port.
Deploy the Lambda function outside the VPC and configure the database security group to allow inbound connections from the Lambda function's public IP addresses assigned by the service.
Deploy the Lambda function outside the VPC and configure a VPC peering connection between the Lambda service VPC and the database VPC to enable private database connectivity.
Deploy the Lambda function in the VPC with a public subnet that has an internet gateway, and configure the security group to deny all outbound internet traffic except database connections.

explanation: Deploying Lambda in the same VPC and private subnet provides direct network access to the database through the VPC network. Without a NAT gateway or internet gateway route, the function has no internet access. Option C (VPC peering from Lambda VPC) is not how Lambda VPC networking works. Option D (public subnet) provides internet access via the IGW. Option B (Lambda outside VPC) cannot reach resources in private subnets.

stem: A company has an application that uses Amazon Aurora MySQL as its primary database. The company needs a disaster recovery solution that can recover the database in a different AWS Region with an RPO of less than 1 minute. Which Aurora feature meets this requirement?

options.text: Configure Aurora automated backups with cross-Region backup replication enabled, copying automated backups to the secondary Region within the configured backup retention window.
Configure Aurora Global Database which replicates data from the primary Region to a secondary Region with typical replication lag of less than 1 second, meeting the sub-1-minute RPO.
Create an Aurora cross-Region read replica that replicates data asynchronously from the primary cluster, with typical replication lag of several minutes during normal operations.
Configure Aurora Serverless v2 in both Regions with DynamoDB global tables as the replication mechanism, synchronizing data between the two Aurora instances through DynamoDB streams.

explanation: Aurora Global Database uses dedicated replication infrastructure that achieves sub-second replication lag (typically under 1 second), providing an RPO well under 1 minute. Option A (cross-Region backups) has RPO equal to the time since the last backup, typically hours. Option C (cross-Region read replica) has higher replication lag than Global Database. Option D (DynamoDB replication for Aurora) is an invalid architecture; DynamoDB cannot replicate Aurora data.

stem: A company has a DynamoDB table that serves a high-traffic API. Read operations are 100x more frequent than writes, and the same items are read repeatedly. Read latency must be under 1 millisecond. Which solution optimizes read performance?

options.text: Create a DynamoDB global secondary index (GSI) on the most queried attributes to distribute read traffic across the base table and the index for improved read performance.
Deploy DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as an in-memory caching layer in front of the DynamoDB table, providing microsecond response times for frequently accessed items from the cache.
Enable DynamoDB strongly consistent reads for all read operations to ensure the most up-to-date data is returned, with single-digit millisecond latency guaranteed by DynamoDB.
Increase the DynamoDB table read capacity units (RCUs) to handle the high read throughput and enable auto scaling to adjust capacity based on actual read traffic patterns.

explanation: DAX provides microsecond read latency by caching frequently accessed items in memory, well under the 1-millisecond requirement. It is fully compatible with DynamoDB API calls. Option C (strongly consistent reads) provides single-digit millisecond latency, not sub-millisecond. Option D (more RCUs) increases throughput but does not reduce latency below DynamoDB's single-digit millisecond baseline. Option A (GSI) provides an alternative query pattern, not faster read latency.

stem: A company has multiple AWS accounts and wants to consolidate billing to receive volume pricing discounts. The company also wants a single payment method for all accounts. Which AWS feature provides consolidated billing?

options.text: Create IAM cross-account roles that allow the billing team in one account to access billing information in all other accounts and generate consolidated billing reports.
Enable AWS Budgets in each account with the same billing alert configuration and use SNS to send all billing notifications to a centralized monitoring account for aggregation.
Create an AWS Organization with all accounts and enable consolidated billing under the management account, which aggregates usage across accounts for volume pricing discounts.
Configure AWS Cost Explorer in each account to share billing data with the management account and create a consolidated billing dashboard for centralized cost tracking.

explanation: AWS Organizations provides consolidated billing which aggregates usage from all member accounts under the management account. This qualifies for volume pricing discounts and provides a single invoice. Option D (Cost Explorer) provides cost analysis but not consolidated billing or volume discounts. Option A (cross-account roles) provides access to billing data but not consolidated billing. Option B (AWS Budgets) monitors spending but does not consolidate billing.

stem: A company needs to centrally manage SSH key pairs for EC2 instances across multiple accounts without distributing private keys to users. Users should authenticate using their existing corporate Active Directory credentials. Which solution provides centralized, credential-based EC2 access?

options.text: Store SSH private keys in AWS Secrets Manager and grant IAM users access to retrieve the keys, with Secrets Manager audit logging tracking all key retrieval operations.
Deploy a bastion host with Active Directory authentication that users connect to first, then SSH to target instances using shared key pairs stored securely on the bastion host.
Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to provide browser-based and CLI access to EC2 instances without SSH keys, with IAM policies controlling access based on AD federation.
Configure EC2 Instance Connect to push temporary SSH keys to instances on demand, with IAM policies controlling which users can connect to which instances using their AD credentials.

explanation: Session Manager provides secure instance access without SSH keys, ports, or bastion hosts. It integrates with IAM, which can federate with Active Directory, providing centralized access control using existing corporate credentials. Option A (Secrets Manager) still requires distributing private keys to users. Option D (EC2 Instance Connect) provides temporary keys but still uses SSH and requires port 22 open. Option B (bastion host) requires managing SSH keys and maintaining the bastion infrastructure.

stem: A company runs a serverless application using API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB. The company wants to deploy application updates without risk. If a new version causes errors, traffic must automatically roll back to the previous version. Which deployment strategy provides this capability?

options.text: Use Lambda aliases with weighted traffic shifting and configure CloudWatch alarms on error metrics to automatically roll back to the previous version if the error rate exceeds a threshold.
Use Lambda versioning to publish each deployment as a numbered version and manually update the API Gateway integration to point to the new version number after testing.
Deploy the new Lambda version as a separate function with a different API Gateway stage, monitor errors manually, and switch the production stage back if errors are detected.
Deploy the new Lambda code using SAM with the AutoPublishAlias property but without configuring deployment preferences, allowing instant full traffic cutover to the new version.

explanation: Lambda aliases with traffic shifting gradually route traffic to the new version. CloudWatch alarms on error rates trigger automatic rollback to the previous version if errors increase. This is integrated with CodeDeploy. Option C (separate function and stage) requires manual monitoring and switching. Option B (manual version update) has no automatic rollback capability. Option D (instant cutover without deployment preferences) does not enable gradual shifting or automatic rollback.

stem: A company runs a high-performance computing (HPC) workload that requires low-latency, high-throughput communication between EC2 instances. The instances need to communicate with each other at up to 100 Gbps. Which networking feature provides this capability?

options.text: Enable Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) on the EC2 instances and deploy them in a cluster placement group to provide low-latency, high-throughput inter-instance networking at up to 100 Gbps.
Deploy the EC2 instances in a spread placement group across multiple Availability Zones and enable jumbo frames (9001 MTU) on the instance network interfaces for larger packets.
Attach multiple Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) to each EC2 instance and configure network bonding to aggregate bandwidth across all ENIs for higher total throughput.
Enable enhanced networking with Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) on the EC2 instances to provide up to 100 Gbps network bandwidth with lower latency than standard networking.

explanation: EFA provides OS-bypass networking for HPC workloads, enabling low-latency communication at up to 100 Gbps. Cluster placement groups co-locate instances on the same rack for minimal network latency. Option D (ENA enhanced networking) improves performance but does not provide the OS-bypass capability needed for HPC. Option B (spread placement group) separates instances across hardware, increasing latency. Option C (multiple ENIs) does not increase per-flow throughput to 100 Gbps.

stem: A company runs a containerized application on Amazon ECS with EC2 launch type. The containers use only 30% of the EC2 instance CPU and memory capacity. The company wants to improve resource utilization and reduce costs. Which change improves efficiency?

options.text: Migrate from ECS with EC2 launch type to ECS with Fargate launch type, which allocates exact CPU and memory per task without provisioning or managing underlying EC2 instances.
Enable ECS cluster auto scaling with capacity providers to automatically adjust the number of EC2 instances in the cluster based on the actual resource requirements of running tasks.
Switch from ECS to Amazon EKS with managed node groups that use Karpenter for bin-packing and automatic right-sizing of EC2 instances based on pod resource requests.
Increase the number of ECS tasks per instance by reducing the CPU and memory reservations in the task definition, allowing more containers to share the available instance resources.

explanation: Fargate eliminates EC2 instance management and charges only for the exact CPU and memory allocated per task. This eliminates the 70% unused capacity on EC2 instances. Option B (cluster auto scaling) adjusts instance count but each instance may still be underutilized. Option C (EKS with Karpenter) adds complexity for a similar outcome. Option D (reducing reservations) may cause resource contention and instability if tasks need more resources than reserved.

stem: A company has an S3 bucket that should only be accessible from within a specific VPC. No other network path should be able to access the bucket, including other VPCs and the internet. Which configuration enforces this restriction?

options.text: Disable the S3 bucket's public access using the S3 Block Public Access settings and configure the bucket policy to allow access only from IAM roles in the VPC's AWS account.
Configure an S3 bucket policy with a condition that denies all requests unless the aws:sourceVpce condition key matches the VPC endpoint ID of the specific VPC's S3 gateway endpoint.
Configure the S3 bucket to use a VPC interface endpoint and restrict the endpoint policy to allow only requests from the specific VPC's CIDR range for all S3 API operations.
Configure the S3 bucket with server-side encryption using a KMS key that only IAM principals within the VPC's account can use, preventing access from other VPCs and the internet.

explanation: An S3 bucket policy with aws:sourceVpce condition restricts access exclusively to requests coming through the specified VPC endpoint. All other access paths are denied, including internet and other VPCs. Option C (interface endpoint with CIDR restriction) does not prevent access through other paths. Option A (Block Public Access) prevents public access but not access from other VPCs. Option D (KMS encryption) controls decryption access, not network-level bucket access.

stem: A company runs a critical application across 3 Availability Zones that must maintain at least 6 running EC2 instances at all times, even during an Availability Zone outage, without waiting for replacement instances to launch. How should the Auto Scaling group be configured?

options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group with a minimum and desired capacity of 6 and maximum of 9, spanning 3 AZs, allowing Auto Scaling to launch additional instances when an AZ fails.
Configure the Auto Scaling group with a minimum, desired, and maximum capacity of 6 instances distributed across 3 AZs (2 per AZ), relying on Auto Scaling to rebalance during AZ failure.
Configure the Auto Scaling group with a minimum, desired, and maximum capacity of 9 instances (3 per AZ) so that losing one AZ still leaves 6 running instances in the remaining two AZs.
Configure three separate Auto Scaling groups, one per AZ, each with a minimum and desired capacity of 2 instances, providing 6 total instances distributed across the three AZs.

explanation: Provisioning 9 instances across 3 AZs (3 per AZ) means losing any single AZ immediately leaves 6 running instances in the remaining two AZs, with no wait for replacements to launch. Option A (min 6, max 9) relies on Auto Scaling to launch replacements after the AZ fails, leaving fewer than 6 running instances during the launch window. Option B (single ASG capped at 6) drops to 4 instances when an AZ fails and only recovers to 6 after replacement instances launch in the surviving AZs. Option D (three per-AZ ASGs of 2) also drops to 4 instances on an AZ failure, and the per-AZ groups cannot launch capacity in the surviving AZs.

stem: A company needs a managed Apache Kafka service for real-time event streaming between microservices. The company wants to minimize operational overhead while maintaining Kafka API compatibility. Which AWS service should be used?

options.text: Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) which provides a fully managed Kafka service with automatic broker patching, monitoring, and native Kafka API compatibility.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams which provides a managed streaming service with similar functionality to Kafka, including partitioned data streams and configurable retention periods.
Use Amazon EventBridge which provides a serverless event bus that routes events between microservices with built-in filtering rules and schema registry for event validation.
Use Amazon MQ for Apache ActiveMQ which provides a managed message broker with support for multiple messaging protocols including AMQP, MQTT, and OpenWire for microservice communication.

explanation: Amazon MSK provides a fully managed Apache Kafka service with full Kafka API compatibility, automatic infrastructure management, and built-in monitoring. Option B (Kinesis) is a streaming service but uses a different API, not Kafka-compatible. Option C (EventBridge) is an event bus, not a streaming platform with Kafka compatibility. Option D (Amazon MQ) supports traditional messaging protocols, not the Kafka protocol.

stem: A company stores sensitive customer data in Amazon DynamoDB. Regulatory requirements mandate that the data must be encrypted using a key that the company can audit and rotate on a custom schedule. Which encryption configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure DynamoDB encryption at rest using a customer managed key (CMK) in AWS KMS, which allows the company to audit key usage via CloudTrail and set a custom rotation schedule.
Configure DynamoDB encryption at rest using the AWS managed key aws/dynamodb in KMS, which provides automatic annual rotation and CloudTrail logging of key usage events.
Configure DynamoDB encryption at rest using the AWS owned key, which provides transparent encryption managed by DynamoDB with automatic key rotation handled by the service.
Implement client-side encryption in the application layer using the AWS Encryption SDK before writing data to DynamoDB, managing encryption keys in an on-premises HSM cluster.

explanation: Customer managed KMS keys provide full control over key policies, custom rotation schedules, and detailed CloudTrail audit logs of all key usage. Option C (AWS owned key) provides no customer visibility or control over the key. Option B (AWS managed key) rotates annually and cannot be customized. Option D (client-side encryption with on-premises HSM) adds complexity and does not use AWS-native key management.

stem: A company runs an application that processes financial transactions. Transactions must be processed in order without loss, and the system must handle up to 100,000 transactions per second. If the processing service is temporarily unavailable, transactions must be retained for later processing. Which architecture ensures reliable transaction processing?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge to route transactions to Step Functions workflows that orchestrate the processing logic with built-in retry and error handling for each transaction step.
Use Amazon SQS Standard queue with a Lambda function consumer to process transactions, with dead-letter queues capturing failed messages after the maximum receive count is exceeded.
Use Amazon SNS to fan out transactions to multiple SQS queues, with each queue processed by a dedicated Lambda function to achieve high throughput through parallel processing.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enhanced fan-out consumers and checkpointing to process transactions in order, with 7-day retention allowing replay after consumer downtime.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams scales to 100,000+ records per second, preserves ordering within each shard, and its 7-day retention lets consumers resume from the last checkpoint and replay records after downtime, so no transactions are lost. Option A (EventBridge to Step Functions) cannot sustain 100,000 TPS; both services throttle far below that rate for per-transaction workflows. Option B (SQS Standard queue) provides only best-effort ordering, so transactions can be processed out of sequence. Option C (SNS fan-out to multiple queues) also provides no ordering guarantee across the parallel queues and adds complexity without solving sequencing.

stem: A company uses Amazon CloudFront to distribute content globally. The company notices that 60% of CloudFront costs come from data transfer out to viewers. Which strategy reduces CloudFront data transfer costs without degrading performance for users in any geography?

options.text: Increase the CloudFront cache TTL to 7 days for all content to maximize the cache hit ratio and reduce the number of origin fetches that incur data transfer charges.
Switch to CloudFront Price Class 100 which limits distribution to the least expensive edge locations in North America and Europe, reducing per-GB data transfer pricing.
Configure CloudFront to use Origin Shield as a centralized caching layer that reduces origin requests and consolidates data transfer through a single optimal edge location.
Enable CloudFront compression for text-based content types (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON) to reduce the size of transferred files and lower the data transfer charges.

explanation: Enabling compression shrinks text-based payloads by 60-80%, directly cutting the data-transfer-out charges that dominate the bill while every user continues to be served from their nearest edge location. Option A (7-day TTL) reduces origin fetches, but origin transfer is not the viewer-facing cost that makes up 60% of the bill. Option B (Price Class 100) lowers per-GB pricing but removes edge locations in Asia, South America, and other regions, degrading performance for users in those geographies. Option C (Origin Shield) reduces origin-facing requests and transfer, not the data transfer out to viewers, and adds its own request charges.

stem: A company is implementing a defense-in-depth security strategy for its VPC. Which TWO network security controls should be implemented at different layers? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Configure AWS Network Firewall with intrusion detection system rules to inspect all traffic entering and leaving the VPC through the internet gateway for threat detection.
Configure VPC Flow Logs to capture and analyze network traffic metadata for all ENIs in the VPC, storing the logs in CloudWatch Logs for security monitoring and analysis.
Configure Network ACLs on subnets with both allow and deny rules to provide stateless packet filtering at the subnet boundary for an additional layer of network security.
Configure security groups on EC2 instances to allow only required inbound traffic on specific ports and from specific source IP ranges for application-level network access control.

explanation: Security groups provide stateful instance-level filtering, while Network ACLs provide stateless subnet-level filtering. Together they implement defense-in-depth at two different network layers. Option B (VPC Flow Logs) provides monitoring and visibility but does not filter or block traffic. Option A (Network Firewall) provides advanced inspection but is a single layer, not two distinct layers.

stem: A company has an application that stores session data in local memory on EC2 instances. When an instance fails, users lose their session and must re-authenticate. Which architectural change enables session persistence across instance failures?

options.text: Enable sticky sessions on the ALB with a 24-hour duration cookie to ensure users always connect to the same instance where their session data is stored in local memory.
Configure the Application Load Balancer with connection draining set to 300 seconds to allow existing sessions to complete before removing failed instances from the target group.
Externalize session storage to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with Multi-AZ enabled, allowing any instance to retrieve session data from the shared, highly available Redis cluster.
Configure Auto Scaling to use lifecycle hooks that copy session data from the failing instance's memory to Amazon S3 before the instance is terminated and removed from service.

explanation: ElastiCache for Redis provides a shared, external session store accessible from any instance. Multi-AZ ensures the session store survives AZ failures. If an instance fails, other instances can retrieve the user's session from Redis. Option B (connection draining) allows in-flight requests to complete but does not preserve sessions for new requests. Option A (sticky sessions) still loses session data when the pinned instance fails. Option D (lifecycle hooks) cannot reliably capture in-memory data from a failing instance.

stem: A company has a mobile application that needs to sync user data across devices in real time. Users should be able to access their data offline and have changes automatically synchronized when connectivity is restored. Which AWS service provides these capabilities?

options.text: Use Amazon SNS mobile push notifications to notify devices of data changes, with the application fetching updated data from a DynamoDB table via API Gateway when notified.
Use Amazon Cognito Sync to synchronize user profile data and application state across mobile devices, with automatic conflict resolution and offline support built into the SDK.
Use Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API with a Lambda backend that pushes data changes to connected devices and stores pending changes in DynamoDB for offline synchronization.
Use AWS AppSync with a DynamoDB data source and enable conflict detection and resolution, providing real-time synchronization and offline data access with automatic sync on reconnection.

explanation: AWS AppSync provides a managed GraphQL API with built-in real-time subscriptions, offline data access, and conflict resolution. When a device reconnects, changes sync automatically. DynamoDB provides the scalable backend. Option C (API Gateway WebSocket) requires custom offline sync implementation. Option B (Cognito Sync) is deprecated in favor of AppSync. Option A (SNS push) notifies of changes but does not provide offline access or automatic synchronization.

stem: A company has a multi-tier application with a web tier, application tier, and database tier. The company wants to reduce NAT Gateway data processing charges. Analysis shows that 80% of NAT Gateway traffic is API calls to AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, SQS). Which solution reduces NAT Gateway costs?

options.text: Create VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB, and VPC interface endpoints for SQS, routing AWS service traffic through endpoints instead of the NAT Gateway to eliminate charges.
Replace the NAT Gateway with a NAT instance on a t3.micro EC2 instance to reduce the per-GB data processing charge while maintaining internet access for the private subnets.
Migrate the application from private subnets to public subnets with Elastic IP addresses on each instance, eliminating the need for a NAT Gateway entirely for all traffic.
Enable VPC flow logs to analyze traffic patterns and implement caching for AWS API responses to reduce the number of API calls that traverse the NAT Gateway.

explanation: VPC endpoints route AWS service traffic privately without using the NAT Gateway. Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free. Interface endpoints for SQS charge per hour but eliminate NAT Gateway per-GB processing fees for 80% of traffic. Option B (NAT instance) has lower per-GB costs but introduces management overhead and single points of failure. Option C (public subnets) removes private subnet security. Option D (caching) reduces API calls but does not eliminate NAT Gateway traffic.
